i had c diff (and got it again due to recurrence as of this moment). it was a 7 hour wait at this place when they got me a private ed room. the staff were all kind. only concern i have is that i suspected i had c diff a few weeks ago due to explosive diarrhea and abdominal cramping. they wanted to do a urine test and not a stool sample on me at first. eventually after me pushing the envelope, they accepted a stool sample (it was c diff positive). their ct imaging people are obviously a separate entity and my bcbs insurance denied the ct scan and the radiologist charged me over $500 for that scan (pitts radiology). they sent me home with a prescription for flagyl and other meds. let me make it clear: every healthcare institution should always be following the latest evidence based practice guidelines to ensure optimal recovery and a reduced risk if recurrence. this is something this hospital failed to do. flagyl killed it off and then a week later without the antibiotic (i had finished 14 days of it at this point), the c diff returned. surprise! i graduated nursing school and even i know better about keeping up to date on ebp guidelines. if it's the hospital policy to treat c diff with flagyl, someone needs to either get fired or do extensive ebp research. honey, nobody is using flagyl anymore. 

i ended up having to go to an urgent care center and explaining the situation and this time i am on vancomycin.  even the doctor at the urgent care clinic stated that flagyl is no longer the #1 drug for c diff treatment. this costed me a lot of money between er and the urgent care. 

beware that this er may not be up to date on their evidence based practices and may treat you with outdated and ineffective methods. consider yourself warned.

full story: i had an intense case of food poison and several violent episodes of vomit early on the evening of january 5th of 2020. around 8pm, i had no strength to continue throwing up and my partner brought me to the er at this hospital. 
after getting there and on the way to get my vitals (before being admitted to the er itself) my episodes of vomit were so violent and continuous that they had trouble even to have me seated straight to measure my blood pressure. at this moment, i basically dragged myself to the outside bathroom of the er so i could literally be on the ground with my face on the toilet, and avoid passing out.

when they got me in my slot in the er, we noticed that the place was not properly sanitary, let's say. the floors were not clean and the general appearance of the er was far from ideal. moreover, they were improvising new beds in the er by basically putting people in the halls of the facility.

i came back to the er here recently in what was one of the worst decisions i could have made. i should have known better after my last visit.

what i experienced in icu here still gives me nightmares.

i waited over 8 hours after being triaged, with obvious symptoms of advanced pneumonia, including coughing up blood, shortness of breath and rapid breathing, severe and extreme confusion--all without anyone paying attention.

eventually, i started losing consciousness and apparently had gone into sepsis after waiting to be treated for so long.

the only reason i probably survived was that a hospital administrator (i believe her first name was sandra) happened to be nearby and intervened. she was horrified upon finding out how long i'd been waiting, and paged her medical director to see me. he showed up, then walked out when i had to go to the bathroom while talking to him. i forgot his name, but she fired him that same night after he refused to come back, and replaced him with dr. mathew.

upon my admission, a team separate from icu was assembled and confirmed a primary diagnosis of acute multi-focal pneumonia. despite this, a full course of antibiotics wasn't started until long after i'd been transferred out of icu. i was stabilized and given oxygen--for nearly 4 days--while still coughing up blood! dr. mathew was now supervising both critical care and icu, so there was no one watching over things most of the time.

now, i know how unbelievable it may sound, but my treatment was abruptly cut off and i was suddenly transferred to out of icu as a result of my bed in icu literally being sold to someone else.

this patient somehow walked into icu with his family and a lawyer, threatening to sue for previously poor treatment; they also offered an alternative: a huge sum of money just to get proper treatment. i overheard the panicked conversation, since my room was closest to the icu entrance, and all rooms there are kept open.

i was rushed out of icu under these truly bizarre circumstances.

this late-night, hushed maneuver must have resulted from a decision being approved at some high level by hospital administration. whether the motivation was money or fear of legal repercussions, putting patient care last is not only antithetical to the hippocratic oath, it's downright shameful, and the move was very likely illegal under state regulations.

i was so shocked by what i'd heard i initially said nothing when the nurse manager walked in and started to clear my room for that patient. she was clearly ashamed while disconnecting my iv line and oxygen (with my spo2 still dipping under 40%), then covering me up with a full bed-sheet.

i finally said, "i guess my my room is being given to someone else." she responded, "i guess you know everything." i was then told "you always have friends here," before being quickly wheeled out.

as deathly scary as that was, things only got worse.

once out of icu and out of sight of the new patient, i was handed only a small plastic bag of oxygen to breathe from. arriving in a medicine wing, the nurses alarmingly asked why there was no equipment to provide proper flow of oxygen.

as i found out eventually, i was transferred to a wing for palliative care; someone in icu must have been aware of this, since a portable oxygen machine was left anonymously in a plastic bag outside my room.

the wing i was transferred to was essentially a death ward. my vitals were checked only a handful of times in several days. the nurses' only job seemed waking me every hour, on the hour, to make sure i wasn't dead--there was no monitoring! i managed to negotiate a transfer to the main floor, 9, where actual medicine was practiced.

days later, when the cdc came back with results on the culture icu sent them, confirming a particularly bad strain of pneumonia, a full course of augmentin--a common antibiotic--was finally started.

to summarize, i nearly died in the er for lack of proper attention and treatment; was stabilized then received practically no treatment other than oxygen in icu for several days; had my bed there sold to someone else; was transferred to a palliative care wing--a death ward--before negotiating my way out; then was kept on medical hold, with my life upside down in the outside world, for 11 days--when i could have finished treatment at home.

the staff may mean well, but there's something very wrong with this place. the higher-ups seem either completely out of touch, or at least entirely disinterested in patient care, outcomes, any level of comfort, or balancing the needs of patients with real-world obligations.

it seems there is one thing they are interested in--money.

i'd say this establishment lies somewhere between a third-world clinic and a mortuary. there were some redeeming qualities--after all, i walked out alive. sarcasm aside, i hope this review comes across as factual, because it is.

judge for yourself, but take heed, and for goodness' sake, pick another hospital.

my due date was close to christmas, so you can imagine my surprise when my water broke at home on november 19th. we weren't really sure if it was the real thing, so we called the maternity floor at st. luke's. they are always available 24/7 for questions, which was so helpful leading up to my daughter's birth, especially in this case. the nurse i spoke with told me i needed to just come in so they could figure out what was going on, so after a lot of scrambling and throwing random items into a bag, we were on our way.

if you are in labor after normal hours, you enter through the er and they take you up to maternity. i got checked in, and after only ten minutes, the nurses confirmed that my water did break. surprise! from there, there were a few hours of relaxation and then an insane amount of chaos. my labor progressed so fast that my doctor couldn't even take the elevator; she had to run up the stairs. a few minutes later, my precious girl arrived. thankfully, i had my epidural about twenty minutes before that happened. i was so happy that my nurse encouraged me not to wait; her exact words were "it's not the time to be a hero." had she not encouraged me to get it when i did, i would have missed my window.

i cannot speak enough about the nurses at st. luke's. they calmed my nerves. they always made sure i had what i needed. they knew when i needed a joke, and when i needed to be left alone. they anticipated my needs and hard moments. they genuinely cared about my family, and took such wonderful care of my girl. what i appreciated the most was that they took her to the nursery to make sure i could sleep... i've heard nightmare stories of nurses wanting newborns to "co-sleep" in their mom's hospital room, and honestly the rest that they gave me made the first few nights at home bearable. 

the house pediatricians on staff were also incredible, and stopped by each morning to update us on our baby's health and answer all of our questions. the lactation specialist, pam, deserves her own five stars. having pam there was like having the world's most loving and supportive grandma in the room. she had my daughter breastfeeding in no time, and was so encouraging and loving. we wanted to bring her home with us!

i was sad to leave the hospital, and i feel like most people can't wait to get home. we are forever grateful for our experience at st. luke's, and they should never be overlooked when considering a place to have your baby!

we recently brought an immediate family member here for treatment of an acute reaction to a chemotherapy drug.  she spent 3 nights in critical care (icu), followed by 3 nights in the oncology unit.  the quality of care and attention she received was exceptional.  the nurses and physicians who managed her care were highly skilled and compassionate.  this facility is up-to-date and immaculately clean.

but since my forte is restaurant reviews, naturally i'm going to comment on the hospital's food service.  upgraded since our previous visit years ago, it's ably managed by sodexo, the france-headquartered institutional food service goliath (indeed, the french do know a thing or two about food prep).  inpatients receive a menu which includes rotating daily specials.  it's like room service at a fine hotel; you pick up the phone and order.  i'm told visitors can also order food.  food arrives within 30 minutes.  michelin stars my foot, but everything looked and smelled quite appetizing.

the oasis cafeteria on the first floor of the main building is open to hospital staff and visitors.  the missus and i dined here on two consecutive evenings.  their well-stocked salad bar is superior to those at many restaurants and groceries.  a special callout to the incredibly good 5-bean soup.  entrée choices were limited to just one or two main dishes, but the grill offers a variety of freshly-prepared hot sandwiches and there is also pizza.  i had a rather good grilled chicken sandwich one night and a decent quesadilla the next.  prices are very reasonable.

my pet peeve (with so many hospital cafeterias) is their short hours.  they close ridiculously early.  we are late eaters, and the chow line here gets locked down precisely at 6:30.  arrive at 6:31 and you're out of luck.  the only other meal option, a single vending machine dubbed "farmer's fridge," was completely empty during our visit.  thank goodness, a portillo's is located close by.

i wrote a google review but it seems they deleted them.

i can only speak for my stays in 2016 and 2018.

to;dr: find a better program, you deserve better. if you don't want to be trapped with angry explosive people and uncaring staff, find another facility or program. also you have to sleep on uncomfortable beds with the doors open so you can see the hallway lights and hear the night staff as they check your room every hour. but, to be fair, they give you eye covers and ear plugs. they don't seem to care about the effects of sleep on mental health.

my experience:

i was admitted as a voluntary patient seeking help for suicidal ideation. i was placed with other voluntary patients as well as involuntary patients. 

involuntary patients tend to be people who are court ordered to be there. the problem with this is that they can't really get kicked out unless they really cause problems. however, it means that they are incredibly angry and are not focused on recovery, while half the other patients are.

so you have patients struggling with anything from anxiety, depression, addiction, suicidal ideation, mixed together with people who have angry outbursts and staff that don't know how to manage them. 

my first stay there was a guy who kept trying to start fights with people. the staff then tried to put him in a room with the person he kept fighting with. everyone suspected it was because the staff didn't like either of them or because one of the nurses thought it would be funny to mess with them. it was immediately fixed but it just goes to show that they are either incompetent or are willing to mess with people seeking help with their mental health issues.

the second time i stayed i needed treatment and didn't have many other options so i stayed again, thinking that things would be better. they were significantly worse. there was a woman there that screamed at staff and humiliated other patients. she constantly insulted other patients, complained very loudly about all the ways she was abused, got in people's faces, yelled at the staff, and that was my whole stay for a week. the staff couldn't do anything about it so she got to sit in on groups and say whatever she wanted to other patients while they opened up about their struggles. because of issues i'd had in my past being around her was incredibly triggering, and i threw up during my whole stay. i kept wanting to leave but the case manager laughed and said i needed to work on healing.

you're minimum stay as a voluntary patient is a week, don't bother trying to get out sooner. you're labeled as a danger to yourself or others and they want you to stay that whole time, at least, just so they can "monitor" you and "help" you with your mental health. also, doctors are the ones who decide how long you stay and they're not there on weekends and holidays. you have to be cleared by dr and case worker. 

half the staff are genuine, the other half feel the need to put you in your place. if you're going because you are in a bad place, this place will do 2 things, make sure you're "safe" and make you beg to go home. i met people there that would have rather gone back to their abusive households.

there aren't a lot of good er options in queens, but this one is my choice for the future.

urgent care sent me here because my ekg results, along with my shortness of breath & chest tightness/pain, could have meant a blood clot.  it's a good thing i didn't have one, since i had to wait 5 hours to get the blood test.  took another hour for the results.  i understand that it's an er & things get busy, but come on- if it's suspected you might have a life-threatening issue, you really can't be waiting this long. 

not only will this hospital scam you after making you wait forever, but the care is just bad.  they did the x-ray & ekg shortly after i got there, but had me sit in the waiting room for about 4 hours after that.  then, they brought me back & had me sit in a chair in the hallway- didn't even get a room.  the nurse said he "needed to go check something with security" but he would "be right back".  i ended up sitting there for half an hour.  doc finally came & said they were going to do a d-dimer test.  i asked where i could get some water because i was insanely dehydrated, & he said he would bring me some.  then he was called away for an emergency.  so, from my chair, i asked the lady at the front desk the same question.  she said only the doctor can give me water because it might interfere with any tests they perform.  i explained that i was just doing a d-dimer & that the doc said he would bring me some but had to leave.  she seemed not to believe me and simply ignored me (this lady was also incredibly rude & unhelpful regarding my paperwork).  i was so dehydrated & felt awful.  i somehow fell asleep for a while until they finally came to do the test a while later. 

in short, this place just wants your money & doesn't care about its patients at all.  go to another er unless you have 5-6 hours to wait for rude & uncaring staff.

kids have in-toeing so we come here for xrays and observe growth development on their legs.  to be honest, i really wasn't looking forward to this visit because last year, it was such a huge confusing process, especially since it was new patient visit.  check in process has improved but not sure if it's because we are returning patient visit. 

you go to the front desk, check in at a computer and take a pager with you.  then they page you to a desk and do all the paper work there. after that, you sit down and wait to be called in to exam.  they check vitals and then you proceed to exam room.  then you go from exam to xrays, then back to exam room for consult. 

we did not have to wait long after checking in or waiting in exam room to be seen, or wait long for x-rays, everything was pretty quick today so i was very happy about that.  

shriners i believe requires a referral to be seen.  parents need to be on top of scheduling shriners appointments and not procrastinate with scheduling these visits, you schedule these appointments well out in advance. it is important for families to ensure they come here on time because there are families who travel a lot further away to be seen.

depending the date of the visit, if there's a holiday, like valentines, shriners had a ton of toys and goodie bags to give to children from generous donors. i wasn't expecting this since we are outpatient visit.  my kids were very happy with the goodies they got. last time we were there, there were tons of free snacks at the lobby.  it is a very kid friendly environment and the staff truly seem to enjoy working with children. they expect good commitment from volunteers too.  

i remember visiting shriners years ago as a kid with my parents to make a visit to another family whose daughter flew in from argentina to get orthopedic surgery at shriners slc. this family didn't really know anyone in utah so through some networking, my parents (also from arg) found out and we went to go visit them. we discovered they didn't have to pay for her surgery and stay. children are taken care of here. definitely consider making a donation to shriners.

"good" sam, here i come.

the reasons why i have rated riverside as a three star is for two reasons. 

1. when having my gallbladder surgery, i had to have surgery twice. everyone knows that undergoing anesthesia is not safe nor cheap, but i had do it twice. the first time was to remove my gallbladder and gallstones. when i awoke, i was advised that some gallstones had been missed and that i would have to undergo surgery again the next day to remove the remaining stones. let's not go into detail about that nor discuss my anesthesiology bill. 

2. the billing department for the hospital has some of the rudest and most non-empathetic individuals i have ever encountered! they would not work with me in regards to my $12,000 bill i had accrued in less than six weeks. i had a $4,000 deductible through my insurance so they charged me $4,000 for me when giving birth (in december), $4,000 for my daughter when she was born, and then $4,000 for my gallbladder surgery (in january). the only payment plan they offered to work with me on was a 12 month - $1,000 month plan. this also did not include the numerous separate bills that i received from anesthesiology and some other medical offices. they immediately sent me to collections after three months since i could not afford their $1,000 per month payment plan - especially with being on maternity leave for eight weeks. 

now that i am on a better insurance plan (far less deductible), i may consider using riverside again if for some reason any medical emergency arise. my tip to others is that you better make sure you're on a pretty good insurance plan before visiting riverside as their billing department is not one that you want to work with! koop

my son recently had major surgery at chla. not only were the doctors and nurses attentive and helpful, but they did a great job of helping him recover quickly. 

they gave him a stuffed toy during his pre-op, gave us blankets the day of the operation while we waited, and the nurses always tried to make him and us comfortable.

when he was in icu, the nurses listened to us when we thought he was in pain and did whatever they could. the doctors and nurses communicated everything they were doing to us so we were aware and asked us if we were ok with things.

there is a lot of chaos at this hospital- if you are there you hear the helicopter coming frequently. when we were there some emergencies happened in other rooms as we heard the alarms. for all the staff is dealing with, they try to make everything as calm and helpful as possible. even when we would mention the chaos, they responded in a way that wasn't alarming. they do a great job of not scaring families but at the same time keeping you in the loop with your child. in icu they even let the parents attend the morning meeting where the doctors and nurses are discussing your child's care plan.

we were discharged pretty quickly which was the only thing that felt rushed, but i'm pretty sure they needed the room and my son was recovering well enough to go home. 

we had to go to the emergency room recently because of a possible issue from surgery. turns out it wasn't anything, but we needed to check. that experience was also good. yes, emergency rooms are crowded, with long wait times, and lots of sick people, like many people have mentioned in the reviews. that's typical of an er. as with any other emergency room, priority is given to the more urgent cases. we got in pretty quickly considering, and we were out within a few hours. 

the food at the cafe is good considering it's hospital food. that's a separate review i'll review specifically for the hbo cafe, but the only thing i'll mention here other than good food is be wary of dinner- it's the same food from lunch, so if you come later in the evening, they may not have much selection.

the only other thing i could say that's not positive is there was not clarity about giving blood before surgery. we were under the impression it was part of the pre op process. however, we found out that day that we really should have done it days before if we wanted it to be ready for our son for his surgery. chla has a large blood bank so it is not an issue, but good to know if you want to give blood for your child. they said many parents come back after to give blood for another child who may need it.

positive note, max parking per day is $10, and there is a parking pass for a week for $40. these are great rates for la and i'm happy they've done this. note on the parking though, the garage gets very full and sometimes it takes a while to get out. prepare accordingly for arrival and leaving. 

another positive, they have a full on farmers market on wednesday's, which is very nice if you're there with your child.

overall, chla is a great place considering how sad it is to see so many kids who are there. it's an eye opening place that has staff that do what they can to make it more positive, help kids heal, and bring smiles. 

i'm not sure why there are so many negative reviews. it seems most of them are about the emergency department and people who do not understand how that process goes, so please don't let those deter you from going here- whether to see a doctor, have a surgery, or to the er. it's a great place that takes care of kids!

miami healthcare exec philip esformes found guilty of paying kickbacks and bribes
by jay weaver and david ovalle
april 05, 2019 10:15 am 
philip esformes is a miami beach healthcare executive at the center of a massive medicare fraud case.
philip esformes is a miami beach healthcare executive at the center of a massive medicare fraud case. rob latour rob latour/invision/ap
philip esformes, an obsessive businessman who built an empire of healthcare facilities in miami-dade, was found guilty friday of 20 charges, including paying bribes and kickbacks, in a scheme to generate streams of medicare patients for his businesses.

the wealthy miami beach executive managed his chain of skilled-nursing and assisted-living facilities with an iron hand, with prosecutors arguing he had billed $1 billion to the federal health insurance program for questionable services that patients largely didn't need or even receive.

esformes faced 26 charges overall. the 12-person federal jury, after three full days of deliberation, came back with guilty verdicts on most of them in what was touted as the biggest medicare fraud case in the country -- in the reputed capital of such criminal activity, miami. jurors, however, did not reach a verdict on the main count -- that esformes had conspired to defraud the taxpayer-funded medicare progra

 

esformes, 50, went to trial alone in february because two key conspirators -- a physician's assistant and a former larkin hospital administrator who recycled patients for cash -- had pleaded guilty. several other healthcare associates charged with medicare fraud in related cases had also pleaded guilty and cooperated with federal prosecutors, including some who testified against him.




 1:32feds break up largest medicare scam in u.s. history

the u.s. attorney's office held a press conference in miami on july 22, 2016, announcing the filing of charges in connection with a $1 billion medicare care fraud scheme. by logan riely
esformes, who was arrested in july 2016 and has been held without bond at the federal detention center, could spend the rest of his life in prison, even without a healthcare fraud conspiracy conviction. he faces a forfeiture hearing before the jury on monday. no sentencing date has been set before u.s. district judge robert scola.

one of esformes' defense attorneys, roy black, focused on the fact that the jury was hung on the indictment's main conspiracy count of defrauding the medicare program.

"for three years, they [prosecutors] have touted this case as a $1 billion healthcare fraud and they failed to prove it," black said.

"the jury was unable to reach a verdict on that and several other counts; however, they did obviously find him guilty of a number [of other counts]," black added. "it's certainly a mixed bag."

the deadlocked verdict on the main conspiracy count was puzzling to some legal observers because jurors found esformes guilty of bribery and paying and receiving kickbacks to generate medicare patients for his facilities as well as those of other healthcare operators. it is possible that some of the jurors believed esformes' facilities provided healthcare services to patients and therefore did not technically fleece the federal program.

despite the mixed results, especially on the hung healthcare fraud count, the justice department declared total victory.

"philip esformes orchestrated one of the largest healthcare fraud schemes in u.s. history, defrauding medicare and medicaid to the tune of over a billion dollars," said assistant attorney general brian a. benczkowski of the justice department's criminal division. "i commend our dedicated prosecutors and law enforcement partners for their professionalism and unyielding pursuit of justice on behalf of american taxpayers and vulnerable beneficiaries who, as a result of esformes' crimes, were denied the level of care that they needed and deserved."

at trial, convicted healthcare operators, the former hospital administrator and an ex-ivy league basketball coach testified that esformes paid them and various doctors hundreds of thousands of dollars in bribes to buy and sell patients as well as to get his son into the university of pennsylvania. esformes himself made $38 million from medicare and medicaid payments between 2010 and 2016.

"ladies and gentlemen, the amount of cash was staggering," justice department lawyer allan medina said in a packed miami federal courtroom during closing arguments last week. "when you commit fraud of this magnitude, it's a win-win for all the partners in crime. philip esformes has a commodity, the patients. philip esformes has the doctors to do what he wants them to do."

unfortunately, going to the er at ojai valley community hospital (ovch) in recent years has become a little like playing a game of russian roulette with a couple rounds in the cylinder.  
   between 5 active, athletic kids and my own injuries, we've been there dozens of times over nearly 20 years. and in most cases it i'd describe our experiences as pretty good - as far as a trip to the emergency room goes. 
   however in the past few years that's changed, and seems to be getting progressively worse.  and our recent january 2020 er visit didn't help improve my opinion. 
   why the decline?  one big reason is that  ovch has been "contracting out"  it's emergency room services to what i'd describe as out of town medical "mercenaries" who come in and gouge the hospital and the patient.  they have no connection to the community, no affiliation with the hospital, and are essentially accountable to no one. they won't even tell you that your medical insurance is no good with them. it's insane. 
   even if ovch is part of your insurance plan and is recommended by your insurance carrier as your emergency care facility......even if you make your er co-payent to ovch when you check in at the emergency room desk..... these unethical parasite physicians will bill you separately for their er care because (as "contract physicians") they simply don't have to accept your medical insurance.  
problem is - you'll never know that until you subsequently receive their bill in the mail!  
   that's a sign to me that ovch has recently become hard-up for doctors / nurses and is failing the community with it's overall lack of oversight.  **the ovch foundation board needs to take action.   
   in fairness i'd say that as long as the er physician on duty happens to be one of the good local docs like doug nelson or gordon clawson (and a few others)  you're in competent care.  and if you're able to confirm beforehand (before any care is rendered) exactly who your er doc is going to be and that he/she fully accepts your insurance as full payment (get it in writing), you're probably ok from at least a billing perspective.
   if not i'd head immediately to cottage hospital in santa barbara or to saint john's hospital in oxnard where you'll get far more comprehensive (and much faster) care.  it'll be worth the drive and peace of mind.

the good: the nurses, doctors and support staff largely make a herculean effort to care for those who find themselves at this ancient medical facility. hugely grateful to them for saving my life. 

the bad: this was, without question, the dirtiest, most poorly designed, badly run hospital, with the most limited facilities, i have ever witnessed. 

summary: 9 hours in the shockingly dirty er which seems to operate much as one would anticipate in a third world country. 2-1/2 days in an equally filthy er room, while going through a battery of tests. several hours in surgery, which was very professional on all accounts. 2-1/2 days on the first floor ward, which was (again) shockingly dirty and poorly outfitted.

besides the excellent staff, this hospital is terrifyingly bad. apparently, nobody ever takes a shower here, as when one can find a shower, it appears to have last been cleaned in 1998. everything about this place (besides most of the staff) smacks of stunning disregard for the patient's comfort and wellbeing. i never saw anybody cleaning, beyond taking out the trash. there was visible dirt everywhere, save for the surgery and scanning areas. the blankets are as thin as paper and threadbare. ditto for the towels, if you can get your hands on one. 

the business office visited me twice, while i was doubled over in pain, waving documents and asking for money on the spot, in spite of my $1160 monthly premium being fully paid up -- and offering no specific details about what i was being charged for. apparently, my hospital co-pay is $1400, which they wanted on the spot, with zero itemisation. 

though i am grateful to the nurses and doctors who saved my life, i hope to never return to this hospital again.

doc_text:
hca must pay $162 million for charity care problems

healthcare giant hca, based in nashville, tn, must pay a kansas city, mo, charitable foundation $162 million and undergo extensive auditing after a judge found that the for-profit hospital operator broke key agreements regarding charity care and capital expenditures in its billion-dollar purchase of hospitals from health midwest in 2002.

judge john torrence, jd, of the circuit court of jackson county, mo, ruled that hca, the nation's largest investor-owned hospital company, did not spend as much money improving health midwest's existing facilities as it said it would. the judge also ruled that hca did not abide by an agreement to provide at least as much charity care to the community as the health midwest's not-for-profit hospitals had provided before the sale. that amount was said to be $65 million annually.

the health care foundation of greater kansas city (hcf) had sued hca in october 2009 to ensure that it had complied with its more than $950 million obligation to charity care in the kansas city area. the purpose of the lawsuit was to determine if hca had complied with its obligations to make $450 million in capital improvements to existing health midwest facilities and provide over $500 million in charity care. hcf chairman karen cox, rn, supported the ruling, saying "as a voice for the uninsured and underserved, the hcf board of directors felt it had the fiduciary responsibility to make sure that this population had been afforded the services promised to them through the sale of health midwest."

hca issued a statement saying it would appeal the decision. "rather than simply put money into the repair of old facilities, we built two new hospitals, spending hundreds of millions of dollars to ensure this community has high quality care," the company said in a written statement. "we believe we have complied with our agreement, exceeded our promises, and we continue to spend millions for the benefit of a community we love."

health midwest had operated 11 not-for-profit hospitals in missouri and kansas before the sale.

excellent hospital for giving birth in the bay area

we had two of our babies born here (3 years apart) at the sequoia "dignity health" hospital. both times we had a very pleasant experience. we found that virtually all the nurses were very well trained and highly experienced. we found that they were very caring for the health of the mother and the baby. i know a couple of our friends also gave birth in this hospital and were very happy. generally, it is not super crowded like some other hospitals and feels very clean and premium hospital. 

nurses:
i believe that each nurse are assigned to manage 2 patients during their shift. and there are two shifts (7am-7pm and 7pm-7am). so expect two main nurse assigned to you each day you are there. there are also other nurses who do some specific things, who keep coming in-and-out during the stay. they also have monitors in their lobby areas where they constantly monitor all the patients. one of the things that really impressed me is their team work. all the nurses were genuinely helping each other even when they were not assigned directly to the patient. 

emergency situations:
giving birth is a very complex thing and is really a miracle! at any given point in time, there could be an emergency! each room is equipped with emergency buttons that the mothers can push and it literally creates an ambulance like noise in the nurses' break rooms and control rooms with red-lights blinking above the patient's door and alerts every nurse about it. and both times we were there, some patients pressed their emergency buttons in the middle of the night for different reasons and i saw all these nurses literally running and rushing to that room to help that patient! it was really amazing to see them caring so much! this is the main reason i gave 5-stars! 

they also have a couple of in-house obgyn doctor (at least 1, 24x7) and couple of in-house anesthesiologists to take care of things in addition to nurses.

birthing room:
each birthing room has a fancy birthing bed with a lot of special capabilities to help with birthing. the bed also has a bunch of buttons to articulate the bed, plus there is a tv that the mother (or spouse) can watch while waiting for the baby to arrive. next to the bed, they have a small bed for the spouse or relative to take some rest (if that's possible). 
each room also has an attached restroom with a toilet, sink and a shower.

hospital food:
hospital food, especially for vegetarians like us was pretty blonde and terrible :( we suspected it and so we actually cooked food at home and brought it to the hospital, so it was not much of an issue. i hope non-vegetarian foods are better, but i encourage you to do the same as we did :)

postpartum:
one thing i've heard is that during some months it does become quite busy and after the birth, they'll move the mom and baby from the main birth room to a different smaller room during the 48 hours recovery period. i know one of our friends were moved but we were not.

i believe the hospital also has other departments, and i don't know anything about them but if you are planning to have a baby, i highly recommend this center and am sure this is one of the best in the bay area. 

btw, after the birth, make sure to give the nurses cookies and chocolates to thank them!

all the best!

the doctors, nurses, technicians and staff at memorial hospital of gardena rock! can't say enough nice things about them. i have been to their e.r. twice in the last 20 years (most recently this past week), and my wife has been here 3 times in the last year 1/2. my wife took me to the emergency room because i kept having chest pains, tightness, palpitations and burning in my stomach, back and arms. surprisingly the waiting room was pretty empty, then again it was a wednesday morning. 

i was admitted pretty quickly into the e.r. had my vitals checked and given a bed. they did an ekg on me and i was "glad" i was having the heart palpitations right at that moment and they were pretty intense and nonstop. i figured whatever was going on, if it was heart related they should be able to see it. that's the tricky thing with heart palpitations, often times they don't always happen, so you might go to the doctors office and not be having the symptoms when they do the ekg or listen to your heart. but this time i was having the palpitations and the doctor said my results came back normal and good and that i wasn't having a heart attack.

dr. sean howse was awesome as was the ekg technician. the phlebotomist was the best i've ever had! i didn't even feel the needle prick, and that was the part i was dreading the most, because i hate needles! but he took several vials of my blood and i didn't feel a thing! even the receptionist and security guards were nice! overall it was a great experience considering where i was at. i mean, no one wants to really go to the e.r., especially me! 

after the ekg and the doctor talking to me, listening to my heart and me describing my symptoms, he told me i had gerd and gastritis. he was about to discharge me but my wife and i insisted they do all the blood tests, all the heart tests to 100% rule out that it was not my heart, since i kept having these symptoms. the doctor was like "you're fine, it's not your heart, but if it'll make you feel better i can do all the tests." we were like "yes please do all the tests." 

i also insisted on him doing an ultra-sound of my stomach and intestines, since i kept having nonstop burning in my stomach and chest area and striking pains/cramping. he agreed to do all the tests i requested. for some time now i had been agonizing over if something was wrong with my heart and since i suffer from generalized anxiety disorder it constantly gave me panic attacks. i really needed to figure out what the hell was wrong with me and try to fix it. 

so they drew several vials of my blood, gave me a chest x-ray and a stomach ultra-sound. the test results for my heart and all my blood panels came back good. no liver, kidney, thyroid or heart issues, also no infections. the doctor said "that's good news that you have no stomach infections, i was worried about that, and your pancreas is good too, which was another concern." he said "my test results came back better than his!" dr. howse was very funny and his anologies are hilarious. my wife had him on a previous visit. he takes his time talking to you, explaining what's going on and what the results and treatment options are. he didn't rush when talking to me like some doctors do, he was very patient and caring and answered all my questions. so was the ekg nurse/tech ,the phlebotomist and the lady who did my ultrasound.

there was no evidence for active cardiopulmonary disease. there was no evidence for congestive heart failure on my chest x ray. no evidence of pneunothorax (a collapsed lung), and the osseous structures are intact. he said i need to drink more water because my water levels were lower than they should be but otherwise "my tests results came back better than his." but i do have gerd, gastritis, and i have several small gallstones. the doctor said they're tiny but they're there. he prescribed me antibiotics and several meds for gerd and gastritis and recommended a follow up with a gastroenterologist. 

we got there at 4am and left at 7am. not too bad for an emergency room visit, especially considering all the tests i did. glad this hospital is only 5 miles from my house!

on march 6, 2018 my wife was admitted to amg on gibson, for recovery and rehab of her body, after beating the flu at presbyterian hospital - where she was for over three weeks in acu.

right from the beginning, their nursing and doctor staff thwarted me at every attempt to be part of her care.  according to the initial paperwork and documents i received from their head nurse, they were supposed to include me in all of the actions to be taken during her rehabilitation, but instead battled me, rejected my input, and were in fact very obstinate and belligerent in the care i requested to be part of.

my wife was 54 yrs old and not of the senior citizen level - which their facility looked to have been the main type of patients in the rooms, so i really don't think they were qualified for the admittance of my wife.

for one mistake, it took them three days before anyone even looked at her for muscle rehabilitation.  and even that staff member, came in on a friday afternoon, and then said he won't be back until the following tuesday.  what the eff was that all about?  they were also strapping her arms and legs down to the bed at night - unneeded, after she and i both asked them not to.  i had to call the night nurse daily to ensure it was not happening to her.

the doctor who they assigned to her was a neurosurgeon and was employed with amg for only one day, and refused to look at her chart before he boldly and consistently refused me to speak for her.  i had to go to the ceo in order for them to understand that he wasn't going to do any work with her, until he reviewed her file.  he adamantly was angered that i stood up to him.  he even tried to leave the conference after i pointed out to the ceo what he was doing.

the same atmosphere was present with the supposedly "head nurse", who on the first day, gave me a list of things i was allowed to do - primarily, allowed to participate in every step of the care they were to provide.  she continuously was aggitated at my requested and constantly denied my participation.

even when my wife's eyes rolled into the back of her head and i screamed for help and no one came and then had to go and get a nurse to help myself, when i got back, and my wife seemed to have recovered from that moment, they looked at me and all they said was, "well she seems to be okay now."  they did not do anything but scoff at me and her.  even then, they had an intern stay to help my wife with a bed adjustment, and the same thing occurred again, while the intern witnessed it.  i again requested some help. and the intern looked at me with, "what would you expect me to do?" - and thus, did not even bother to back me up when i said it happened again.

the atmosphere i witnessed at this facility was totally against me and my wife's care. 
it was not in the least caring, supportive and helpful - and all i was trying to get the best care for my wife.

i will admit that the assigned neurologists and the nutritionists were helpful and took care of her as much as they could, but others - no they were not.

they failed time and time again.

after 5 days of this nonsense, i finally was able to speak with the ceo, kari, and we agreed that in two weeks time, my wife would be able to go home after her body had been rehabilitated.

this was also after they agreed that my wife's trachemotry tube would be removed.

my wife died in their care two days later on march 13, 2018.

i would advise everyone to either choose a different facility, or be like me, and show them that their own documents allow the family to participate in the care they supposedly say they offer.

keep them on their toes if you want the best care for your loved one - as they apparently don't think they should.

beware and think twice before you use this service.

dr. kosari is a terrible, careless, incompetent surgeon. do not trust him. i've made that mistake twice, so i'm not sure which of us is the bigger idiot. i've tried to summarize my experience with him below, but happy to describe in more detail through message for those considering a surgery with dr. kosari.

in 2013, i started to develop an umbilical hernia just above my belly button. it was never that noticeable, but in the spring of 2019, it had grown just enough to always be noticeable to me. i was referred to dr. kosari. i thought that the reputation of cedars-sinai would hold, but i was wrong.

in the examination, dr. kosari was friendly, but clearly rushed. he let me know he only had about 10 minutes. i explained i'd had the hernia for a few years and, while seated, he asked me to lift my shirt, briefly touched the belly button (literally for less than a second) where it was visible and that was it for the exam. he said he'd recommend doing the surgery with stitches, not mesh. knowing nothing about the difference, i trusted his judgment.

the day of the surgery, i was a bit tense as this was my first surgery. i was also concerned he had not adequately inspected the hernia (and he had not ordered any type of ultrasound). i waited for about 2 hours and then they took me in to prepare me. when i saw dr. kosari before the surgery, i explicitly asked him, "so you are going to be able to fix not only the part below the belly button, but also above it, right?" dr. kosari responded, "yes, don't worry. once we're in, we'll be able to check it all to see what we're dealing with."

i woke up after the procedure and went home. i had the surgery on friday, sep 13. i removed the bandage (which was covering the belly button and surrounding area) and showered on sunday, sep 15. by monday, i felt the hernia above my belly button exactly as before the surgery. panic immediately struck. i called cedars-sinai and was able to tell dr. kosari's nurse i felt a bulge exactly like the hernia, and she told me to just come in for my checkup in 2 weeks for dr. kosari to examine it.

when dr. kosari examined me, he tried to say there was nothing wrong, or that it was something else (like a result from the surgery or a problem with "skin" being "detached"). i told him, "no...i am 100% sure this is the same hernia i've had...it feels exactly the same." he told me to come back in 4 more weeks after the recovery period "to see if it's still there." that really aggravated me, i left the appointment knowing i still had the hernia, but he wouldn't acknowledge it.

at the next appointment, he acknowledged i still had a hernia, but never acknowledged it was because of his carelessness. compared to the first surgery, he was pushing much more strongly for not operating again. i think it's because it would make him look bad to have to repeat the exact same surgery, but i scheduled a follow up surgery for dec 3 anyway to get it dealt with once and for all (had already pretty much met my out of pocket max, so thought why not - and couldn't get in to ucla before the end of the calendar year - book ahead!).

on dec 3, i had the second surgery, and this time we did an ultrasound before the surgery. again, he did not recommend mesh, just a single stitch he said. this time, i didn't notice the hernia for a few weeks, but could definitely feel a slight bump, which i thought might be the stitch or something. now, just over 6 weeks since the second surgery, i still have the hernia. i can feel it exactly the same as i used to.

after one surgery, i'd expect a hernia to be fixed, at least for a few years before it might recur. after two surgeries, i would really expect a hernia to be fixed. now, after spending thousands of dollars, taking months off from the gym for two separate recoveries, and still having the problem that was supposed to be fixed, i'm so filled with anger and frustration about this "doctor." he is careless, negligent, or uses poor judgment in making choices for his patients' care. 

please, do not select this doctor. i will be seeing dr. chen from ucla instead....happy to compare my experience after my third hernia surgery for the same hernia. in my last check-up after the second surgery, dr. kosari told me, "if it comes back let me know and we can go back in there with the mesh." to myself, i thought this moron will never touch my body again. don't let yourself become another one of his mistakes. i will forever regret it, but hopefully i can get a successful surgery from ucla and eventually put this behind me. but i'm sure i will continue to live with the nightmares about the hernia problems that i've had ever since the first surgery was unsuccessful, i hope you can learn from my pain and experience to avoid the same experience with this terrible doctor. cedars-sinai should not allow this man to be operating under their name.

as they say, "fool me once, shame on you, fool me twice shame on me." he won't be fooling me a third time.

and told us to call in a couple hours and she would let us know if she was awake. i called the # at 2:00 and no answer, 3:00 same results. finally at 4:00 we just showed up. she had been moved to a different room and was basically unattended as she was waiting for a room to become available. we asked the staff if her husband would be allowed to stay with her in the room as she becomes agitated and uncooperative if separated from him. we were told by a couple er nurses that it wouldn`t be a problem and they would put a recliner in the room next to her bed. so here we are in a er room awaiting a room. one chair for us to sit on  which we gave to my step-dad while my niece and i stood. mom was still out of it. still waiting for a room to become available. a board in the room shows that some test were ordered and completed and others were pending. we asked about which test were done and the results but nursing staff was unable to give us answers. we asked which test were pending and the answer was the same. we are getting mad that we are just in a room with no idea whats going on or when a room will be available. finally about 7:00 pm they told us a room was available but it had to be cleaned. we waited and waited. finally the nurse tells us that because multiple room became available at the same time housekeeping had to clean them in the order of the vacancy so we had to wait longer for them to clean her assigned room.

i don`t remember what time we got to the room but i again asked the guy transporting her about her husband staying in the room. his response: that`s not a problem. in the process of transferring her to the bed it was discovered she had been laying in her own urine for quite awhile. i then asked her nurse about her husband staying in the room and the answer was "absolutely not". this is the women`s floor and no men were allowed to stay in the room. they said he could sleep in a recliner at the end of the hallway, in the visitors area. i asked to speak to the charge nurse and she reiterated the same thing. she didn`t get that i was upset because everyone up to this point had stated "no problem" and at the last minute she says no! major communication breakdown. this lack of communication causes us problems and get my mother and step-dad to become upset. in addition, even though they had a list of her meds it took them until the next day to admin. to her.

last month, my wife required a standard procedure that was going to be done at the hospital in salina. the procedure was done as promised, performed exactly as expected. the nurses and the doctor were excellent. 

prior to the procedure, the insurance experts at salina hospital, after reviewing our blue cross and blue shield policy, determined that our share of this procedure would be $823. however, after the operation, we received a bill for $592 in addition to the apparently grossly under estimated original $823. i called them at 3:00 in the afternoon and they finally returned  the phone message i left, three days later. i was informed that there were additional expenses that were unknown. at the risk of being redundant here, it was a standard procedure. being a contractor, if i estimate a job at $800 and then tell my customer that it's going to cost  hundreds of dollars more at the end because of other expenses, a 75% increase will not be acceptable to the customer. however obviously in the medical industry that's not a problem. you're just expected to pay that additional amount. 

why even offer an estimate if it will be 75% more at the end?  do we need medical reform? should salina regional health fire their insurance estimating department? does salina need to hire someone to figure out what the costs will actually be? 

the bottom line is don't believe anything that salina regional health center tells you prior to any procedure. we have had various surgeries done in manhattan and they somehow knew how much it would cost us.  i am still waiting for a return call from diane , the supervisor at 2:09 p.m. (she missed me today), to get back with me. not that i'm holding my breath that anything will make any difference or even that she'll call in the next few days. go to a different town for medical procedures if you want true estimates for billing. ken, ellsworth, kansas.

turns out, i was suffering from a very severe complication - placental abruption. my nurse was terrible and started screaming at the top of her lungs - in no way did she try to calm me down at all, in turn causing me to panic and go into distress. they got both of us on to the operating table within minutes - no heartbeat from the baby and an  unconscious mom.

fastforward to the next 4 days in the hospital....i got told i need to suffer through the pain and work through it because 'i shouldn't be needing pain meds this frequently this long after a c-section.' 
i had concerns about the latch of my baby for breastfeeding - no one ever checked, i was simply told 'look at him, he's latched and doing great!!' he in fact was not latched and was not doing great. he had lost 12% of his birthweight and nobody at the hospital cared. he had a severe lip and tongue tie, making latching very difficult. nobody at the hospital took the time to check or figure out. my poor baby was starving and  my concerns were being ignored!

once again, we found ourselves back at mercy gilbert, but for my mother-in-law this time. overall, the medical care was great - the doctors were skilled and personable and the nurses/nursing staff were patient and considerate. 

we came in through the ed and, as always, the care and experience was excellent! if i were rating only the ed, it would be a 5-star review. 

but! this is the 4th time i've had a loved one at this hospital and the discharge planning was either non-existent or poor, at best. this leads me to believe that this is a pattern for their social services department - that they have been led to believe this kind of service is acceptable. 

this time there, the experience with social services was poor - extremely. 

the first social worker was impatient, did not follow through and was very casual regarding finding a snf for my mother-in-law - we were overwhelmed with everything going on and she hands us pages of facilities in no particular order and tells us to "pick one" and left. we are fairly confident she did not follow up on our request to check with another facility with which we had prior experience as she blew us off when we asked if it was an option.

on the day my mother-in-law was to be discharged, the social worker poked his head in the room and said "they'll be here to pick her up between 4 and 6" and then left. that was it. he didn't tell use what facility it was, provided us no information about it or the address so that we could meet transport there. he didn't sit down with my mother-in-law to explain what was happening or what to expect. she is elderly, just broke her hip and has dementia...she needed that explanation! 

we never saw social services after that. we had more caring, personality and compassion from the surgeon (they're not known for their bedside manner) than we did from social services.  and, then, transport was over an hour late and was terrible. that is a separate issue that we will take up with that company. 

i guess that we should just be grateful that we had any discharge planning at all. and, unlike my father-in-law, she was not discharged with a broken nose from a fall sustained at this hospital because someone did not turn the bed alarm back on. 

perhaps social services did not get the "hello humankindness" (the 
"motto" of dignity health) memo or they just ignore the plaques on the walls that are reminders of that idea. but, really, social services is the department lacking humankindness?  i am confused.

i've come to this emergency room twice in recent years and have to say, based upon past experiences at other hospital ers, this one is pretty damn good. 

a few years ago i sprained an ankle playing volleyball and came in for x-rays.  i waited probably less than 25 minutes to be called back for x-rays to make sure i didn't fracture anything and was assisted by friendly a pa who did an exam and answered all my questions. i was probably in and out in about an hour. 

the second time i had recently had a very long flight and had swelling in one leg and was concerned it could be a blood clot. i was quickly called back for a blood test to rule out deep vein thrombosis and ended up waiting in a back staging area for about an hour and a half for the results. again, a super friendly pa introduced herself and explained what they were going to do and what the tests were for. much appreciated. 

eventually, i found that i was going to also have a vascular ultrasound of my leg to rule out the blood clot which was about another hour or so and then i was just waiting to be discharged or find out what was happening from there while the radiologist read my scans. 

the internal waiting room was a bit cold and uncomfortable but it is what it is.  it's a hospital. 

this er is pretty fast and efficient and the staff are friendly and seem to really care.  my only issue is that both times i've only spoken to a p.a. or a nurse.  while i understand the doctors are busy, for the cost, it would be nice to be seen and spoken to by one of them.  on the most recent visit last week, my discharge was done by the nurse who didn't really answer my questions and said they didn't actually know what was wrong with me, but they had ruled out a blood clot so good luck and follow up with my pcp.  

for however many thousands of dollars i spent - that was disappointing.  

still, the staff are friendly and the wait is usually short, that's important.

below is a detailed description of our experience giving birth here: 

my wife received a total of 18 excruciating cervical checks within 1.5 days of trying to induce! she received 4 doses of cytotec inserted vaginally which caused her to be so sore and sensitive that each cervical exam was beyond painful. several of these could have been eliminated but the hospital was out of the applicator. i mean come on, how do you run out of that? i offered to drive to another nearby hospital to pick one up but they wouldn't allow it. 

because induction didn't work, she had a c-section. the hospital was out of something called a joey pack so they refused to do skin-to-skin once baby was born. after talking to them for awhile, they agreed to allow it. but once baby came, they ignored this request and didn't do skin-to-skin as promised only moments before. 

baby couldn't latch and the nurse told us to feed newborn only 15ml (1/2 oz) of formula at each feeding. this is way too little and is why she lost over 7% weight within 1 day! why would they have purposely told us to under feed her? they also strongly discouraged us from using our own formula since it could only be mixed with sterile water (according to them). even though the nicu had this water, they flat out said the nicu was closed and it was too difficult of a process getting permission to open it. even after waiting until the next morning when the nicu was sure to be open, they insisted it was too difficult getting permission to use the water. really, i mean come on, you've seriously got to be kidding! 

although almost all of the nurses were great, one latin nurse in particular was very rude to us and just unfriendly. i won't post her name here but she was the only nurse at night so we couldn't switch. she is specifically the one in question who gave us all the issues with using our formula that i mentioned above.

instead of getting all the blood work needed at once, they kept forgetting necessary tests which caused our baby to get multiple blood draws that were not necessary. these could have been taken at once to avoid pricking her with the needle so many times! again, communicate better and get your shit together! 

after talking at length with the hospitals pediatrician, we agreed to not administer the hepatitis b vaccine at the hospital. we had to sign papers, talk with several people about it, but it was all agreed we would do it in a few weeks with our own pediatrician on our own schedule. however, after we were discharged and at home, we read through the hospital paperwork and it says that they did administer the hep b vaccine. did they do this behind our backs without our consent or is their paperwork incorrect? how can a hospital make this kind of mistake?

overall, even though we were mostly satisfied with the level of care we received, i would not recommend good samaritan medical center in west palm beach to give birth based on all the issues i mentioned above.

this is regarding the kaiser south sacramento infusion center an rheumatology clinic. 
several months back, i took my sister in for her infusion. she had an anaphylactic reaction to the medication being infused. the male nurse (who transferred in from the ed)  was excellent. he knew what to do and took good care of her. this was supposed to be our last visit under the care of the rheumatologist who ordered the medication. we had, had enough of her poor practices and decided to transfer care to ros. kp.
somehow, because it was the middle of the month, she superseded the new rheumatologist we were transferring to. my sister went in for what we thought was a new medication to try (to get her disease under control). 
i dropped her off and told her i would be back after i picked the kids up from school. within minutes of me getting home, i received a phone call from my sister. she was whispering "can you come back and take me to the bathroom". i asked her to repeat it several times because i could barely hear her and i couldn't believe what she was saying. nevertheless, i rushed back, in rush hour traffic. her door was closed all but a crack. anger came over me when i saw her condition. she was horribly swollen with a bright red face. her face was so swollen her eyes looked closed.  she had a bath blanket over her chest with spit all over it. she said she felt like she had to have a bowel movement and urinate. she said that her nurse told her it that they don't take people to the bathroom. i was stunned, shocked and in disbelief. just then, her rn walks in and says " yeah, um are you the family"? i said "yes". to which she replied " yeah, so we don't take people to the bathroom so if she's going to need the bathroom when she's here one of you need to stay with her and help her to do that. this is an outpatient clinic, this is not inpatient hospital we do not transfer or take people to the bathroom". "if she is gonna be needing to use the bathroom then you're going to have to talk to her doctor and see if she can be admitted to the hospital for these infusions and then discharged when she's done". i was speechless. i looked at her probably with disgust and confusion, then looked at my sister, then looked back at her. she then went on and said "oh yeah she went into shock again we almost had to transfer her to the er". i said, she's allergic to the new medication to? the nurse replied, "her rheumatologist, wanted to try the medication again from last month. we thought that if we front-loaded her with as much steroids as we possible could that she wouldn't have a reaction. but, she did and because we had already front-loaded her with all the steroids; we couldn't give her anything but iv fluid. hence, that is why she is so swollen." i said oh, so you have her the medication that she had known anaphylaxis to. she went into anaphylaxisi again which is why she has to use the bathroom and why she is whispering (swelling in the throat). i said, and which md ordered this? the nurse said it was the md we had just transferred away from. i have since spoke to two separate providers and both agree that the massive amounts of steroid that she was given pushed her into cushing's disease.
in my opinion, the the doctor needs to be reviewed for unsafe medical practices. and the nurse should be reviewed by the nursing board and perhaps have her license suspended. regardless of if a doctor orders a medication or not, if you know it is unsafe for your patient you should not be giving it. thank god for the medical assistant that heard my sister trying to call out for help over her swollen vocal cords and alerted the medical staff team. that is a huge problem with kaiser. they want people that bsn or higher behind their name regardless of how they obtained it and what experience they may have. 
btw, i tried to file a complaint on my sister's behalf because she was too ill to do it herself and kaiser would not allow me to. i was told they have to come directly from the member or you have to be the dpoa on file to file a complaint on their behalf.

doc_text:
*kaiser permanente santa clara clinic* 
i've been to the evening clinic thrice so far when skyport, where i usually go for routine health care & generally like, didn't have any appointments. each time, i've been disappointed with the quality of doctors at the clinic. granted it is just 3 different doctors so there may be some sampling bias. but i will promptly update this review if i ever visit this location again (& i hope i don't have to).

*kaiser permanente santa clara emergency room*
skyport doesn't have an er so my nearest er is also santa clara. this week when i needed to, i was hoping that their er would be different - at least as good if not better than any regular er (eg. kp oakland) - from its evening clinic. after all, they're two different buildings, adjacent but on the same campus. but i was just so disappointed. at the er, it was an experience, just as bad if not worse than some civil hospitals. first, we couldn't find parking & there was no one available at the valet. it took us 10 min to find parking, but far away. registration took us another 25 min. i was in pain but there was also another patient behind me on a wheelchair who appeared either passed-out or in deep-pain so had just put her head down & was being assisted by another kaiser helper waiting their turn. long lines & only two nurses to register & only 1 nurse to take the vitals, who was also a part-time helper if a patient needs wheelchair assistance, after. it appeared that they had no sense of urgency or emergency, sometimes even chit-chatting & laughing amongst themselves while we were still waiting in the line, in pain. in fact, most of the er medical staff including the doctors & the nurses seemed fairly junior & disorganized too. as you'll read further, all of them (from the nurses that registered to the doctors & nurses who diagnosed/treated me) were asking me the same questions all over again, yet re-typing my responses into their computer, not realizing i was in pain & frustrated, repeating the same responses. for example: 
-what brings you in today?
-when did you start feeling this way?
-on a scale of 1-10, how would you rate your pain?
-have you seen a doctor for this & when?
-is this your first time at the er for this issue?
-have you had any medication recently?
-other personal questions, already on my chart
after the registration, i was sent to the waiting room & after another 30 min, into the screening room - the first point of medical triage. in the screening room, the nurse first asked me the same bunch of questions that i had already answered during registration. she hadn't read my chart nor my earlier responses to these questions. then after about 5-10 min a doctor came by & asked most of the same questions, again, without having read my chart, but a few new too, related to my pain:
-do you have any sensitivity to light?
-do you have stiffness in your neck?
-have you been already tested for this infection? (no. but as you will read below this somehow got interpreted to yes!)
he then told me that some other doctors would examine me further and i was sent to a patient room at the back of the er. after waiting for 10-15 min another nurse came in & asked me the exact same questions all over again. the room was very cold, so i asked her for a warm blanket which she quickly got for me. 
then after about 5 min, a doctor came to see me. she asked me most of the same questions again & ordered bloodwork, saline water, & other pain medicines through an ivr. finally reading into my notes, she thought that i was already tested for this infection earlier. (remember my answer above was no.) i said no again, and she said she'd order it - she didn't. the nurse inserted an iv needle to draw out blood & then administer saline water & pain medication. but while inserting the iv needle she wasn't gentle -showed her inexperience. she inserted the needle so hard that a lot of blood spilled over the sheet & the floor below -by the way, not the cleanest i've seen in an er. instead of apologizing, she asked me:
-have you had any alcohol or use blood thinner? (no.)
she just smiled & told me that i have a lot of blood that just oozed out so quickly (ok! what!?)
i was administered the saline water & some pain medicines. after 30-min, another doctor came in. he also assumed my infection test was done but i said no yet again but he said that it didn't matter anymore!  he suggested some otc medicines, assured me that i should feel better soon & left. after about an hour i started feeling better due to the pain medicines but during that time a lot of people were walking & talking pretty loudly outside. i overheard an entire conversation of a random nurse who's soon moving in with her boyfriend (good luck, but this is an er!). then my nurse came back with my discharge papers, went over them, wished me well, & then i gladly left. at least no longer in pain. at least i'm not mad at yelp for not letting me leave them 0 stars & they get 1.

on the position side of gwinnett medical center (gmc) i am a fan of their women labor and delivery unit (gwinnett women's pavilion). we had two children born here one back in 2012 (before the takeover) and in 2018 when northside hospital just started taking over gmc. all of the nurses and doctors were pleasant and i liked that they changed their policy to keep the babies in the room with the parents.

i'll give 4 stars for the women's pavilion.

now on with the emergency room...

my biggest complaint is the gwinnett medical emergency room center. the wait time here is extremely long (about 3 hours minimum). my wife is on the clinical side of healthcare and i used to be so we are consider ourselves very understanding.

we decided to here as our daughter who was 12 months came here to visit as she had an extremely high temperature of nearly 104 that would not go down using acetaminophen, ibuprofen, or liquids. nothing would lower her fever after about 3-4 hours, so we came here.  after hours and hours of waiting, we were seen. the nurses ran several tests, one after another and they found nothing, as we thought maybe it must be a viral infection or a uti, but it was neither.

we went home and after a month received a bill for $3,469.00 and our insurance picked up a little. gwinnett medical center now is under northside hospital, so all of their bills are under northside hospital now.

they apparently have a financial assistance program to help patients who are in a certain income bracket, which we qualify for. after speaking with their financial assistance people we have been told they would call us on the phone and not to call them. they insisted they would call us and after waiting and waiting... we have called half a dozen times with them telling us to keep waiting. yet, month after month we keep getting this extremely high medical bill saying our balance is delinquent - pay immediately. why have a program that does not work? gmc/northside you guys can do better.

the bill: 

$3,469.00 - 2 hour room rental, 2 saline iv's, 1 uti test, 1 blood test, 2 nurses (est. 20 minutes), 1 amoxicillin rx and 3 freeze popsicle's.

honestly, i really thought having northside hospital take over gwinnett medical center would be such a blessing for all those who live in gwinnett county. my professional advice is if you have an option (non-life-threatening) to take your children to choa (children's health care of atlanta) and stay away from the (er) gmc/northside hospital unless you have health insurance benefits that pay 100%. if you are an adult with non-life-threatening issues, more than likely, one would be better off to just visit an urgent care facility. my personal experience is they are cash base ($100-$150) and that is all you will pay if treated in their clinic, of course, that depends on what one needs (specialists refers...)

it stinks i had to write this, but i thought it was important to inform others, just so there is some transparency. do not expect the same as it was under gmc. when it was under gmc ownership the reviews here were mostly extremely good.

so i went in for a d&c, which is a fairly standard operation. no matter how i tried, i couldn't get them to put into their medical records that i'm allergic to some antibiotics--one severely. my primary care doctor told them. i believe my ob-gyn's office told them, but friday afternoon before i was to have surgery, they called me on an old phone number i haven't used for fifteen years (somehow, it still put a notice in my email), and when i called back, they had no record of these allergies. 

what they wanted (it was a nurse who didn't seem to care about putting in my drug allergies) was $4,000 upfront, or they wouldn't operate. i needed this operation to rule out cancer, so i argued them down to $1,000 upfront.

the medical information they had on me was 20 years out-of-date, including illnesses i hadn't had since my 20s. i'm almost 50. 

spooked by this horrible record-keeping, i made sure to walk in on the day of my operation with several printed copies of the medicines i was taking and the medicines i was allergic to. i gave these out to several nurses. (it was never clear to me who was a nurse and who was a med-tech. they should introduce themselves better.)

on intake, they mentioned that they gave people lavender essential oils as part of pain relief. i told them not to--that i was allergic. lavender gives me asthma. remember this....

so i gave out my sheet listing my medications and allergies to several people, but when i got into the operating room, one of the last things i remember the surgeon saying was, "so, no allergies?!" i told him then and then--they were already giving me things through my iv, that i had a severe reaction two two common antibiotics (clarithromycin and cirpo) and could not take them.

this was after telling seven people that i had these issues.

so i woke up in recovery, and there was the nurse, trying to give me lavender.

i told her to go away.

i was in pain, but only accepted an extra-strength tylenol because i was afraid that, if i was out-of-it, and they screwed up and tried to give me something that would make me sick, i wouldn't be able to stop them.

harbor hospital is not a safe place to go because they can't get basic info about your drug allergies into their system.

getting money out of you is more important than taking care of you.
