i'm a labor and delivery traveling rn and have been to many hospitals over my 18 years of travel nursing.  i wanted to take the time to write a review of this hospital because i am very, very impressed with the care and service that they give their labor and delivery patients.  
the rooms are not as big or flashy as sutter or kaiser, true, but the nurses are kind, intelligent, and very caring.  they know their stuff, as the hospital is able to accept high risk patients from the area.  their c section rate is very below the national average (i heard it was 10% which is amazing) and they have a really wonderful lactation consultant that sees patients all week.  every patient gets a social work visit as well, in case they have personal issues they might need help with.  midwives attend most deliveries but the obs are very non interventive and will respect individual wishes.  eating in labor is normal as well as using mobile monitors or just being intermittently monitored to begin with. there are no prima donna surgeon types here and i so appreciate that.  the coffee they bring to the floor is starbuck's, and the food will improve when their kitchen renovation is complete!  all in all, it's one of my favorite hospitals i have ever worked in!

since there are only two long term acute care facilitates in san diego, you don't have many options for your loved one.  once i found out my father would need to go to one, i immediately came to yelp to check the reviews.

i'm of the opinion that a lot more people come to yelp to complain about something versus coming here to praise something so the reviews tend to trend to the negative.  therefore, so people can get my honest opinion, i will do my review on a day-by-day basis.  i'm going to start my rating at 3 stars just so that it doesn't skew the overall scores on here.

admissions - i spoke with april on the phone.  she made me feel very comfortable with this facility.  she gave me all her contact information.  my dad's transition here went very smoothly.  

day 1 - when my dad got to his room on the 4th floor, he was greeted by david and tami.  they did a very thorough check of him and changed all his bandages.
they were great at explaining everything which made me feel like he was in good hands.  

day 2 - i arrived at the room just after 10 a.m.  my father was alone and eating breakfast.  the orders that came over here from ucsd state that he needs to be supervised while eating due to the possibility of choking.  i spoke with the dietician sherry about this and she promised that she would get those orders onto his plan over here.  apparently, that information didn't get transferred to this facility but i'm not sure who's fault that was.

he did get his best nights sleep in about 2 weeks.  he has a private room here and isn't constantly being woken up by the two other patients bells and whistles going off every 10 minutes like at ucsd.

day 3 - the orders for supervised eating are now on his orders here.  his nurses name today is eileen.  she is giving him great care.  she checked an infected wound dressing that wasn't scheduled to be checked until tuesday.  she changed it and is now adding to his chart for it to be checked daily instead every three days.  nurses like her make it so much easier on the family when they leave for the night.

days 4 to 15-  mostly very good nurses here.  there was only one that he didn't seem too happy with one morning when i got there.  but since he's been unable to speak since his stroke, i'm not sure why.

laura the speech therapist was good.  so were the physical therapists.

it's never an easy time having a loved in a care facility.  you're always worried if they are being taken care of well when you're not there.  looking back on the past two weeks here, i'm very satisfied with the overall care of this hospital.

my elderly mother has been rushed to this hospital's er and subsequently admitted for congestive heart failure flare-ups and other health issues numerous times since 2017. i've been very involved in her care as her patient advocate and dpoa (durable power of attorney). as a concerned son, i always aim to collaborate with the care staff. each time my mom and i have engaged this hospital's healthcare services, we have enjoyed a deeper understanding of just how difficult it is to provide 100% care, 24/7. the er is a fascinating and unpredictable mix of chaos and coordination. yet with the challenges of providing care for the never-ending flow of patients, this hospital's er has been extraordinary in my view. thank you to trisha (charge nurse) and her team for keeping my mom safe and stable until her admit to the hospital was possible. beds were limited due to the swell of flu cases in sd county, i assume. mom and i had to wait a long time, but we got in and once admitted, my mom continued to receive excellent care from the team on the 5th floor - north.

for those family members who read this review and have had different experiences, please remember that these facilities have protocols that must be followed and limitations on what can be provided. our health care industry in the usa is always evolving, and insurance is like navigating a never-ending sea of red tape and bureaucracy. you must advocate for yourself or for the loved ones who can't advocate for themselves. be patient and polite, when possible. your nurses and doctors care... and they're only human. team work makes the dream work!

i was admitted to antelope valley hospital as a trauma patient early last month after a terrible head on collision. initially the trauma nurses were great until the ct scan. a woman who was in the ct scan room asked the man who was wheeling me in if he asked if i may be pregnant. "that's not my question to ask" is what he said. then she asked me directly if there was a chance that i could be pregnant and i said yes. after that the entire staff seemed extremely annoyed, and didn't end up even administering a pregnancy test before the ct scan. although this was very upsetting i wasn't in the state of mind to bring any more concern on the matter.

they then put me in the emergency room and eventually came in to tell me i had a fractured l5 vertebrae, and fractured fibula on my left leg. i knew something was wrong with my right foot but they insisted that nothing showed up in the ct scan. they ordered a cam boot for my left leg then tried to put it on the right instead. a common theme in my 5 days here was that i had to inform almost every staff member of my own injuries and i wasn't even confident that they had diagnosed everything properly.

i had two mris done because i kept complaining about my foot. it wasn't until the 4th day that they found 2 fractures in my right foot. this was extremely upsetting after a ct scan and x-rays on my feet, and the doctors kept promising that i would go home the next day after day 2.

i spent the first night and second day in the critical care unit, which most of the nurses there were extremely attentive, i believe angela was the name of the rn i had during the day and she was great. once they moved me out of critical care the second night, it all went extremely downhill.

the remaining 3 days consisted of an average wait of 30-45 minutes for any nurse to assist after i pushed the button (especially during the night time) and a lot of rough handling when transporting me anywhere. keep in mind i have a fractured spine vertebrae and (soon to realize) three total leg/foot fractures between my two legs so i could not do more than roll on to my side, let alone sit up/stand/walk. this is incredibly disappointing beings how i am only in my 20s and someone who would seriously need help could possibly not have their call answered in a timely manner.

the two other nurses that stood out to me were stephenie (rn) and sherri (nt). sherri, who was very nice and talkative, unfortunately spent entirely too long speaking with patients about her personal life. she was the one i had the biggest problem with answering my calls. after 45 minutes, i sent my husband to find her, then 30 minutes later she came back in a rush and told me i just needed to be patient. i'm sorry but waiting over an hour for a bed pan because i can't walk myself to the restroom is ridiculous. this seemed like a common theme before shift change that the wait times would get longer and longer.

stephenie on the other hand, was the best nurse i had. she answered my calls promptly (usually within 5 minutes),was very informative, gave me a lot of supplies and products to maintain my hygiene, and helped clean my tables often. she was very nice and offered a lot of emotional support as well as she was my nurse on day 4 and i was ready to get the f out of that place.

all in all, if you are not a trauma patient, please go elsewhere. that is the only reason i had to go here and although i am grateful for the staff members that truly helped, i wish that my experience was different.

franciscan health wound care institute is precisely what you'd expect. it's an outpatient clinic located within st. francis hospital that provides care for wounds including hyperbaric oxygen therapy, diabetes foot and ankle care, limb salvation, and general services related to a wide variety of wounds including pressure ulcers. 

during my recent hospitalization, much to my dismay, i was found to have multiple pressure ulcers secondary to my recent health decline and also due to my status as a wheelchair-using paraplegic and amputee. these wounds healed dramatically during my 10-day hospital stay, but following my discharge i was also seen by a wound care nurse through home health and, as such, was provided an appointment with the wound care institute to ensure that healing was maintained. 

my appointment was about three weeks post-discharge. the stitches were still in my recent amputation, while i continued to be receiving home health care. 

the clinic is located inside the hospital at the outpatient center entrance - entrance 12, a fact that should probably be advertised somewhere but isn't and partly contributed to my being a few minutes late for my appointment. as this is a healthcare setting, accessible parking is plentiful and st. francis actually offers free valet services. 

the clinic is located on the first floor - it's a bit winding, but the signage is actually pretty solid and i had no problem finding it. 

while i had some experience with iu wound care previously, i'd never been to this wound care and it's run quite differently. with iu wound care, you're essentially seen by physical therapists who specialize in wound care and are nationally certified. at franciscan, it's a more traditional clinic overseen by two physicians. i was seen by a tech who did my vitals, a nurse who examined my wounds and took measurements/photos, and a physician - dr. monica joyner. as my frame of reference had been iu, i expected a different set-up and had specifically requested my clinician be a female due to my background as a survivor. 

due to issues with my transportation and getting lost a bit within the campus, i arrived about ten minutes past my appointment time and past the 15 minutes early they had requested. i thought the response to this was a tad snarkier than it needed to be, but by appointment's end i had certainly apologized and they seemed fine. instead of a "we told you to be here at 10:45," a simple "we were getting worried as we expected you at 10:45," a gentler way of inquiring about someone's tardiness. since i'm post-op and reliant on others for transportation, i just really didn't need or deserve the snark. the nurse had even made a point of saying that she was getting ready to go upstairs and see a patient (implying that i'd almost missed her), an odd fact to me since my appointment was scheduled for an hour and i was there well within that hour. 

okay, i'm done venting. 

fortunately, once the snark was done st. francis got me to providing the usual quality care i've come to expect. i was pleasantly surprised by how accessible the table/bed in the room was and i was easily able to transfer independently even as a new above-knee amputee. the nurse in question had actually seen me while i was inpatient and was well informed about my case and quite wonderful to work with. she was professional and compassionate and explained everything she was doing. she was pleasantly surprised with the amount of healing and actually showed me a photo taken of the first day she had seen me - my first thought was "wow, gross!" and my second thought was definitely a little pride at the work i'd put in to get healing going on. 

dr. joyner saw me quickly and agreed with the nurse that both wounds of concern were obviously in good shape and improved. she didn't change the course of treatment and only sought to schedule one more follow-up with possible cancellation if everything continues going so positively. 

my appointment actually did finish within the hour, though i was very pleasantly surprised that they didn't have any intention of seeing me on an ongoing basis. i always felt like at iu like they were determined to squeeze in as many appointments as possible. franciscan, on the other hand, focused on healing and didn't seem to be trying to extend treatment. they simply did what was necessary. 

while the wound care institute is a decent drive for me, i was impressed with the warm atmosphere and it felt less clinical. it felt like a doctor's office and this was even with one elderly patient nearby who was obviously suffering. it was a very peaceful setting and very healing. 

i didn't appreciate the initial sense of snark, but everything else that followed was top notch and i would definitely return should the need arise.

well, a few weeks before giving birth, my husband and i went on a tour of the hospital (sloane) where i was going to give birth bc that's where my doctor delivered (ironic that at this time i didn't realize that my doctor's practice has about 12 doctors and whoever is on call at the time, even if that doctor is a complete stranger to you, they will deliver your baby = i could have just rolled up to any hospitals and would have had the same level of personal care).  anyway, we were highly unimpressed with the aesthetics of the hospital:  it's located within a children's hospital, there is no waiting area for family, the only food is a small, dirty "cafe" with limited hours and a lot of the rooms and areas we saw just looked dingy and dirty.  we sucked it up because we had no choice unless we wanted to change doctors and that seemed like a hassle.  

flash forward to being in labor.  i must say, all of that one star is for the nurses - awesome, kind and phenomenal labor and delivery nurses!  and then came in the anesthesiologist at 2:30am.  little did i know that she was on the 23rd hour of her 24 hour shift (and this is the head of ob anesthesiology!).  she started my epidural and i immediately felt an electric shock run down my leg and an intense splitting headache and neck pain wash over me.  she had me lay down and confusingly offered to let me know what was going on after birth.  what??  no, tell me now.  she rambled on about giving me a wet tap instead of an epidural but how this is actually better than having a regular epidural.  the back labor excruciating pain allowed me to not really care about what she was saying in the moment and carry on with labor.  as i had said to my doctor for months, i started asking nurses and doctors about the baby's position so he was presenting posterior on the prenatal exams and i knew that this would cause back labor.  everyone continued to brush me off and as the wet tap wore off, i began to feel the most intense pains of my life in my back, head and neck.  after 15 more hours of this pain and questioning what was happening, i finally started calling for a c-section because i didn't know how this was going to happen (why is the patient bringing this up when they know the baby is in an unfavorable position and very large! and they know the mother is a small framed person!) - i didn't want a c-section but i had no other option at this point.  

as they moved my body to the operating table, i screamed in pain for my head and my neck - as they prepped for the c-section, i had two anesthesiologists standing behind me trying different drugs in my botched epidural and asking me if i could feel what they were doing.  as they started the surgery, i would scream out as i could feel (yes feel!) parts of the procedure and they would quickly inject more drugs into my iv.  when all was said and done, my 9lb 6oz baby was not breathing well when born and sent to the nicu and i laid on the operating table and cried - cried bc i didn't have my baby, cried bc i was in so much pain, cried bc this was so far from what i could imagine a nightmare would look like.  

i am now 4 weeks post partum and i was hospitalized for 12 days of that time due to the spinal headache i developed from the botched epidural.  on monday i go to a vascular neurologist to see why my mris have been abnormal and see if the botched epidural has now caused issues with my brain.  i missed out on so many moments with my baby due to this nightmare - i know this is a long post but i feel like it doesn't even scratch the surface of the reasons to stay away from
this hospital.  especially the head of anesthesiology.  

i never published this review and now i am almost 9 months out.  i am still dealing with the neurological effects of their huge mishap and i have thousands of dollars of bills rolling in for my baby's room and board.  they have their patient services lying in writing saying their care was extraordinary and helped (all lies!) - this place is an epic nightmare- please stay away.  no one deserves to have the first months of their new family life completely destroyed.

the medical system as a whole has issues that won't be taken care of with a simple fix, but if the right people are in charge and holding people accountable; i think they can all take steps toward improvement.

i had the unfortunate experience of working with a highly unethical psychologist named dr. lillian kaner yamamoto.

for 4 months i had worked with dr. lillian yamamoto. at the time, she was a resident working to gain her clinical hours towards licensure. dr. yamamoto was invalidating, disrespectful, sarcastic and would not create a treatment plan. for our 10 sessions, all she told me was to listen to music, play with my dog, and watch tv. at $166 per session, i was robbed. mediocre advice at premium prices. 

i spoke with her supervisor, dr. emily wile schiller, and she denied my request to work with someone else. she insisted i work things out with dr. yamamoto. i don't know why my request to change therapists was denied. kaiser policy states that members can change their provider at any time and for any reason. as a result of having my request denied, i was stuck working with dr. yamamoto.

dr. yamamoto resented me for talking to her supervisor. she falsified my medical records in petty retaliation. therapy notes are supposed to honestly capture what goes on in session. it is not a tool for getting back at a patient. she failed to be impartial.

when i read the notes, i felt betrayed, heartbroken, and felt the kaiser system had failed me. i had planned to end my life by jumping off an overpass. i was already depressed and this was the final push. i was put on a 5150 hold at another hospital for being a danger to myself. being hospitalized for 72 hours was scary. there were patients with severe mental illness. one patient tried to tackle me but failed since nurses intervened to protect me. i was sleep deprived and lost 13 pounds in those 3 days. 

when i was discharged from the hospital, i felt like a part of me was broken. my depression worsened and now i have a 5150 on my record. naturally, i was upset, and filed a grievance through member services and the board of psychology. the board did not have jurisdiction over residents, and so this means dr. yamamoto got a free pass for harming a patient. no consequences. member services spoke with kaiser leadership and dr. yamamoto. they found that my notes were jeopardized and told her to make corrections. even so, the damage was already done. member services also told me that she refused to apologize. horrible! she harms a patient and has no guilt or remorse? 

dr. yamamoto is now licensed and is working at kaiser oakland. i found out by chance when i called crisis for support. reception said "i'm going to transfer you to dr. yamamoto to help you." after what she did, kaiser thought it was appropriate to let her work with vulnerable patients? this is outrageous. dr. yamamoto is vindictive, malicious and most of all dangerous. if she could harm me without any remorse or consequence, other patients are at risk. 

i never got an apology, and kaiser psychiatry has condemned me for filing the complaint. i now have nightmares of the 5150 and ruminate on this injustice. i am now worse off having worked with dr. yamamoto. she chose the wrong profession. she has no desire to help patients. 

as a result of reporting dr. yamamoto, kaiser leadership has taken steps to deny care at various kaiser locations, including ones i have never been to. when i called kaiser oakland to schedule an appointment, reception hangs up the moment i give my medical record number. i managed to speak to the director, mr. tim barry lcsw. he explained that no one will work with me because i reported dr. yamamoto. when i reminded him of kaiser policy and how patients can file a grievance without fear of reprisal or interruption of treatment and services, he dismissed me and said to go somewhere else for treatment. when i brought up not getting an apology, mr. barry told me to "let it go. it's water under the bridge." what a callous remark. how could he say that? i find it odd how kaiser therapists went on strike advocating for patients to get better care and here they are denying me care for speaking up about mistreatment. they are hypocrites. member services has not helped either. 

the bottom line is if a kaiser provider mistreats you and you speak up about it, they will blackball and blacklist you. they would rather cover up their crimes than to help the patient who was harmed. therapists at kaiser locations i have never been to, such as oakland, are denying care. i have never stepped foot there. i don't even know where the psychiatry department is located and they are denying care.

my experience with tosh is through the physical therapy and pool therapy programs due to shoulder issues and previous spinal surgeries.

i have had nothing but positive experiences at tosh.  all of the pts i have seen have been very professional and knowledgeable, and relatively  easy to book with.  i am currently waiting to see a knee surgeon who is booking a month out, but he is apparently amazing and in high demand, so i'm ok with waiting.  front desk staff are always friendly.

something that tosh has that other clinics typically don't have is an olympic-sized pool. this has been excellent for my spinal surgery recovery. there are options to see a therapist in the pool, and after "graduating" from the therapist sessions, there is an option for an independent program.  lance is the exercise specialist (he rocks!!), and he is able to provide additional exercises to complement the routine from the therapists. you pay a monthly fee for the independent program, and it has been a lifesaver for me!  there are both morning and evening hours available, which works well for my work schedule.

my only complaint is how much the pt services cost.  a pool session with a therapist cost me $300 for an hour (with insurance), which is completely unaffordable.  a few years back, someone in the office told me that i should look into other offices because tosh charges so much more.  (the exception is the independent pool program, which is very affordable).  just something to keep in mind if you have a high deductible plan.

doc_text:
nothing in life is more irritating than when a billing dept. contacts you with a price that is significantly lower than the price presented to you from your healthcare insurance provider.  

prior to being rendering services at this location, i was contacted by billing and was presented with the amount of $738.72 as well as a request for payment.  mind you, this is before being rendered services; hence my insurance had not yet been billed.  aggravating, i know.

then, when i go check in, the same amount was listed in their system; and then after being rendered services, an estimate w/ that same amount was sent to me via usps; with a request for payment.  

meanwhile, i decided to go and check my claim through my healthcare insurance provider and i see an amount of $1,684 for the same services; as the amount of my deductible.  i call my insurance and inform them that i was presented with an amount that was less than 50% than the amount displayed on their portal; only to be told that that is the accurate amount that i will be responsible for.  so what happens next, you ask...

i file a grievance through my healthcare insurance and then contact the attorney general's office; even though i know deep down inside that not a damn thing is going to change what has happened.  i wait to hear back from either or; and below and behold i hear back from my healthcare insurance provider with the lame explanation of:  " in review of your grievance, i brought your case to the attention of a svh patient access operations director, who appreciated being made aware of your concern. the director stated that you were provided an estimate based off the cpt code that was going to be used during the procedure. the director stated that the estimate is subject to change if the provider in question uses a different service code (cpt code) or adds any services..."  

ok...let me start off by saying... that in the world of business, i have witnessed estimates being different by either 10-20%... and the differential is usually written on the estimate to let the customer know.  
in this case, the amount was over a 50% difference and nowhere was it listed that the amount could be significantly higher... also too, where it was an "estimate" then they truly had no flippin' business requesting payment in the first place.

seriously... the poor business displayed by the billing department is unbelievable and the fact that they can get away with, what other companies cannot, is repulsive.  i mean,  would you allow a company to bill you a price that is significantly higher than the price you were originally presented with?  would they not have to honor that lower price?

i thought so... 

so with all due respect, what makes this situation any different?  it may be the medical field, but it's still a business...and well the same rules should still have to apply... 

needless to say... i am not in the least bit impressed and if i have my way, i will be taking my medical needs elsewhere in the future.

i've been to medvet on a few occasions with my beloved furbaby 'abby'. 
i've been to the worthington location, as well as the hilliard location, and the hilliard location by far shines the brightest. 

i think it's really important to know that med vet is an emergency vet service. just as you would expect a large bill from a regular er for your own medical issues - such would be my expectations for med vet. if you feel you have an issue where your pet could wait until a check up with your vet, then you really should wait. it's $100 fee just for entering their doors. 

it was an early sunday morning - i knew my vet's office would not be open, so my only option knowing the inevitable was here was to take my abby to medvet. i won't post the entire story of my day, but just know that the staff there was caring and compassionate from start to end, which is all i would have expected even from my own vet's office. 

the staff gave us plenty of time to be with abby before euthanasia and were compassionate and sympathetic knowing that this process was both overwhelming for myself and my husband. up until the end and abby's last breath they made her comfortable and calm. 

they offered a few different options for handling the body. we went with their cremation option, and they also include keepsakes such as an ink paw print, clipping of fur & clay paw-print with their name printed in it. they outsource the cremation process, but the company that did handle it did a great job and got her ashes processed within a business day. 
 
there were so many tears that day, but the process was made easier knowing how compassionate the doctors and assistants were when handling pets. she was always treated well - even with minor injuries, or ailments when we had to visit the 1-3 times over her 11 year span. 

rip abby and thank-you medvet for caring and taking gingerly care of our old dog!

i wish i had the time to really explain my experience at henry mayo.  in july, i had a bad kidney infection and went against my gut instinct to go to cedars, and opted to go to henry mayo because it is closer.  i should have followed my gut instinct.  

their website said that the er had a five-minute wait.  

i was in the er for eight hours without a room, just stuck on a gurney in the hallway with no pain medicine (i was in excruciating pain), no care whatsoever, and had to be moved to another hallway at one point due to some loud and crazy criminal who was threatening patients (cops were everywhere).  it was a nightmare.

finally i was put into a room, and received pain medicine.  the nurses felt really bad for me, and that was appreciated.  the room was shared (unnecessary as they had many empty rooms) and my roommate wanted the room so hot i was dripping sweat.  the nurses called the room "the sauna" because it was so hot in there.  i begged them to turn down the temperature and every time they tried, she'd cry and beg them to turn it up because she was so cold (even with many blankets).  i am not a complainer, and not demanding in the slightest. she was very loud and very demanding.  so she won out.  they could have moved me into another room--that would have been great.  but no.  it was days of this...it was awful.  finally, i was ready to go home and because they didn't have the proper staff to release me (it was a friday and they are understaffed on the weekends), they wanted me to stay an extra 2.5 days because they would be back on monday.  

i could not deal with this for that long--besides, i did not want to overcharge my insurance company (that seemed like fraud to me), so i checked myself out ama.  they threatened that my insurance would not pay (this is blatantly not true).  they tried everything to scare me into staying.  my doctor even told me to go home.  they refused to talk to me once i signed on the dotted line, and would not even give me outprocessing papers.  i had to walk myself to my car.  fine with me.  the nurses were really pissed.  i found out later that they are audited based on number of amas, and they get dinged for each one.  i'm sorry for that, but maybe they should run a better business.

top all of that off with receiving a $1500 bill from the er doc--the doc i never saw.  turns out that, though the hospital is in my network, they hire out of network doctors for their er.  now i'm fighting with my insurance company, the doctor, and the hospital.  this is ridiculous.  this has happened to me before--getting an out of network doc in an er--and now i always ask if the doc is in my network.  if not, i won't see them and/or i'll go to another er.  i did this on this trip, and was told that he was in my network.  they lied.  he is not.  this is quite a racket, henry mayo--taking the people who need the care the most, who put their trust in you, and give them the bait-and-switch with out-of-network doctors who will bill as much as they want for their "care" (even if there is no care).

between the misleading information on their website for er wait times, the lack of care in the er, the hospital experience, ama experience, and final billing--this was a nightmare that i hope i can save you from.  skip it.  it's just not worth the convenience of "local".  

providence holy cross is not far from here--and it's a great hospital.  next time in the need of an er, i'll either go there or to cedars.  never again, henry mayo.

the wait time was outrageous and the staffs were unbelievably rude, also they lied to us trying to scare us into staying the night at the hospital.

i went to the er with my grandma this past sunday (12/15/19) because she was feeling really sick. we arrived at the hospital at 2:30p.m. and i was surprised there was only one other person in the waiting room. we were immediately called by the triage nurse after checking in. my encounter with that triage nurse was very unpleasant, and looking back i still can't believe how they could have someone this rude to work a position that requires so much communication with patients - when i met the nurse we immediately greeted her. she didn't greet us back and she asked us what languages we speak and i told her we speak english. while we were walking to her office she asked and i quote, "does anyone speak english? fluent english." i was like, "miss, didn't i already tell you i speak english. is my english not fluent enough?" and she somehow was offended and literally started yelling. ridiculous. i mean, why did she even have to ask? was she going to ask if i can speak fluent english with perfect grammar and american accent next? i decided to let it go and asked if we could just move on, but she refused to quite her yapping and babbling until after i have requested her to shut up and give my grandma the treatment three times.

after the triage nurse took my grandma's blood sample, we were sent to the emergency room at around 3:00 to wait for the doctor. a doctor soon came and told us they would check back one the blood test result came back. that was the last time i saw her. we didn't get any update until we were seen by a nurse at 6:30 who said my grandma was admitted to the hospital. i told her we were not staying, then she said my grandma's troponin was high which might lead to a heart attack, and that we should talk to the doctor if we refused the admission. a moment later the doctor came and i was on the phone with my cousin who is also a doctor. i let them talk and the doctor told my cousin a different story. she said the blood test result had not come back so they didn't know what happened, but she wanted to order another blood test to compare the results before we decided if we wanted to stay the night. my cousin told me later troponin doesn't cause heart attack, it should be the other way around and without the blood test result it would be impossible to tell my grandma's troponin was high. was the nurse just misinformed or was just downright lying to our faces? i'll let you be the judge. 

anyway we waited and waited but no one came to take my grandma's blood. it almost felt as if everyone's shift all ended at the same time and they all went home. at 8:30 a nurse who just started her shift finally came to draw the blood and i was told normally it would take 30 minutes for the test result to return. i couldn't help but wonder what happened with the first blood test that took forever to be processed. eventually my grandma was discharged at around 10. i guess i can understand why there were almost no one in the waiting room when we arrived.

we felt stuck at that point, because the stitches needed to be done within a certain time frame. after all of this, we to the front and get called back again-they decided to finally take vitals/check the blood pressure of the girl who fainted! they also said they needed to take do a cat scan of her head! at this point, we refused treatment to the tech and said we needed to see an md/physician. the ct tech said okay and said we could go back out front. over an hour later, we were called back so more blood could be drawn; i asked if there was something wrong with the first draw, and was told no- they simply have to draw blood for the particular test over a period of six hours. we inquired as to why this was necessary and where the doctor was and why this was all needed for some stitches! the np came and said she was waiting on the cat scan results before she did stitches. we asked her who was ordering all these tests, and we absolutely refuse to have a cat scan. she said the doctor ordered them and we'd have to sign a waiver saying we decline treatment. we said we would like to see the doctor who is ordering these tests, because why is he/she doing so without even seeing the patient. she said she was ordering on behalf of the doctor. we proceeded to sternly say we need to see a doctor, and her response was, "well i see patients all the time by myself." we replied that was fine but we need to see a doctor. in the meantime, she went back to her office and we heard her talking to the doctor on speakerphone who said that we did not need to sign anything, but simply make sure it was noted in the chart. after some time we were put in a room, and then waited for the doctor. 
the poor doctor came in a while later and was very sweet. i was ready to just have my sister receive treatment and leave, but my mother said it was important to tell/ask about what happened because other patients need protection to. i then went into detail of everything happened, and said i felt the chest x-ray was completely unnecessary, i was appalled that the blood pressure of a patient who came in because she fainted was taken after having a chest x ray, and the bedside manner and advanced terminology of the np (kim tarver) was unacceptable. very surprisingly, the doctor agreed. she professionally stated she agreed that the chest xray was unnecessary and my sister did not need a cat scan. she said the blood pressure thing was an outlier, but still needed to be noted...and she stated the terminology used was a personnel issue. after all this, she used liquid stitches (liquid skin) on my sister. she's good to go now, but it was an incredibly painful, unnecessary process.

i have been extremely sick for 2 days and knew i had the flu, so i called my doctor's office to see if they could call in a prescription for tamaflu for me. they said they dont do that, i would have to come in, and my regular doctor didnt have any openings so i had to see doctor dolan. fine. i will have my husband drive me and my 2 toddlers, who are all also sick but not as bad as me, to the appointment (because i am too sick to drive and we dont have a sitter).  so now we have 4 people sick with the flu in their waiting room. sounds great so far, right? way smarter than just calling in a prescription durning the middle of flu season, right? 

so the nurse calls me back, takes my vitals and swabs my nose for the flu virus. fine, whatever. then the doctor comes in and wants to know what i "want?". kind of weird thing to ask, but i tell her i think i have the flu and i would like tamaflu. she tells me i don't have a fever and i let her know i am taking dayquil religiously every 4 hours because i am very sick and it helps a little with the fevers. then she asks me how long i've had symptoms. i tell her and she says that's longer than 48 hours and they dont prescribe tamaflu after 48 hours. mind you, we are now at about 50 hours. i asked her why not, since i have read many times that tamaflu helps even if you start taking it after 48 hours. her answer was "it makes people nauseous". ok, i think that if that's your only concern you should let the patient make that decision. 

so after that conversation, dr. dolan says "your flu results will be done in a couple minutes". i told her i didnt see the point in waiting on the flu results because they wouldn't prescribe me medication anyway. all of the sudden she says that i might be a special case because i take steroids for an autoimmune disease that makes me more susceptible to pneumonia. 

at this point i'm wondering what's wrong with this woman. she goes on and on about how she wont give me tamaflu because it's been close 50 hours and it makes people nauseous, then literally her next sentence is telling me i'm a special case and i need to be on tamaflu.

anyway, she leaves for the lab results and guess what, i have flu type a. she gets my local pharmacy phone number to send over a prescription for tamaflu and i ask her for a prescription for cough medicine. she says they dont give prescriptions for that. fine. can you reccomend an over the counter cough medicine? "we reccomend a teaspoon of honey". i asked her to repeat herself because i was in disbelief. she repeated "a teaspoon of honey". listen lady, i already know you are a nut, but if you think i am getting up every 3 minutes in the night with coughing fits to eat a teaspoon of honey, not only will i not get any sleep but i will have diabetes by morning.

anyway, we head over to the pharmacy to pick up the tamaflu i had to suffer mind games at the hands of a doctor to get, and guess what. they didnt send my prescription to the pharmacy i specifically asked them too and gave them the number for. nope. they submitted it to my mail order pharmacy. so the kind people at the pharmacy called my doctor and told them to send over the prescription and cancel the order with the mail order pharmacy because my insurance wouldn't cover both. cool. except now i have to wait another half hour for my prescription. we wait a half hour, go back up, and they tell us my doctor cant seem to cancel my mail order prescription and they wont be able to do anything for me until the mail order is canceled. at this point i'm exhausted so we just leave.

as we get in the car to drive home my doctor's office calls to tell me what the pharmacy people already told me, that they sent the prescription to the wrong place and they were not able to fix it and i about lost my mind. they made a huge deal about how many hours i had been sick and didnt want to give me the medication, but then realized they should, but instead of sending it where they were supposed to, they sent it to mail order where it would take literally days to fill. i told them to cancel all the orders since "hours" seem to make a huge difference in efficacy. they had already wasted at least 2 additional hours at this point and i didnt even have the medicine yet. i just needed to rest and the stress was making me feel even worse.

done, right? nope, 2 hours later i get an email from the mail order pharmacy saying that my order will be delivered in 4 to 7 days. thanks dr. dolan and thanks to her super incompetent staff, i guess i will just wait and see if i get pneumonia.

oh, also, the staff at the doctor's office was apparently supposed to have me put on a mask so i wouldn't spread the flu virus to others in the waiting room with my horrible cough, and they didnt. doctor dolan told me that after she came into the examination room.

bye bye saint mary's! if this flu doesnt kill me i will be seeking care at another practice.

doc_text: our experience at the schneck er was awful.  we had an uncooperative, arrogant doctor by the name of dr. griffith.  he wanted to do a cat scan of my husband's throat to determine if the blockage was still present.  i asked him about the cost of a cat scan and he said around $2,000.00.  i asked about the price of a regular x-ray and he told me about $200.00.   i asked why a more expensive procedure was necessary and he told me that an x-ray would probably not show the obstruction (which we believed to be a chicken bone and he knew this). i asked how a cat scan worked and he told me it was a 3-d x-ray. he'd already told us that my husband would have to have his throat scoped to remove the blockage, so we wanted to know why either test was necessary.  he explained nothing.  he left my husband's room and ordered the cat scan,  proceeding with the expensive test which showed, wait for it.... nothing!    the man spent a total of 5 minutes with us and his bill was $1,300.00, more than the surgeon charged to scope my husband's throat.  we are under a self-pay insurance plan and part of our contract with them is that we get the best price possible for each service provided.  dr. griffith's office will not give us the cpt codes we must have for reimbursement.   we called the hospital administrator and complained about the unnecessary use and expense of the cat scan.  our complaint fell on deaf ears.  they did not care that we were fiscally exploited as self-pay patients. so, it looks like we'll have to eat the entire $1,300.00   once my husband was admitted, which was also unnecessary, the nurses were wonderful.  he also really liked his surgeon, dr. iwema.  she was compassionate and caring.  she even called the day after his procedure to check on his progress.  her bill was very reasonable and her office was wonderful to work with regarding the cpt codes necessary for reimbursement.  both she and the hospital did give us a self-pay discount.  the appropriate cooperation from the hospital and dr. iwema's office is the only reason this review received a three star rating.  the emergency room itself, would have received a zero.  always be your own advocate and never assume the hospital is working toward your best interest.  i know when you go to the er things are scary and you often aren't at your best, but these people will take advantage of your vulnerabilities.  we will never go back to the schneck er, but we will wind up at an er somewhere eventually, and when it happens, there will be a better result.

ok lets be straight- i'm a big girl. i've struggled with my weight my whole life. 
i'm also narcoleptic, and have fought a battle with depression and anxiety since i was 10. are these things an issue? yep. do they define me and explain every issue without an obvious answer? no, they do not. 

unless, of course, i am an in-patient at abrazo central campus.

the first doctor i met was called "dr. d." the first thing to roll out of his mouth upon meeting me was "have you considered gastric bypass surgery?" no hello? the second thing was "are you diabetic?" diabetes was a natural first question, as i was there because neuropathy in my feet was spreading alarmingly fast up both my legs.

something to rule out for sure, but folks, i am not diabetic. 

not if abrazo staff pokes me every 6 hrs for 2 days, not if the dr orders 2 different blood tests, not if he adds insulin to my prn list while neglecting my actual prescriptions, not by the hair of my chinny chin chin! 
so whats next?

oh awesome, here comes the neurologist. a gallon or two of my blood was taken for testing, a spinal tap and mri were ordered. 

the spinal tap was, of course, terrifying. one of my symptoms was spontaneous involuntary muscle spasms and they wanted to put a giant needle in my spine that could paralyze me if i moved! 
i had a panic attack. i have already admitted that i have anxiety. but wouldn't you call that a reasonable fear? 

now, looking over the paperwork, i see references to my anxiety all over the place as a poor explanation for their failure to find the reason for the neuropathy

but back to the fat prejudice, as that is my theme.
 
when i was admitted, i was starving. i had spent hours in the er before being transferred to the hospital. i had only expected to spend a few hours at the er and for them to do whatever they do and send me home.
so i asked for a sandwich. 3 hours and multiple ignored requests passed between me and that sandwich. it was one of those little elementary school sized ones with one slice of mystery meat, a slice of cheese, and two pieces of bread cut in a diagonal. 

i ate it thankfully. an hour later, i was still hungry and asked if there was somewhere i could get some food. perhaps a vending machine? they put me off a couple more hours and served me fat shame with my second sandwich. 

then, when i was sitting up in bed in the middle of the night (as i do multiple times a night, part of the narcolepsy) the nurse walking by stopped and asked, "your not eating again, are you?" with a horrified expression on his face. 

time for the mri came, and the tech walked in, looked at me, and walked back out into the hall. he announced that i was too fat for the machine several times using different descriptors. he was ordered to try anyways. yep, i heard all of it. i'm sure the neighboring rooms did too. 

he left, and came back with the biggest wheelchair i have ever seen. 
i told him i had heard him in the hall, and he did look genuinely embarrassed and apologetic, so i dropped it.  it turns out that i did fit, but it was so snug that we decided it would be better to wait for a machine that was 70 inches rather than the one there that was 60. 

so yeah, he was pretty much right. 

but my complaint is about a complete and widespread attitude of prejudice and lack of tact because of my weight. 

i am also concerned about the fact that we, the patients, could hear everything the staff was saying to each other in the hallway. i can tell you exactly what was wrong with the people on either side of me and not because i was trying to listen. i think its unprofessional. 

i have a lot of other complaints too.... but i'll just leave it at that.

well, that and that my symptoms have not resolved, an explanation has not been found, and now i have a giant bill for labs that nobody bothered to interpret, and that i can only pray the insurance company will cover most of. 
the list is a few pages long. i may have been tested for bubonic plague, i haven't made it through the whole list yet.

if you are planning a visit to an abrazo er, do a quick check first. can you see your feet while standing up? 

if not, you might want to chose a different er.

warning: this is long and probably tmi but whatever!

this review is for the walk-in/urgent care clinic. i was told at the ward clinic the wait would be 45 minutes there so i called here and the receptionist said that she couldn't promise anything but at the moment there was only one patient and two doctors. i was in a bit of pain so decided to come here instead. 

i wasn't aware the main hospital had a walk-in clinic, but the receptionist at ward was very helpful in explaining where to find it, and that we should park in the main hospital garage.

so fyi, the walk-in clinic is in the strode building to the right as you're looking at the entrance from king street. my husband dropped me off at the patient dropoff area so that i could go to the clinic while he parked, and there were plentiful signs for the strode building. it's located just past the pharmacy, and you go through a walkway to get to it. 

the super helpful receptionist quickly took my info and immediately provided me with a cup for a urine sample. i provided it, and it took about 10-15 minutes before they called me back to see the doctor.

based on previous experience, i thought it was a kidney infection or kidney stone - but i wanted to rule out appendicitis because two of my sisters had to have surgery for it, one of them just a month ago.

after hearing my symptoms, dr. susie chun didn't think it was appendicitis and ordered an ultrasound to check my right kidney, where the pain was. we then went to radiology, which is in the main building, second floor. the receptionist and techs were also friendly and helpful there; btw it's super freezing in there, so they provide warm blankets in a metal heater at the back, against the wall. note: you open the heater by pulling on the right side of the door, not the left. watched a couple of people struggle to open it before realizing what side to open. also, for an ultrasound, you must have a full bladder. because i emptied mine to provide a sample at intake, i had to drink several cups and wait about 20 minutes before they could do the procedure.

after the ultrasound, we went back to the clinic, where dr. chun said it showed slight inflammation to my kidney. she didn't want to have me go straight to a ct scan since it involves radiation, but with the ultrasound results she thought it best to confirm with a ct scan. so i went back to radiology, where they were just as nice the second time, and did the procedure quickly.

back at the clinic again, and dr. chun confirmed the kidney stone, showing me the imaging of one in my kidney (wasn't causing the pain) and one in my ureter (that was the culprit). it wasn't large enough to require surgery so she prescribed a medication to help me pass that sucker and i could go home. all in all it took about three hours, but the pain had eased and i was so relieved,  i could be patient with all the tests. 

everyone at both clinics were so helpful and friendly, from the receptionists to the nurses to dr. chun. it was a fairly slow saturday so maybe that made for a better experience since no one was rushed dealing with a ton of patients, but i appreciated the warmth and care i received today. it made a very uncomfortable experience much easier to bear.

plainview hospital er - go elsewhere

horrible. charge nurse "colette" was disgusting, rude, & horrible to my mother who was there advocating for me. i was seen on 3/11/20 for severe abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting which had progressively worsened for 5 days, 2 weeks after iud paragard  placement. i was seen this past sunday 3/8/20 at citymd who determined infection & started me on antibiotics. upon arrival to plainview hospital er they ran some tests which indicated fluid accumulation outside of the uterine tissue & again, infection. they also identified very high levels of eosinophils, indicative of allergic reaction, likely to the copper in the iud poisoning me from the inside. they hap-hazardly switched my antibiotic after about 10 hours of waiting. i was sent home with fever, severe abdominal pain, and throwing up. i repeat; discharged with a fever and throwing up on the way out the door.  i was there through lunch & dinner, but was only offered a mini can of ginger-ale despite all testing being completed before the dinner cart came around. 

that evening, the vomiting and pain became worse. i felt as though i was going to die of sepsis. i returned to plainview hospital er on 3/12/20 for severe pain, continued vomiting, fever, and now dizziness & confusion. i was provided a room with fresh blood on the fitted sheet after about 2 hours of waiting in triage. the nurses response "do you want me to change the bed linen?". after i insisted that it be changed, the nurse drew my blood, which again showed infection. after about another 2 hours of waiting to be seen by the doctor, he told to go home & follow up with gyn which was a pre-scheduled appointment with the wrong information on it. the doctor's name had been switched with another doctor, and the address was inaccurate. while we waited in limbo, my mother called to confirm this appointment scheduled for tomorrow, 3/13/20. the office had no record of me scheduled to come in, and denied speaking with plainview hospital er in coordination of services. the most pathetic of all was plainview hospital er's reasoning to send me home; they have no ob-gyn able to come to the hospital, nor competent enough doctors in-house to perform an iud removal at plainview hospital er (which was actually placed by a nurse at time of insertion). in the charge nurse colette's words, an iud causing such severe symptoms & infection was "not an emergency". i could not walk out to the pickup area due to such severe pain, vomiting, and dizziness. i passed out during removal of the saline iv drip, then began again vomiting. the nurses response "someone get a wheelchair to wheel her out".  i was given a vomit bag & wheeled out to the pickup area, shaking in pain. i am 25, excellent health, no prior medical issues. i live an active lifestyle, i am an avid skier & scuba diver. i was not seen for an injured leg, or as an elderly adult. i was seen for severe abdominal pain. to be in such severe pain warranting full body shaking, low bp, dizziness, & inability to walk; there is clearly an issue. i walked into this hospital. for a nurse to send someone who cannot walk out, worse than on arrival, is disgusting & negligent.  their excuse; "this is a community hospital, we can't help you". i work in a community hospital also owned by northwell health. the staff that i work with would never treat a patient or a patient family member like that. it was absolute negligence. 2 days wasted & infection worsening, but they "could not help" as "it is not an emergency".

and to make matters worse, the staff have zero concern for hippa or patient privacy. they sent an elderly woman with a broken eye socket having zero memory recollection in the bed next to me home too, after asking her about her iud removal. when she appeared confused & her family denied her having an iud, the nurse stated "oh right that is the patient in bed a". are you kidding me. not only did they clearly confuse myself with her, but they humiliated me in front of several of her family members present & violated my hippa rights. 

moral of the story; i guess the staff's operational definition of "emergency" only caters to certain populations. women's health & elderly health is neglected. stay away.

i really expected better from penn medicine, which has given me exceptional care and service in every other specialty.  take my review with a grain of salt:  i came here for six weeks immediately following surgery on my acl and medial meniscus.  i would wager that even the pts themselves would not consider this to be the best facility for this kind of injury; the focus seems to be patients with parkinson's or huntington's.  

i found the equipment and overall space to be antiquated.  no elliptical, no stairmaster, and a single treadmill with insufficient shock absorption.  the staff is constantly juggling multiple patients, precluding one-on-one attention.  i would be given an exercise, and then my pt or her assistant would tend to another patient or go back to her laptop.  my form was rarely corrected, and there seemed to be a disconnect between my pt's approach compared to her assistant's.  appointments lasted about 30 to 45 minutes, and no manual work such as stretching or massage was offered.  this was not unlike my experience at rothman four years ago, when i went for bilateral gluteal tendinitis from running.  unfortunately, this business model has become the norm for physical therapy, but not all places have to be this way. 

if you're young, active, and want to be challenged, i cannot stress how much better zarett rehab and fitness is.  they provide a personalized experience that feels not only like a medical appointment, but like getting personal training in a state-of-the-art facility followed by an expert massage and stretch.  after my first appointment at zarett, i felt refreshed and was more flexible and able to walk with less pain.

patients regularly fight one another and staff once again do nothing about it. they're completely useless for the field they signed up for. 

a woman around her mid twenties fell into a seizure right in front of me and the staff didn't realize it until the other patients alerted them. patients aren't told anything for hours upon hours and are left there without being properly updated on the process of getting them discharged or into a room. there's only a limited number of beds, which are usually all taken up, and you have no choice but to lay or sit on a cold hard surface. patients regularly piss on the floors in front of others, it's ignored. 
there's a clear pattern here of things being ignored they simply shouldn't be. 

there's no cushions or anything to give you some semblance of comfort except for the limited number of beds. 
they do not care. they really don't seem to have any empathy whatsoever. 

let's get to the ward part..

there was never enough water to drink. i was severely dehydrated to a point they couldn't draw blood from me for days. 

they make you bathe like an animal in showers that only stay on for, no joke, 5 seconds at a time. you have to keep pressing the button every 5 seconds to keep the water going. no counters or toilet in the shower area, so everything you brought in with you got soaked. even your clean clothes and towels. it was just one single small room you got to bathe in. 

one night they completely "forgot" to feed me and i was physically sick from not eating/drinking enough for so long.

you also never saw the same doctor more than once, they sporadically just disappear mid conversation, these "professionals" are never on the same page with each other. one doctor said they were thinking about holding me longer, then she just leaves without saying anything else. literally never saw her again. she left the unit. she caused a huge, unnecessary meltdown for me that night i'll never forget. (don't worry, all that was ignored too!)

there's no group activities, no counselors to talk to, not enough snacks left out at any given time, i had to hoard food in my room to make sure i had enough to make my meds work.

if you don't have enough staff or funding to operate this place and give those who are at the lowest point of their lives any sort of compassion or empathy, do buffalo a favor and cease to operate. 

you're doing much more harm than good and should be investigated. 

this is my final warning, do not go here. seek alternative mental health help. anything is better than buffalo ecmc.

do not bring family here. my aunt who was dying with stage 4 cancer was in the emergency for 3+ hours without any help because they "couldn't find the bloodwork results" and it was because of the staff's negligence. they took the blood and left the vials on the counter in my aunt's er room for over 3 hours! once i brought this to their attention they profusely apologized and tried to gaslight us into understanding there's a lot of patients in the emergency-- that does not excuse your negligent behavior. we moved her to another hospital.

unfortunately my grandfather was taken to this hospital by ambulance when he had pneumonia. he was under the care of palliative dr. cortez during his recovery with pneumonia. and dr. cortez lacked complete emotional awareness, professionalism, and had terrible bed-side manner.

he gave my grandfather a death sentence which turned out to be a false alarm and caused my family to experience unnecessary emotional turmoil and trauma. this all could have been avoided if he had taken the time to first get the full results of my grandfather's condition instead of making assumptions and condescendingly demanding we hold a conference to have my family decide between hospice and a feeding tube causing my family extreme emotional distress before my grandfather even took the swallow test recommended by the speech therapist.

we spent days grieving and mourning and had to plan a really difficult family dinner to make a decision between hospice and a feeding tube because dr. cortez made it clear that my grandfather wouldn't be swallowing food and his body was preparing for death by his weight even without conclusive results yet from the speech therapist. dr. cortez assumed because of my grandfather's bmi he was dying, although i explained he had swallowed fine prior to coming in for pneumonia and has always been a small petite guy his entire life. dr. cortez did not hear me at all.

my grandfather passed the swallow test and did great. and when dr. cortez came into my grandfather's room the next morning to tell us that my grandfather passed, he said, "he did great, but let's see if he actually eats!" which i felt was extremely cynical and negative. dr. cortez's attitude and lack of empathy causes families to have to endure even more emotional distress and negativity when they are already facing a really traumatic time having a loved one in the hospital.

this was after my grandfather had already eaten two meals at the hospital which dr. cortez could have checked on prior to making his assumption about if my grandfather eats. he then proceeded to say that if my grandfather continues to eat, he does not need hospice care, which he is eating and is doing well at his new nursing home.

this entire ordeal was rather infuriating to have gone through and we felt it could have been completely avoided had dr. cortez taken the time to wait for the results and gotten the proper information or at least had better emotional awareness because these are actual people's lives, family members, not just numbers or diagnosis-- actual people. and especially considering he works in a very sensitive field. just because most cases of palliative care turn out to be end-of-life, doesn't mean each individual patient shouldn't be looked at on a case-by-case basis as a person but with assumptions.

his bed-side manner was also horrible. i was sitting in my grandfather's hospital room while dr. cortez was at the nurses station ranting about another family to the staff. he literally said, "it's unfortunate that family just can't come to terms with reality." it's not appropriate at all to judge how a family or anyone handles a traumatic experience especially one so emotionally sensitive as end-of-life, and i feel it's even less appropriate to be ranting about other patients and families in a space where others can hear you. it's extremely unprofessional and something should be done about this type of unprofessional behavior.

again, please please please don't bring your loved ones here.

my father went to kindred after a week in desert springs for treatment of a foot infection. he died there on tuesday morning, january 28. the issue with kindred that i will discuss here has to do with what happened after his death.

or does it?

the afternoon he died, i received a call from someone at kindred, a woman whose name i didn't get, who told me that they had found a shaver in cleaning his room. i said i'd come by to get it the next day if that was all right. she said yes, it would be left on the cart the nurses used (it has everything from a computer to gloves and the like) in the hallway where his room had been.

the next day i went by and went up to the nurse, who i did not recognize (the nurses do not always work only the same hallway, which is not the point here anyway) and explained that my father had been in that hallway and they had left a razor (i should have said shaver) on her cart. she checked a couple of places on it and said it wasn't there, and said i should check at the nurses' station. i went there and said what had happened. they asked who had called. i said i didn't know. they looked around and couldn't find it.

the nurse practitioner walked by. i thought i'd ask her, and did. she asked who had called. i said i didn't know. she asked if it was a man or a woman. i said a woman. she said that narrowed it down. she sent someone to check in a nearby room, where, i guess, they put laundry and that sort of thing. the person came back to say they hadn't found anything. she then thought maybe the social worker could help and i headed for her office.

she came out and offered condolences on my father's death. i thanked her and told her someone had called me the day before that they had found a shaver, it would be on the nurse's cart, it wasn't there, and we were looking for it. she said, "who called you?" i said, "i don't know." she said, "was it a man or a woman?" i said a woman. she said that narrowed it down and then said, "i need to look into this for a few minutes, so can you wait?"

i'd had it. i said, no, i could not wait, i had funeral arrangements to attend to, that they had the address, they could send it if they found it,  that i found this whole thing offensive, and i left.

over the next few days, i called back the number that had called me a couple of times and got no answer. on saturday, someone answered that number. i told her what had happened and she said the number probably belonged to a social worker, though she wasn't sure she was in her office at that moment, and she would transfer me. she did so. i got a voicemail and left a message. ten days later, i have not heard back.

the shaver was not important (it had no sentimental value, although it was my backup, and i'd brought it in for my father to use--but did they know that? of course not). nor is it the issue here. the issue is how kindred handled this situation and dealt with me, including not even having the courtesy to call me back after i left a message, or to apologize.

does this mean i question kindred's medical care for my father? well, what would you do? would you have faith in kindred as a hospital when its staff, many of whom i found to be quite nice when my father was there, cannot even do something like this right? all i can suggest is that if someone suggests kindred hospital to you, run the other way. your life may depend on it.

by chance this year the doctor's ekg had an "blip", nothing crazy, but his primary doc decided to let a cardiologist look at the doctor. the cardiologist scheduled a nuclear stress test on valentine's day and immediately checked him into the hospital based on his stress test.  so instead of eating chocolate cake and drinking champagne we were in the hospital.

on feb. 25, 2020, the doctor went in for a triple bypass at evanston hospital. there was 100% blockage in two areas and 90% in another area. there was absolutely no indication that there was anything wrong as he didn't exhibit any of the common symptoms (fatigue, shortness of breath, chest/jaw/arm pain, water retention, etc.).

the procedure went smoothly with no complications. he had an amazing surgeon who rocked that procedure. his surgeon was very pleased with the process and said he could see an immediate improvement in brian's heart function. he was in icu for 24 hours, then in a private room and they had him up and moving right away once the tubes came out.

fast forward to today. he is home and doing well. to look at him, you would never know that he had major surgery this past tuesday. he still has a long way to go in healing, but he looks great. i was concerned about a possible personality change as i have read papers about that...hell look at bill clinton. but the doctor is still the guy that went in before getting cut :-) 

i am giving major props to this hospital.  from the time we checked into the emergency room to the day of the surgical procedure, the staff was amazing!  customer service skills were off the chart!  the nurses, pas, housekeeping, food service, transporters, the staff where the angiogram was done, the people working in the cafeteria, etc. were all so nice.  i am saying for the record this was not a fluke,  the doctor was initally in the hospital from 2/14 to 2/20 as they were trying to figure out the best course of action for him, then 2/25 to 2/29 for the surgery.  i was at the hospital every day from early morning to late at night to be with the doctor.  everyone was friendly and seemed to genuinely care...great bedside manners, even the intern chaplin.  i had no idea that hospital chaplins did internships!  during the surgery, a nurse called me every two hours to update me on the doctor's progress.  at one point i was on a conference call on my work phone and missed a call from the nurse on my personal phone.  she called the receptionist at the desk in the waiting area and had them look for me so i could get the update from the desk phone,

i wanted to be there with the doctor every day and had no problem getting him ice water when needed it, but the nurses were constantly telling me to call them for that as they would take care of it, even if i needed water.  i just felt like i was capable of getting that for my lil man to free them up for more medical stuff.

i hope none of you ever need heart surgery, but if you do, ask for hyde russell for your surgeon.  he was amazing, but most important, he was very personable.  when he talked to us prior to the procedure, he was reassuring and comforting.  after the procedure, he came out to tell me how it went and it honestly felt like he was happy the doctor did so well.  his delivery of the news felt like he was happy how things went, not that he was this great surgeon who played god and save my husband.  he stopped by every day that we were there to check on the doctor's progress and to give us time to ask questions.  he didn't look at his watch, he didn't rush us because we loooove to talk things through (that is the engineer in him and chemist in me).

and i hope none of my yelp folks in the chicago-land area never need to go to the hospital, but if you do, this is the place to go.

you may ask, why one star rating?  

the good:  

1.  the staff is very friendly and attentive with great attitudes.  they really try to provide good customer and family service.  

2.  small facility-73 beds

3.  the facility is clean with no gross  or "old people"  smells of urine or feces.  

4.  aesthetically, the facility looks well maintained.

5.  issues brought to the attention of staff are immediately addressed; except for the middle of the night, unauthorized room charge (read below).  

the bad:

1.   this is a kaiser-contracted facility and as such it appears to have very little oversight once the patient is transferred.  

2.  this is a for-profit facility and it is clear by the available equipment and amenities that making money is the bottom line.

3. below standard rating in health inspection (2 out of 5 stars) is accurate.  this primarily has to do with quality of care.  specifically, shoreline has a lower percentage of short-stay residents who improved their ability to move around on their own compared (59.5%) to averages for california (67.5%) and nationally (67.5%).  the higher the % the better.

another rating that his bothersome is the percentage of short-stay residents who were re-hospitalized after a nursing home admission (30.1%) versus california (21.1%) and national average (21.1%).  lower percentages are better.

4.  it's been 24 hours since admission and we (the family) has not been contacted to schedule a meeting to develop an appropriate treatment plan.

5.  the discharge and treatments plans have not been followed.  

6.  it's very noisy because most rooms have 3 patients in a very small room.

7. my loved one was moved from a 2 patient per room to a 3 patient per room without our knowledge or consent in the middle of the night.  clearly, a medicare violation.  issue still not resolved.

if you or a loved one is admitted to a nursing home or rehabilitation facility, make sure you familiarize yourself with the following information about your rights:

https://www.medicare.gov/pubs/pdf/02174-nursing-home-other-long-term-services.pdf#page32

and

https://downloads.cms.gov/medicare/your_resident_rights_and_protections_section.pdf

also, make sure you look up the rating and violations report for the facility you are considering.  at www.medicare.gov.

shoreline's report is located at:

https://www.medicare.gov/pubs/pdf/02174-nursing-home-other-long-term-services.pdf#page32

also, if you have complaints find the ombudsman for nursing facilities at:  

https://www.medicare.gov/pubs/pdf/02174-nursing-home-other-long-term-services.pdf#page32

lastly, if you are like me and are a part of the "sandwich generation" (caregiver for both your parents and your children at the same time) it will be important to file for family leave to protect your right to care for a loved one without fear of losing your job.  
here's more information about fmla:

https://www.dol.gov/whd/fmla/

knowledge is power!!

given what we have experienced in just 24hours i really believe this facility is a mismatch for thetype of facility and the level of care needed for my loved one.  i will be strongly advocating (demanding) for her immediate transfer.  


update:  i was notified by the licensing agency the kaiser physician and his case manager were terminated!  that's the best thing that can happen to shoreline!

my 92-year old grandfather was admitted directly from st.jude er due to insurance reasons on 12/30/19. it is definitely not one of the nicer hospitals. but i do think the staff here does an amazing job, the nurses in particular. he initially got admitted to dou in the middle of the night, during which grace (almost positive that was her name) was the admitting nurse. i was not present but i was on the phone with her during the entire intake process since my parents speak minimal english. i could clearly tell she was incredibly patient and caring, thoroughly explaining every level of dnr and expressing her concern for blood in his urine seen in the foley bag. she ensured that his pain was controlled from the foley insertion (which was immense), not treating him like a drug seeking patient. 

the next day he was transferred to med-surg 3rd floor, stella (daytime) as his nurse for the next 2 days. she likewise provided exceptional service, tending to all his/our needs in a very prompt manner. she consistently went above and beyond, not hesitating to call physicians and inpatient pharmacy to obtain orders, inquire about starting his new chemo meds, verifying home meds, etc. 

the last nurse i encountered was chona up until his discharge (1/4). i did not have too much interaction with her but according to my sister, she was also very kind to make sure that he was able to be discharged home with enough supplies before home health nurse can visit. 

shift manager (unfortunately don't remember her name) was also diligent in consulting case management when we expressed our concern for discharging without having a follow-up with a urologist and oncologist, given he newly had a foley catheter and a nephrostomy tube, although the doctors were basically telling him to just follow up with the primary doctor to get referred to a urologist. i knew for a fact that it often takes months to  see a specialist through primary md referral. case management did an amazing job of securing an appointment with an oncologist, urologist, and even home health within a day. thanks to them we were able to take him home, knowing he will have adequate follow up with the doctors and professional care for his foley and nephrostomy tube dressing changes at home. 

we were less impressed by the physicians but everyone else sort of made up for it. maybe it's because i'm an inpatient pharmacist and knew to demand the right things to the right people, but they really did deliver. and even though i deal with nurses everyday, being on the other side as  patient's family, i realized so much respect and gratitude for all the nurses who genuinely care for their patients.
