the er, with breathtaking negligence, almost killed me. i'd wanted to write the administration at the time but was experiencing a major illness so could not. another recent reviewer stated the er's decline has been recent but no, this happened back in mid august 2014, so it's been going on a long time. so im writing yelp, at this point im sure the administration is well aware of their own problems, my letter i'm confident would have fallen on deaf ears anyway 

   i had a large tablet lodge in my throat at home when i tried to swallow it, and barely had an airway. it was like trying to breathe through a coffee swizzle stick.  i was losing oxygen, and seeing glimmering floaters in my vision and couldn't feel my fingertips. and was starting to pass out. luckily i am an rn myself and am very good at handling emergency situations, and through the grace of god, managed to keep a cool head. 

  i knew i didn't have time to wait for an ambulance, and after failed self heimlich attempts, signaled my friend with my hands to grab her car to drive me directly to the er. as i was reflexively trying to cough and breathe, the tablet shifted to a spot where it completely blocked my airway, and i fell to all fours and almost passed out in the driveway. luckily it shifted back to the "swizzle stick" position, but then just continued to alternate between swizzle stick and complete obstruction. 

  "fortunately " i made it to the er. my friend drove straight up to the front of the building and burst through the doors with me in tow, explaining that i was choking and didn't have an airway. 

   i was handed a clipboard, "please fill out this paperwork (asking for name, address, insurance info etc)."  i desperately wrote "cant breathe - pill" in jagged, panicked handwriting and pointed (as in "please let me go there") to the er patient area behind her.  "no, we can't help you until you fill out the paperwork."

  at this point an rn walked behind the desk, and i showed him my note, and pointed to the door that lead into the patient area with the most imploring look of my life, and he begrudgingly let me in. 

  he told me he was going to take me to a room and let me wait there.  afraid to be left alone and knowing i needed immediate attention or could die, i grabbed his upper arm. i didn't think it was too tight, just really really scared and urgent. he immediately spun on his heels and reprimanded me like a 4 yr old, "no no no! do not touch me like that, or i won't be able to help you. you are still breathing mam, you can wait until we're ready for you." 

  i tried one more note in the presence of an aide, who looked at me pie eyed because he got what was happening. but he was too low on the totem pole, and his own attempt to say anything to the additional nursing staff outside was ineffective, and i was left alone. 

  realizing that the only thing that was going to get them to respond was my impending cyanotic collapse, i decided to try and help my own self one last time (because even at that point, by the time they perked up and eventually intubated me - if they could even handle that - i would have sustained permanent anoxic brain damage, if i survived it at all). all by myself, i found an empty gurney. the guard rails were at a better height apparently than the chair i used at home, and after another round of heimlich attempts, the tablet flew out (along with blood - the tablet was a prescribed digestive enzyme, and after such an extended amount of time, had started to dissolve and "digest" my throat). 

  their response still blows my mind. day 1 of nursing school, we're taught our "abc's", where "a" stands for "airway", the number one thing in need of protection to keep someone alive. for pete's sake, 16 yr old lifeguards are taught this. 

   shaken, the anger now starting to kick in now that i wasn't wholly absorbed with saving my own life, i walked straight back out of the double doors.  "i'm leaving now, it's out - thanks for nothing!!!!" as the nurses' station, full of qualified staff standing behind the counters doing god knows what, looked back at me with slightly confused but mainly empty, "just another day" stares. 

   i shudder at the number of people that must have died at this er's hands. i think of all the poor family members who have been told, "i'm sorry, we did all we could."  so i'm writing this yelp review to let you know - they didn't.  avoid this er at all costs.

*** edit: in case this makes a difference, i did also write in my note to the multiple staff "airway obstructing". i couldn't have been any clearer. from one er rn to another, what was happening was virtually mapped out to them in written form, since they couldn't see, or refused to see, what was happening in front of their own eyes

it's hard to put an exact star rating. every medical facility has its good and bad. but my two stars are a reflection that if i had time on my side and another choice of a medical provider, would i choose dominican? no. why?

my mom was rushed here. while the er care got my mom forwarded to icu where she belonged, they didn't explain to my sister what a dnr was. my sister was hysterical and passed over the care to me. i lifted the dnr because we didn't know yet what was going on and she deserved to be revived (if she coded) and time to be diagnosed.they need to explain legal definitions to people when they are making these kind of decisions.

the icu was a dream team. every single one of her nurses, if we weren't in a pandemic where i can't go in the hospital, i'd give them all hugs for their a+ care and compassion. dr. singh soon became my favorite doctor ever. he got to know who my mom is. he listened. he respected us. he's the guy you'd trust with your life because he's trustworthy by going above and beyond with earning it.  even specialist that we interacted with in the icu was just top notch. 

so why the low rating? once we had her moved to telemetry, the hospitalist was abusive screaming at me instead of giving facts or letting me check with the experts that i needed to verify risk versus reward in what was being requested. i fired her. then i got the grim reaper dr. binesh. he spoke fatalistically and pushed hospice on us when we didn't have a terminal diagnosis. when we said we didn't want it, he also sped up discharge to less than 24 hours but notified us on a saturday evening when we couldn't get in home care set up because it was after business hours. i had expressed to them that my mom's wishes was after she was stable enough, her transition goal was to be cared for at home. when my mom was able to talk she told the doctor that she wanted to go home as her next step. so why weren't they helping us?

hospice would get preferential treatment with a magic extension to allow her to stay in the hospital if they took the case,  but we weren't allowed to have an extension to set her up at home with a home health care company outside of hospice. without a terminal diagnosis, isn't that medicare fraud if you engage hospice? we didn't go that route because it wasn't applicable or part of our goal to let our mom go when she was still recovering and we didn't know what was going happen next.  

what happened felt unehtical and like medical blackmail. our only other option was to contest it with medicare and be on the hook for the bill for that time in the hospital past the premature discharge. so now she's in rehab (against her wishes but our best option under these circumstances) until we can get home health care set up because any money that we do have should be reserved for making her better, not fighting the grim reaper and his games. 

they never notified us that they were transitioning her meds from iv to oral. they are supposed to notify you as soon as possible to discuss discharge so you have time to plan. that wasn't done. it would be one thing if she's magically better and could walk out.  she's not ambulatory, can't feed herself, requires meds, still not all coherent, requires aids, nurses, physical therapy, occupational therapy and meds to sustain her. it is pretty heartless to push her out that fast and not give the family time to discuss decisions, find a nursing organization, medical equipment and assist us with setting up support. they passed the buck. unless we chose hospice. no seriously, what's up with that? do they get a commission or something for patient referrals? (shakes head)

i'm happy that she's out of there. when you have a few rotten apples, it spoils it for the bunch. what we went through was extra hard because there are precautions that no one enters the hospital.i appreciate that. i had to advocate over the phone with limited time, limited information. they could have taken extra time or found a way to better share her chart or scheduled extra time to allow the medical advocate to absorb information and get back to them,  and/or not freaked out when you request a consult from a specialist where the risk is to make the best decision possible. even the discharge nurse said get back to me. i said i'd call her right back and she didn't tell me that it was the end of her shift that she was going home. i couldn't get a hold of her and it was someone else on shift the next day. what's wrong with these people? seriously, i hope someone treats them the way that they treat others some day so that they get a taste of their own medicine. 

your name is dignity health. the icu lives up to that name but there are other parts of the hospital that definitely need fixing.

this review is for the birthing center at sequoia hospital. like several other yelpers here, i too, had a wonderful experience delivering my baby at the birthing center a few weeks ago.

leading up to the birth, sequoia gave us all the information we needed. we attended a helpful orientation one month before the birth, and pre-registered ourselves so the hospital knew our due date and when to generally expect us. 

i began labor two days past due, and gave sequoia a call at 2am to let them know that i thought i was in labor. they were clear, calm, and provided instructions on coming to the hospital, where to park, etc. 

as soon as we got to the hospital, we were greeted and they had very short paperwork for me ready. after a few quick forms, they got me into a room and checked out a few things. once it was confirmed that i needed to stay, they got me settled into the room and we finished up the paperwork.

i'll spare readers my long birth story, but the major takeaways were-- sequoia has amazing nurses. literally, the best. i was at the hospital for a total of 96 hours and had several different nurses (they work in shifts of 12 hours each). each nurse was extremely well trained and highly competent in their respective area. i felt very well taken care of and appreciate that each nurse that clocked in took the time to read my birth plan and get familiar with my wishes. a special shout out to nurse ute who was my nurse during delivery. after a long and frustrating time laboring slowly, ute started her shift by instilling the confidence in me to have a baby that day. sure enough, my baby was delivered just as ute's shift was ending... and she stayed with me the whole time i was in labor.

sequoia also has fantastic doctors. my regular obgyn was out of the office during my delivery, but the other on-call doctors, dr. kassis (who delivered my baby and was super encouraging) and dr. rao, were absolutely fantastic. the anesthesiologist, dr. bradley, was also extremely skilled and delivered my epidural quickly and efficiently.

lastly, sequoia gave me everything i needed to take care of myself and my baby when i got home. as a first time mother, i had no idea what i needed to take care of myself. in the blur of labor, i didn't realize that sequoia had packed several bags of "after care" materials for me. it wasn't until i got home, i realized sequoia had given me everything i needed to heal at home.

thank you to all the nurses, doctors, cleaning staff, culinary staff, and others at sequoia for making this a memorable experience.

so during my er visit they ran several blood tests and the doctor gave me ativan eventually. the ativan did help a little bit to calm me down, but my symptoms were still there (i had been having them for about a week). the doctor came in and was adamant that i had to see a psychiatrist. his tone in telling me this was condescending and rude. he made all of symptoms out to be a mental illness, and i 100% know that they are not. perhaps having these ongoing symptoms for an extended period of time resulted in anxiety, but this is not all due to anxiety. i was trying to explain my core symptoms to him - but he kept interrupting me. he treated me like i was not worthy of his time, like i was some sort of drug addict looking for pills (in this case just a human being looking for a diagnosis). 

the er doctor made it sound like i just hop around from er to er wasting everyone's time, even asking me "how many times have you been going to er's for your anxiety" and "when was the last time you went to the er for your anxiety" and trying to reprimand me and shame me for going to the er. well guess what, i don't regularly go to the er. i went one time recently, in the prior week, when all of this started, for similar symptoms. but that's it. and nobody at that time said anything about it being anxiety. they actually encouraged me to go back to the er if i didn't feel better...which is what i was doing!

the most grevious issue is that a front desk person came in close contact with our newborn without a mask, not once, but twice. the first time she came into our room right up to me with my baby in my arms and did something with a tag/monitor on our child's ankle. then another time she came into our room and initially had a mask to take our baby for a test (that we were not allowed to attend), but then returned with our baby not wearing it again! this was a huge breach of policy and is nearly a legal issue because she was endangering safety. newborns are some of the most vulnerable to getting coronavirus and/or mis-c which are both quite serious. as far as we know staff aren't tested but only screened and i myself have already been tested twice (once while in labor because my previous test was more than 4 days prior.) and my husband and i have been practicing strict social distancing for many months. so all this to say that it was very upsetting that this was not corrected or taken seriously.

there was also an issue of lesser importance, but still significant, that we encountered with nurse megan being openly rude and judgmental in regards to breastfeeding. another nurse also didn't seem to want to verbally explain how to use a breast pump. i felt very unsupported at times during our stay.

they also fumbled with registering our baby's birth and getting the birth certificate 'draft' ordered. i waited about 3 weeks, after constantly checking the mail and finding nothing, and tried to call the birth registry. no response for a week to my vm. then i called again at the 4 week mark. emily questioned if i had even given birth there. i assured her i did and she said she could not find the paperwork that we had filled out and given to a nurse in the system. she said she would contact the birth records department. when she called back she stated that the forms were scanned into the wrong place and were scanned in illegibly. we had to go over everything over the phone trying to ensure she was getting spelling correct. then she told us we could use the vitalchek website to see a 'draft' online the next day, check for errors, make corrections, and order. that turned out to be completely false. there are tons of terrible reviews for that 3rd party site and aren't bbb accredited. so i called back. stephanie returned my call and seemed confused. she stated we would still get the draft in the mail. i explained what happened and she said she would call the state vital records office and ask them to put a rush on it. none of this should have happened in the first place as there should have been a "cross-check" to ensure all births had been registered. the draft bc arrived after 6 full weeks-- so we still have no birth certificate and no ssn card due to mistakes made by the hospital. if i had not called twice, her birth would still not have been registered !this seems like a glaring oversight and froedtert should be embarrassed (but they are not). 

these things make the good people at froedtert look bad. nurses on l&d like corey and becky as well as those on the 6th floor including india, robyn, kelsey, and nikki as well as lactation consultants like wanda and pediatricians like dr. francis or franklin (she had red hair) and her male resident from australia. these professionals helped to balance out our experience, but i'm hoping my email to the 6th floor manager & this review might save others the heartache and stress froedtert caused us in a time that is supposed to be joyful, happy, and most of all, safe.

i went to the sleep lab after a referral from my doctor at tripler. i have tricare prime and so far so good on the insurance front.

lady parking security guard was helpful and walked me over to the security check on. she had really nice hair. dude who took my temperature and gave me my name tag was friendly as well. i was very psyched up because my sticker read "destination: sleep."

ruth at the sleep clinic was very kind and gentle with me while dealing with all the electrodes & sensors necessary for my test. 

i would have preferred if the sleep rooms had full size beds instead of the tiny twin size they have now. i kept worrying about possibly falling out of the bed which i suppose is probable for folx with various parasomnias. 

the only reason this is not a 5 star rating is the parking situation. i got validated parking at an outpatient rate of $3 versus $24. coolio. however, when i went to leave, the parking workers don't take cards. only cash or check. who still carries checks with them? i mean, i have checks because i'm a somewhat responsible old millennial, but i don't carry them around with me so i can inconvenience people at the grocery store anymore. 

i was instructed there was an atm in the hospital lobby so i reversed my car and parked. keep in mind that it's about 5:45am, the patient lobby is closed until 7am. i can see the atm from outside the locked doors; it's blue lit lettering taunting me. i am sleepy and i just want to go home, but no say the parking goblins. i am now sitting in my car awaiting the lobby opening. 

on a brighter note, there is a charger for electric vehicles right as you enter the garage. it takes cards. $2 for 1 hour charging on top of your parking fees. 

also, the closest open coffee place is a 10-15 minute walk. normally that'd be no big deal, but as i said, i came here to sleep. i have electrode goop in my hair. i'm not wearing a real bra. i'm donning birkenstocks with socks ala my romanian father-in-law. i'm foggy and attempting not to sleep in my car so i'm not sure questing for coffee in an area of the city i've never been in is wise. i didn't bring my sword so i could go link on any chickens i find and if you can't destroy things with a sword what's the point of a quest???

update: lobby opened promptly at 7 am. atm fee is $3.95. so all in all it cost me $3 with validated parking, $2 to charge my car while waiting for the atm to be accessible, and then $3.95 to withdraw $20 to fulfill my debt to the parking goblins. total: $8.95 and an hour and a half of my life i can never reclaim.  finally pulled up to the parking kiosk and paid, got my change and said thank you. goblin just blinked while furrowing at me. i expect this sort of bedside manner from doctors, unfortunately, but man, the goblin could have been polite back. i weep in sleep deprived silence as i drive home after nearly being hit by an elderly lady while trying to go turn into the parking lot for starbucks. huzzah. 

tldr: a+ for ruth @ the sleep clinic. parking goblins are no joke and will only accept antiquated currencies- cash or check only to leave the parking garage. i do not have any rubies or kiddos so i'm not sure if the goblins will accept shiny gems or a first born child as alternate payment.

you can do better than this hospital. i delivered my baby here in jan 2020. he's my first child, so i don't have other experiences to compare this one to. while i generally had decent care, there were many things about inova alexandria that were not as advertised, and as a result, we struggled on a few fronts. 

first, they actively advertise that they provide nitrous oxide to laboring mothers. this was one of the reasons i chose this hospital. they do not. i was already well into labor by the time i was told that there was no nitrous available at the hospital. i had mentioned this several times prior, had discussed it with my physician/midwife practice (who exclusively delivers at inova alexandria), and it was in my birth plan-- no one thought to tell me that there was no nitrous until go time. 

second, once i decided to get an epidural (given that there was no nitrous and i'd been induced a long time prior), the anesthesiologist clearly messed up as he was setting it up. to the point where he apologized to my doula-- not to me or my husband mind you. thank god i didn't end up with something terrible happening on that front. 

third, since i was induced, i was in the hospital for longer than expected before delivery. they had the most uncomfortable bed known to man. i got no sleep, and both my husband and i went into the delivery completely exhausted as a result. birth plan basically went out the window. 

fourth, this hospital prides itself on breastfeeding support. it's everywhere on the walls, the literature, you name it. but guess what-- their support is lousy. i had to request help multiple times. it got to the point where i had to beg the head nurse to ask a lactation consultant to sit with me and make sure he was latching. breastfeeding is hard regardless- but at a "baby friendly" hospital where they tell you about their fabulous lactation support, and i did literally everything in my power to flag that there was a problem and i was struggling, they failed me. i saw at least four different lactation consultants. there was a lot of happy talk, but very little practical help. when it wasn't working, they couldn't help me, and i left the hospital basically hopeless. i had to hire a lactation consultant to come to my house the next day and by that point my baby was a big fan of formula. 

fifth- as it turns out, part of the reason breastfeeding didn't work for me was b/c i had severe postpartum preeclampsia that went undiagnosed while in recovery, even though we spent extra days at the hospital because my son had jaundice. my body was busy trying to keep me from stroking out rather than producing milk. thank god i was told by a midwife to make an appt within 48 hours of discharge to have my blood pressure checked. i might very well have died in my sleep otherwise. 

sixth, i had the worst experience with a nurse of my life there. one particular nurse insisted on drawing blood from my days old son in the most painful way possible while he screamed as i've never heard a baby scream before. she was ignorant, ill-trained, and thinking of her to this day makes me furious. other blood draws were a breeze compared to this because they were done properly and he never screamed again. she clearly had no idea what she was doing. 

seventh, my baby had jaundice and they did a terrible job of giving you any option but to have a giant, drafty, old school light machine wheeled into your room so that you- in a hospital with trained staff and having had no sleep in days- have to make sure that a tiny baby who cannot have a blanket doesn't take off the thin fabric that protects his eyesight, etc. it was awful. 

eighth, there is not really a nursery here. they make this clear on the tour, but you might want a hospital with a decent nursery. what they have is makeshift, drafty, and not appropriate for proper care. 

ninth, they literally never let you sleep. i'm not talking about the baby keeping you up. they come to check vitals constantly at all times of the day even when there's a do not disturb sign up. we went home having not slept in basically five nights, which led to a nightmare scenario for a brand new family of three. despite all of this checking, they still didn't catch that my body was shutting down. maybe that wasn't possible to do-- but it is notable that i kept alerting nurses to classic preeclampsia symptoms and i was repeatedly told that those were normal after having been pumped with fluids during labor.

tenth, i left never wanting to come back to this place ever again. it was a miserable experience despite the fact that there were some staff who were helpful and tried their best. unfortunately, i had to go back to their er two days later because they had all of my recent birth records and health history on file. here's where they actually saved my life, and i had a generally good experience with excellent staff- save for the lactation consultant who was horrible, insulting, and should be fired.

i have some sort of mystery sickness and was advised by my doc to go to an emergency room and since qotv was the closest one, there i went.
i'll list the good/okay points first:
evening parking was good, we got there after 8pm on a wednesday.
check-in was quick and the social distancing was observed by seating everyone outside in tents.
the wait time was in the middle. it took a couple of hours to get everything done and i could get out of there. wasn't the fastest, considering there weren't that many patients around, but it wasn't the slowest.
the nurse conducting the usual tests was doing her job. 
the doc that gave me the "diagnosis" did a job.
the check out nurse was really nice and helped me get up from the bench, which was a plus.

on to the not-so-good points:
i was having trouble standing but there was no place to sit when i was filling out the entry paperwork.
the nurse performing the initial blood tests and temp checks had a oral thermometer. of course it had those little sanitary sleeves, but this place doesn't have any of those non-touch forehead temperature sensors? during an epidemic? 
the doc came out and made a very general diagnosis and gave me some prescriptions. other than the covid-19, there were no other tests mentioned to figure out what i had. when i asked for the hospital to fax the information to my primary care doc, he replied that "they didn't have that technology." ... what?!  i haven't heard of a fax being called technology in a loong while. no wonder they don't have those other types of thermometers. i wonder how they communicate information, via smoke signals?
when the final nurse came out to give me the check out paperwork & prescriptions he said i could check on my test results via an online portal, color me surprised by that news. how is a place that doesn't have fax technology have a website portal. not very consistent this place.
okay, here it is days later and i feel less like death. i want to check my test results, so i try going to the link. first off let me say the "link" they provided is ridiculously long: https://portal.emanatehealth.org/templates/selfsignup-quvweb.livef-en-us.html 
most people access the internet on their phones, so i can't even imaging how frustrating it must be to type this crap into the address bar and don't even think about making a typo because it won't work if you do.
i tried logging into their online portal multiple times on three separate browsers with zero success. so i guess qotv's "website portal" is more in line with the level of tech savvy one would expect from a place that doesn't have fax technology.
no worries, i'll just call in (and probably get put on perpetual hold or never reach a human which would be par for course) and see if i can get my information that way.

over all, i'm not impressed by this place, but it's not the worst i've seen... but we are talking about the american healthcare "system" so the bar is set pretty low. 

i came in, got some medications which helped a lot and the staff were on average okay, so win- i guess. i don't know what i'm going to do if i get any more strange sicknesses that a doc just can't throw some meds at. hopefully i won't and that's the best anyone (who isn't rich and/or has amazing health care insurance) can hope for.

i recently reported monterey park hospital to the joint commission, the agency that accredits hospitals. i had many reasons, but here's a snapshot: 

 my mother was released from monterey park hospital on 5/24/2020. i just received the discharge summary today, june 2, 2020.
 a typical discharge summary is written with 24-48 hours of a patient's release because the information contained in it will be vital to the patient's aftercare. time, therefore, is of the essence.
 to obtain the ds (and address other concerns) for my 87-year-old mother, i had to write many emails--all unanswered--and in the final one, threaten to get "legal representation" to force the hospital to release a ds.
 my mother's attending physician explained the delay by stating that he had been on vacation. he also complained that he hadn't had a vacation in ten years, and that he and his wife had planned one for march/april, but those plans had fallen through.
 he further explained that when a doctor takes a vacation, he is allowed additional time to write a ds, which sounded to me like a bad excuse for turning your homework in late. 
 no provisions or safeguards are made for patients at monterey park hospital whose doctors go on vacation. my mother's attending physician insisted that the task of writing a ds could not be assigned to another doctor.
 the day after her discharge, my mother went to the emergency room due to pain from a leaking catheter. we had no idea why she had been catheterized in the first place. discharge papers from monterey park hospital did not explain the catheter, so emergency room workers were reluctant to remove it. a ds would have been helpful in that moment. a ds was also the first thing my mother's primary care doctor asked for when we took her in for follow-up care four days after her release from monterey park hospital. however, we had none to offer.
if the ds debacle were the only issue with monterey park hospital, i wouldn't be writing this review. however, there's more, which is why i contacted ericka smith, the coo, to alert her to the many wrong things that occurred during my mother's 5-day stay. but ericka smith was completely unresponsive. completely. she didn't even acknowledge that she had received my emails. she is either indifferent, incompetent, or reflexively anticipates lawsuits and stays silent as a matter of protecting herself.
leadership is reflected in the good and bad practices of any institution, so i don't think my mother's situation was an outlier, or the problem with monterey park hospital is due to individual "bad apples." i think the problems are systemic, and leadership is mute. this is why i alerted the joint commission. when lives are at stake--as my mother's was, and still is--a hospital can't be allowed to operate in this way.

my dad spent two months in this hospital last year and was hospitalized again last month. he passed away in the hands and "care" of the hospital staff, if i could even call it that. what was an already traumatizing experience from his first hospitalization down to his last dying breath was only intensified by the lack of care, communication, consideration, and ethics shown by this hospital.

background: my dad struggled with congenital heart disease as well as a number of other health issues. in april 2019, he ended up in van ness cpmc to get the lvad. there were multiple complications with the surgery, was in the icu, and survived. it was a miracle that he survived that. two months of his recovery was spent here, and went to another hospital after. fast forward to a few weeks ago. he was hospitalized again and was brought to the icu once more. he passed away and due to the pandemic, we were unable to be with him.

our experience:
me, my three sisters, and mom spent every day at icu during my dad's first visit. my mom has been an rn for the last 30 years at a nearby hospital (and a damn good one at that)  and was deeply concerned for the quality of care he was receiving. most of the staff was quite friendly, but wouldn't follow through on their promises. so, we found ourselves assisting our dad to make up for a majority of the nurses' lack of help (will list reasons why later). second time, it was strictly phone communication with both my dad and staff. we were faced with similar issues again.  

concerns:
(first hospitalization)
- staff, both nurses and doctors, would set up meetings for updates and would hardly ever be on time, nonetheless show up  
- would promise phone call updates without delivery
- lack of patient care: wouldn't turn him regularly, my mom had to do it
- during intubation, found that his trach site had puss and was smelly, indicating they weren't cleaning him properly. we addressed this, and found it was infected
- during his approx. 1 month of intubation, they kept him on restraints constantly which put even more stress on my dad.  even when there weren't any ivs to pull out, no trach, they still restrained him, adding onto my dad's restlessness
- nurse practitioner was trying to send my dad home without rehab, even though he was clearly imbalanced and was in no condition to leave 

(second hospitalization) 
- dad was put on npo in preparation for multiple tests, but staff would regularly reschedule his tests. he literally wasn't eating ever because of this 
- ****we had a half hour discussion with the nurse practitioner via phone call to discuss our concerns including that my dad was lactose intolerant and shouldn't be given ensure, and that my dad did not want to be intubated anymore. she said "oh, wow, i will have a meeting tomorrow with the staff about this" on a friday then found out my dad was intubated on sunday night. we did not receive that information until monday at 3pm by the doctor. when we told him about our discussion with the nurse practitioner, he said he didn't know that.****** 
- ...and my dad was still given ensure after we mentioned lactose intolerance. 
- my dad passed away the next day and we were told by the nurse we would "receive a phone call" regarding 1) autopsy, 2) what to do with his lvad, 3) results to his bone marrow biopsy immediately because he might have had tuberculosis. we didn't hear anything. my dad's physician who is not apart of van ness cpmc was the one to tell us he had tb and for me and my mom to get tested since we were exposed. 
- on his death certificate, they put the wrong date of hospitalization and apparently, there was no autopsy at all, despite my mom's request??

  
this hospital has some serious work to do on their organization, communication, and ethics. although the runt of our interactions were with the nurses, this is an issue that the hospital must tackle as a whole. it was a deeply saddening experience to witness my dad's condition from beginning to end, especially being unable to advocate for him by his side during the pandemic. i can only imagine how much more stressful this would be for a family that had no medical background. please, please fix this, so other families don't have to go through what we had to go through.

it has been 37 days since i last was able to see my son who is only 62 days old and still in the nicu - all because of a covid visitation policy at texas children's that is excessive, insensitive to parent's/ patient's well-being and out of line with nearly all surrounding hospitals.  37 days i have been prevented from holding him, watching him grow, and having critical moments of bonding.

tch's visitor policy is one parent per stay.  nearly all hospitals for children in medical center have a humane policy of one parent per day (hospitals offering that are children's memorial hermann nicu, harris health ben taub nicu, houston methodist hospital children, shriners hospitals for children) and woman's hospital of texas even allows both parents to visit.   

how is tch so out of line with their competitors? why are they so unsympathetic to the needs of their patient and their families?  

not to mention that the policy itself is illogical - my wife and i live and breathe  in the same household - we represent the same risk factor & germ pool.   i understand limiting the number of visitors in the hospital at any given time, but allowing parents living in the same household to switch daily would not increase the level of statistical risk for the hospital. your intent here was well placed, but the excessive (& out of line) policy that you have drawn is causing harm to parents and preemie babies and without any real benefit.  

so in conclusion tch has a visitation policy that is dramatically more harsh than their peers, that is causing real harm to patients/ their families and doesnt make their patients any more safe.   

i have worked with child advocacy multiple times and spoken to hopsital administrators, they all recognize the policy does not make logical sense but they are either unwilling or incapable to make humane, logical, reasonable accommodations.

in mid-march, just as the covid-19 virus was ramping up, my husband required emergency surgery, not related to covid, for which time was of the essence.  he had initially been taken to st. mary's where it was determined that they didn't have the resources to perform the necessary procedure and he would have to be moved to long beach memorial.  there was no guarantee that he would survive the short trip to receive the procedure. 

he did survive the trip under patrick's care and from the time he arrived at long beach memorial, my mr. received the best care that i could have hoped for.  from the surgical team to the ccu and icu nursing staff, from the nurse practitioners to the physician specialists, the care and professionalism were awesome.  it was apparent that each of the individuals caring for mr. had a personal investment in his recovery.  i was treated with great empathy, was included in the bedside change shift huddles so that i was informed as to what was going on, and any questions i had were answered fully.

because of the virus lock down, i was only able to stay with mr. for a couple of days of his two week stay before i was locked out but was encouraged to call the ccu and icu nursing stations from home for updates.  staff recognized how difficult the separation would be so they also encouraged me to bring his phone to the hospital so that, after mr. awoke, we would be able to communicate, making it a little bit less isolating for him.

i will say that there were a few hiccups at discharge time.  i chalked this up to the fact that mr.'s discharge took place just as non-essential employees were being furloughed and consequently a couple of non-medical things fell through the cracks.  i was pleasantly surprised (and relieved) when i received follow up phone calls from the nurse practitioners for several days following discharge.

i would not wish mr.'s medical situation on anyone but feel confident in saying that if it happens, the patient will be in the best of hands.

i delivered my daughter at this hospital on april 30th under the advise of my ob who said this hospital was great. i went in for a scheduled induction at 8am on the 30th and my first attending nurse was amazing. super supportive, nice, upbeat and reassuring. unfortunately i can't remember her name but i know she was from hawaii because we made small talk during the induction process. 

well i got to the point where my contractions were coming too rapidly and lengthy (coming every 30 secs for at least 45secs to 1 min each) for the only 4 cm i was dilated. so i elected to get an epidural being that the contractions were strong and i was dilating super slow; i went in already dilated to 3cm. fast forward and things started to move faster after the epidural and dialing the pitocin up quite a bit. the attending nurse was so sweet that she hung out slightly after her shift because she was determined to see my baby girl. unfortunately she couldn't hang out to that point since she was born at 9pm and her shift ended at 5pm i believe. 

fast forward again to postpartum. everything started out good.  but the reason i gave 1 star starts now. the room was freezing cold, i informed the nurse that it was super cold and the thermostat was not working. i was told that they would contact engineering and have them check it out. 2 hours later and freezing, nothing was done. i called again and finally a different person contacted someone who fixed it... temporarily.  of course after delivery things can be "less than tidy" and i consider myself a pretty clean person. well the cleaning crew did absolutely nothing but empty the trash in the bathroom. no one checked the bed/changed the linen, swept or mopped the floor or actually cleaned the bathroom. and unfortunately i had to be there for 2 days since my discharge time would have been too late in the night because of the required 24hour stay after delivery. 

the following day the lactation specialist, nicholette, came in to go over breast feeding with me. not once did she ask me about my personal situation e.g.) personal life and whether i have a partner to assist,  medical history, potential work schedule, nothing i think would be important to establish my personal feeding plan. i had a pacifier for my daughter because i couldn't stop her from crying. the first thing she did was tell me her name and write it on the board. the second was to take the pacifier out of my daughter's bed and throw it in the drawer and tell me "she doesn't need this, these are terrible" i was in disbelief and speechless. she never asked why i had it out but just shut down the use of it. she asked me to try to breast feed her so that she could see how things are going. i obliged and picked her up and attempted to latch. i explained to her that i was having some issues getting her to latch because of the shape of my nipple so i was going to try using a nipple shield that my doula suggested may help.  she asked if i tried different positions, which i had and told her.  i said i was going to try using a nipple shield to help with latching and again shut me down saying those are terrible and she will latch i just have to make her. keep in mind, i've just had a baby, i'm exhausted, i've been trying to breast feed, and my baby was crying quite a bit. now she's come in and told me that everything i've been doing is wrong. so finally my daughter latches, she asked me if she could help out. i said "sure." so she starts aggressively massaging my breast while my daughter is latched and i'm just sitting there because i can't get a word in because she's over talking me. a nurse comes in to ask me a question and suddenly she storms out of the room. she goes and tells the attending nurse, wendy, that i was "non compliant." wait... what?!?! she starts immediately asking me why i didn't want to work with her without asking me how i felt, if there was an issue, if i felt comfortable... none of that. just basically that i was wrong. luckily the pediatrician on call came in to take a look at my daughter and he asked about breast feeding and how it was going. i explained to him that she hadn't urinated and she was crying a lot. he suggested supplementing her with formula because she was likely hungry. well he was right! she sucked down 3 ounces of formula in no time which was what i was trying to explain to the nurse and lactation specialist.  

overall, the lack of room maintenance, communication, and bedside manner were definitely subpar. i definitely would not choose this hospital if i have another baby, and wouldn't suggest it to anyone either.

had my tonsils taken out yesterday as an adult. they also did an allergy panel on me. the doctor at the ent office initially told me this could be done while i was asleep, because it's a lot of blood drawn. but no, the nurse came and drew my blood before i went back for surgery. she had an older nurse come in and supervise. she laid the syringes on my lap and said "i'm gonna use your lap as a tray." 
ok, that's enough to make me feel unnerved. 
but i didn't get an attitude with her. 
she started drawing my blood and i was breathing heavily because i was anxious. the other nurse said "breathe normal! the needle isn't even in you anymore!"
thanks for that. i don't have to have a needle in me to feel anxious but okay. 
after they took my blood, they asked if i needed a wet rag. i said no, but i feel anxious. the nurse said "yeah, well press this button if you need anything." and walked off. didn't try to comfort me at all. they drew 3 large vials of my blood, and just left me there to lay and stare at the ceiling with no cell phone and no one to talk to. 

after laying there for 2 hours, they rolled me to the back for surgery. they put me under anesthesia and didn't ask me to count back from 100. 
next thing i remember, i was back out on the floor and awake. i immediately started crying because they didn't give me enough pain medicine. i was in pain, i was alone, and i was scared. there were 2 new nurses that i didn't recognize. i never saw my initial nurse again, after i guess i had shown too much of a fuss when she was drawing my blood. 
but these 2 were not any more comforting. they saw me crying and started freaking out. they were like "what's going on!? do you just get emotional after surgery?"
typically, no. i had a major spinal fusion prior to this surgery, but i felt safe so i did not cry. 
but i just nodded my head because it hurt to talk. i asked the nurse to give me more medicine so she did, and i started to feel better. 
i asked her if the surgeon took out my adenoids with my tonsils, because i felt like they needed to come out too. she said yes. 
but my boyfriend told me that when the nurse called and spoke to him on the phone, she said that she didn't take them out. she "treated" them, whatever that means. 
when i got home, my bad experience didn't end. i kept throwing up, and i couldn't keep liquid or medicine down. the nurse had given me pepcid, but again, this was before i laid and waited for 2 hours before going back to surgery. my boyfriend called the doctor for me to get some nausea medicine called in. doctor said he would call walgreens to see if they had it, but he never followed up with my boyfriend. when my boyfriend called back after about an hour, the lady at the answering service got an attitude with him and told him that he should have called walgreens. so he called walgreens and they didn't have the medicine. called back, answering service was rude again. they told him "we'll send the doctor a note, he may call you back."
i finally got a different nausea medicine at about 9 pm and i was able to keep down my apple sauce and liquid medicine... by then, i was just ready to go to sleep.

i've had aud (alcohol use disorder) for about 40 years. i've tried everything: hypnosis, acupuncture, years on antabuse, 6 months and then 7 years sober in aa in 2000s. each relapse turned into a several weeks long binge, forcing me to seek help again. finally, in 2014 i discovered sinclair method (https://www.the-sinclair-method.com/), which turned out to be a lifesaver. my drinking quickly went down to safe limits and i started to have alcohol free days several times a week. for 5.5 years i was a social drinker, a "normie" in aa speak - until covid struck. 

i live alone, the lockdown made me seriously depressed. all my routines and nearly all social contacts were broken and it felt like a solitary confinement. at some point in april, i stopped taking my medication as prescribed by the sinclair method. from there, my drinking quickly escalated and turned into a heavy 6 weeks binge. by may 13 i had to go to er and then to a 10 days detox in holister; spent the first night in icu nearly having a heart attack. after i got back home on sunday may 24, i wanted to make sure that sinclaire is still working (i still had some meds left from my last refill); i had 3 drinks on the first day, then it went 1, 1, 0, 1, 0 - amazing, considering my condition before the detox. 

in the meantime, my gf discovered the intensive outpatient program (iop) at good sam behavioral. i was surprised to learn that dr cecil a. bradley, who prescribed me naltrexone all these years, is the medical director of this program. the program seemed very useful since a) it is in person, no zoom, b) i got a double diagnosis and could address my underlying emotional issues and c) i could get an extended medical leave, since i was not feeling up to getting back to work immediately. on thursday, may 28 i was there and talked to marcella (admissions) dr khan (sp? md), nurse diane and some other people. i was very open about what i've been doing before, what brought me there and about my intentions (go back on sinclaire, since it works great and aa stopped working for me at some point). everybody seemed to be open-minded, accepting and approving of my course of treatment. some even wrote down the name of my method and said they were curious and want to learn more about it.

thursday and friday sessions were pretty nice, with meditation, some cbt and open discussions on topics suggested by patients themselves. and then, on friday noon dr bradley showed up, took me to his office and told me that their program is based on full abstinence and if i keep up the  controlled drinking, i have to leave. he said there are alternatives to aa and suggested some other program - he just could remember it's name. he is in his 80s and seems to forget things. i promised to think about it over the weekend and tell him about my decision on monday. after all, at this point i could easily refrain from drinking for the duration of the program.

however, on monday my case manager handed me a recovery plan with mandatory conditions: attend at least 3 meetings a week, find a sponsor and report progress at each morning session. i told her i don't do aa, and i was told to go talk to dr bradley, and again he gave me a dilemma: full abstinence and meetings or leave the program. "there is this other program - can't remember it's name... rational recovery?" "- smart recovery?" "- yes, this must be it". "- i researched it, and it has about the same success rate as aa - which is in single digits - whereas sinclair method has success rate near 80%". "- i don't care. this program requires full abstinence and meetings". so i informed him that i'm quitting and went home.

there are several things that really upset and anger me. 
1) why did dr bradley prescribe my medicine all these years and even wrote me another 3 refills on that monday if he disapproves on sinclair method so much? 
2) how does a doctor refer a patient to some program the name of which he can't even remember? does he know anything about it? or he just doesn't care?
3) why did they admit me at all, knowing full well my intentions, knowing dr bradley's views and giving me false hopes? 
4) what kind of doctors put a patient into completely unscientific, faith-based programs with abysmal success rate and force him to abandon something that is proven to work for 80% and this patient in particular?

so i googled dr bradley and discovered that the medical board of california twice has suspended his license, once in 1990 and second time in 2007 (5 years probation). he also was known to be sending referrals to and working at a couple of shady rehabs ran by an uncertified drug addict.

makes you wonder, how does a doctor like cecil bradley ends up a medical director at well-respected hospital like good sam? i would not recommend going to good sam in- or outpatient behavioral programs until they replace him. the rest of staff seems to be ok, but there is nothing they could do to help me under current leadership.

i highly recommend you go here for your medical care.  also - get that first appointment and be early to it.  be nice to your staff as they sure are nice to you.  while i won't be back soon (knock on wood, fingers crossed), i'd gladly return here in 10 years when i'll get this done again!

anyway, as with most doctor's offices - wait times can be rather atrocious so i would advise trying to take the earliest appointment in the morning or the first available after lunch.  they do tend to run further and further behind as the day progresses (this is common with most medical practices), so just bear that in mind and bring along a book or your ipad (there's free wifi).  i've been a patient of two doctors in the obstetrics and gynecology department and i've been pleased with the interactions and quality of care i received.  even the front desk staff, techs, and nurses have been understanding and patient, even when i've been disheveled and bewildered (as a first time pregnant lady can sometimes be).

i was especially pleased with my stay in the childbirth center.  it's a smaller labor and delivery area compared to some other hospitals in the medical center, which i feel facilitated a quieter and calmer stay, and it enabled the nurses and staff to provide more individualized attention to me and other patients.  granted, i only have this one experience to draw my opinion from, but the nurses were just so extraordinarily kind and helpful during my stay here.  almost two years later, my husband still brings up how lovely everyone was to us during our brief three day stay here.  i had a traumatic (but not life-threatening) postpartum complication that was rather unpleasant to deal with and the nurses really busted their butts to make me comfortable as possible and continuously tried to seek a resolution to my issue.

doc_text:
well, i guess spring break will become a do not leave the house practice in future years.
last year it was the hubster who after a gentle nudge from one of our 100 pound retrievers fell forward down the steps and broke his ankle on the second day of our camping excursion. (unfortunately misdiagnosed by an urgent care facility near walker, tx.)
this year it was my turn. i was backing down the steps to be more able to open the door wider to accommodate me and several items i had in my hands. well dang if i didn't miss a couple steps and felt myself falling backwards onto the concrete slab shared with our rv. i had time to say "oh no" before  a hard landing -not sure if i stuck my head first or my tailbone first but i had the wind knocked out of me (and since i haven't ever experienced that) i panicked thinking i was not going to start breathing again. i was unable to get up and thankfully some camping neighbors came over and after a few minutes were able to help me stand. by that time my son and daughter-in-law and hubby had arrived. my head was not bleeding but had quite a nice goose egg with colorful abrasions and  along with my tailbone (which i had fractured years ago),
and then a cut and abrasion on my elbow. i was convinced that it would be best to go get examined so agreed to go to an urgent care. sadly, the urgent care didn't have the capability to do skull  x-rays or a ct scan which the physician assistant felt was necessary to determine that i did not have any internal bleeding or swelling in my brain .
she called the emergency room at this local hospital and informed them i would be headed that way. the urgent care was really awesome, i could feel the compassion by the pa and she knew i did not want to go to the er but strongly encouraged me, so off we went.
of course this is when the coronavirus had started to manifest itself in texas so there were many precautions once we entered the emergency room waiting area.  upon our arrival we presented at the registration area-explained the situation and advised that the urgent care pa had called ahead. he advised that he just come on shift and didn't know anything about it. that was certainly understandable but he didn't offer to go and ask anyone either. took all my insurance and payment info and sent us out to sit in the waiting room.
don't get me wrong, i fully believe that people should be triaged and treated accordingly but i was surprised that we waited an hour to even go back to be examined in a pre-entrance room. the two nurses that assessed me decided they needed to apply a cervical collar-ugh. they did ask my head pain level which was a 10 at that time. they put me in a w/c and they brought me to my er room. we saw a nurse almost immediately who hooked me up to all the devices they like to apply to monitor you, asked me to rate my pain (still 10). she said i would be going for a ct scan shortly and then would see the doctor. it was evident they were quite busy-which they said had become routine there over the last couple of years. 3 hours later a very nice physician arrived and was dismayed that i had not had a ct scan yet. she advised that the collar could not be removed until after i had had the scan. she asked about my pain level which had subsided to about a 7 on its own. although i reported my other injuries they were so focused on my brain they never assessed them. obviously, the potential for brain injury was the most urgent but the injury to my tailbone was preventing me from walking without quite a bit of discomfort and my elbow wound turned into a burning pain whenever i accidentally touched it on anything-and the pain was not at the site of the abrasion. the md went out to the desk and put in a stat order for the ct.
an hour and 15 minutes later someone from the ct department came to get me. they took me for the ct and then back to my er room in 10 minutes time. 90 minutes later my doctor returned (after i had put my call light on and requested they find out if the c-collar could be removed yet) she removed the c-collar (yay!) and reported there was no evidence of any brain bleeding or swelling and that she would be discharging me.(double yay!)
the nurse came in to discuss discharge instructions by which time i was up dressed and ready to go. so back to the campgrounds we went.
i felt very bad that my son had sat with me all those hours, and was exposed to heaven knows what...with other er patients going up and down the hall to get to the bathroom with their gowns and masks on and coughing and hacking the whole way.  ok-i do realize that being a nurse makes me very annoyed when i feel like there are inappropriate delays in care of any kind. god knows if i had had a brain bleed what kind of condition i would've been in after 4+ hours of waiting for a scan. if you follow me at all you also know that i am a stickler about excellent customer service. in all honesty, i would not return here.

this is for the physical therapy department only.  

i've had the unfortunate luck of having multiple joint replacements and other orthopedic surgeries (before becoming kaiser member) at a young age. the reasons why were never clear though many doctors have tried to figure it out.  the most common theory is that because i have hypermobility but was very active from a young age, this has deteriorated my muscle skeletal structure and started a domino effect. 

i had good physical therapy following my surgeries and the replaced joints are not a problem.  however, i continue to experience profound pain and discomfort on my right hip which is my one remaining major natural joint.  x-rays show no reason for this. i went to kaiser pt multiple times but found that the treatments actually worsened the pain.  when i eventually said this to the pt (actually a very nice guy) he basically threw up his hands.  

this issue has affected me greatly and i am in constant pain regardless of trying things like meditation, turmeric, foam rolling, etc. etc.  i've even had to resort to strong opioids left over from my surgeries even though i had weaned off long ago. i finally decided to bite the bullet and pay out of pocket for a place recommended by a neighbor.  i had immediate relief after the first session.  here's what they do that kaiser pt does not:

- you do the exercises with the therapist monitoring as opposed to going home with an exercise sheet. this allows you to report areas of pain or discomfort as you do the exercises and it also allows them to try other things while making note of your comments.

- hyper-mobile people have distinct needs, and therapy modes that work for most may well not work for them or have to be adjusted. i'm now working with someone who specialists in hypermobile patients.

- the new place truly deep dives into diagnosis.  muscle skeletal issues are complex and there are a diverse set of reasons why x may hurt.  you may have weak hips, but your issue may go beyond that and there may be a reason as to why your hips are perpetually weak.  kaiser pt is great for people who neatly fall into the bucket of widely known issues and common prescriptions, but for people who need a more individualized care it is a black hole. 

- i barely did any exercises in person with kaiser, so needless to say they did not help with any stretching whatsoever. in my case, though i'm double jointed there are a couple of tight areas that i simply cannot stretch on my own.  the new pt recognizes how crucial this is, and i can attest to the importance of this.

i really like kaiser in many ways, but in terms of pt the experience has been literally painful.  i've asked permission for an outside pt referral but if you're familiar with kaiser you understand how almost impossible that is.  this is a shame because i've probably cost them more money in terms of constant doctor appointments, mris, x-rays, etc. than what they could have paid for an outside pt for a few months. i could only afford to pay out of pocket for just a few sessions so i now spend hours each day doing self pt at home.  the personal cost of being in pain is enormous  - financially, emotionally, and socially.  i truly wish that an excellent organization like kaiser, which seems to genuinely care about public health, would take another approach to their treatment of physical therapy and pain management.

i was transferred to john muir inpatient from contra costa regional medical center's psychiatric emergency services (ccrmc, pes) located in martinez. john muir was definitely an upgrade, but i suppose anything would be better than pes.

i had 2 inpatient stays, both in february 2020. the first was from february 6 to february 10. the second was from february 18 to february 26. the first discharge was premature, but the second one was helpful in my recovery.

i was admitted on the second day of my 5150 (72 hour hold) as i had attempted suicide. the remainder of the stay was on a voluntary basis as i was willing to comply with treatment. the oak adult unit has friendly staff. most of them aren't licensed therapists, but they are still knowledgeable in various therapy concepts. i really enjoyed the groups, especially expressive arts. the registered nurses are professional and check in with you frequently to make sure you are safe. 

the psychiatrist i worked with, dr. mundi, is a jerk. when i shared what had pushed me to hurt myself, he was very dismissive. i made sure to let the staff know, and was assigned to a nurse practitioner during my second inpatient stay.

the food is really good. they really care about their patients health, both physical and mental. we had patio breaks throughout the day which was our only time to get fresh air. the nurses giving medication were very nice and helped me understand the specifics such as side effects and a time frame to notice improved mood.

naturally, i was home sick, but we were allowed to have visitors and access to a phone to call our family. the rooms had 2 beds, and a bathroom with a shower. 

the reason i was admitted again was because the first discharge was premature. the post discharge care plan did not work, and no one followed up with me despite me leaving several voicemails. fortunately, the second time around the post discharge care plan worked great and i was able to get a referral for further care at a crisis residental, hope house in martinez.

i give john muir behavioral health 4 stars. the facilty was clean, the staff was nice, the rooms were safe, and the food was good. there were rounds conducted every 15 minutes to make sure everyone was accounted for. it may affect your sleep, but the staff tries to be very quiet. safety is very important, so it didn't bother me.

on a side note, my very first inpatient stay was at fremont hospital in 2018. though the facilty was bigger and had a pool and court, i felt the staff was very impersonal. john muir behavioral health may not have all the extra features fremont hospital has, but quality is better than quantity. you are seen as a person, not as your diagnosis. 

we occasionally had students from samuel merritt take our vitals, all of whom were very nice. overall, this was a good experience and helped me grow. i doubt i will ever return because i now know how to cope in times of emotional distress. but i feel reassured knowing a place like john muir behavioral health exists. 

if i were to give any advice, it would be to speak with your social worker regarding care post discharge. this is very important. if you are troubled, you can talk with the staff. every shift each patient is assigned a registered nurse, mental health counselor, and social worker. they will listen.

thank you john muir staff.

so i was referred here quite a few months back to see dr. milad by my ivf clinic. since i have an hmo i needed to go through all of the medical group routes first. i saw my regular gyno did all of the ultrasounds and had a date scheduled for surgery. he actually called me (days prior to my procedure) to cancel. he also felt it was best i see dr. milad. 

a little background. i am 37, no children, actively trying to get pregnant, with fibroids, heavy painful periods, and seriously anemic. one frozen embryo left at the ivf clinic. i am capable of doing another retrieval but for now just the one. i have had a previous hysteroscopic myomectomy. mri was showing a degenerative fibroid approx 10cm. 

dr. milad is a high volume gynecological surgeon. until i was referred to him i had never heard this term before. basically he does gynecological surgeries and that is it... it is literally his specialty. where other doctors may do a few here and there this is his profession. 

we came up with a game plan all via teams, since we are mid pandemic. it was all great. i could see my images shared on my computer screen. his team was excellent at responding to questions or issues either via mychart email or with call backs. 

i had surgery 3 days ago. i actually just returned home today. my procedures turned out to be more invasive than we had hoped. my husband was not able to be in pre-op but was able to wait in the waiting room. he was very pleased with the nurse's call updates on the progress of my surgery. as it turned out my fibroid had grown into my uterine wall a good deal. it was measuring 12.5cm and with adenomyosis. they needed to reconstruct my uterus. i really feel that my desire for fertility was put into the correct hands with dr. milad and his surgical team. i may have lost my whole uterus without him. now while it remains to be seen if i will get pregnant or will carry to term... i now have that opportunity. 

also, i can not say enough wonderful things about everyone at this hospital!!! the transport team, my housekeeper, room service, care techs but especially my nurses! i mean they were all amazing! kati, gabi, alex, and mausam i truly appreciate all of your hard work and dedication to nursing! thank you all!!!

no one reads reviews of hospitals, but i'm so angry i had to leave something, somewhere.

i've been seen here during a fairly normal pregnancy, with a c-section delivery (unavoidable - complications made it necessary and i believe my doctor made the right call!)  i loved my ob and my care team, and all the nurses were kind and capable.  i chose to be seen here, since a small community hospital tends to provide more personal care than in a metropolitan one, where i felt like a number.

this review is for their billing & record keeping, which is an actual nightmare.  i've encountered multiple issues, including but not limited to:

- having to review the same printouts at every single visit because for some reason, no doctor ever noted that i've seen them.  not a big deal but there's more - 

- they ask for prepayment, so when i transferred there around 25 weeks or so, they asked me for monthly payments of $600.  l o l that's ridiculous.  i spoke to a manager who thankfully, agreed that was preposterous and let me pay afterward

- during my hospital stay someone from billing came in and asked for payment!  i paid it because i thought i was doing the right thing, except....

- i didn't owe that amount.  they hadn't even checked with insurance to see if i owed it.  i was so exhausted from giving birth i didn't realize it.

- so i paid them my entire out of pocket maximum and they're still billing me for other things!  shouldn't happen, and they should have taken it out of what i've already paid them.

- called me within two weeks of my daughter being born antagonizing me for not having added her to my insurance.  chill.  i'm working on it.  i have a month per the insurance company to add her.

- they set it to self-pay when they didn't get payment immediately.  guys!

- they call me months later to say i owe this amount....i ask my insurance to look for it and they can't find the claims.  turns out, they used my name but my daughter's dob.

are you kidding?  i'm waiting on my refund, by the way, of that out of pocket maximum i paid to them.  meanwhile other collectors are calling me asking for their payment, which i could have used that money for.  this is a total nightmare, and they are completely inept.  i'm working it all out with them, but it never should have happened in the first place.  beware.  if you have any other choices, go there.

never go to st. anthony's er.  on june 19, 2020 i injured my left leg and could not put any weight on it.  i drove myself to the er.  there were several nearby parking spaces but i had to pull up to the double doors at the entrance.  there was a lady sitting there taking temperatures.  i got her attention and she came with a wheel chair and helped my get inside.  there were 2 security guards standing there.  i asked one of them if he would park my car in a spot right by the entrance.  first, he said no and said valet would have to park it and it would probably be on the other side of the hospital.  a valet came and gave me ticket to get my car upon release. then the guard changed his mind and told me he would park it in that first spot.  

after triage i was taken to an exam room in the er.  they came and took several x-rays of my leg.  i waited and waited to see a doctor but no one came.  finally a man arrived and told me he was going to put an immobilizer on my leg.  i asked what the x-rays showed and he said i don't know sis they just told me to put this on you.  so he brought a long brace and put it on my leg.  it was new in a package.  then he brought in some dirty looking crutches that were not  in any packaging and gave me a 2 minute lesson on how to walk on crutches.  

a pa came in and told me i was being discharged.  i asked what the x-rays showed.  he said he didn't know.  i asked to see a doctor.  he said no one was available and he was there to discharge me.  i said i wasn't going to leave until i saw a doctor.  he told me they needed the room.  nothing had happened to make my leg bear weight and these people just pointed which way to go to get to the er entrance and sent me wobbling off on those crutches.  they didn't even have the courtesy to wheel me back out.  it took me 15 minutes to get from the room to the front entrance and my leg was killing me. i have never walked on crutches and this is not the way you want to learn.

when i got to the front the guard who was supposed to park my car wasn't there.  the other guard handed me my keys and said your car is out there somewhere. by this time tears were streaming down my face and i saw a blue car and started trying to make my way to it.  i realized it wasn't mine.  i tried using the emergency button on the key and no car alarm went off.  the lady who had initially helped me in saw what was happening and she started walking around helping me look.  then the valet drove by in a van and saw me out there on crutches trying to find my car.  he stopped the shuttle and came and told me my car was across the street at the top of a hill in the valet lot.  he literally ran over there and got my car. then he went and got wet wipes and cleaned it well.  he was the only person who seemed to understand i was in pain.

they had handed me a bunch of paperwork when i was discharged and when i got home i hoped it would have some results of the x-rays but it was all generic photocopies and there was nothing specific about what was wrong with my leg.  i still have no idea.  i am sure they are going to charge my insurance a fortune and i left there exactly the same as i went in except my leg was killing me from looking for my car and trying to get myself out of there with no assistance.  i called the so called patient advocate monday and tuesday with no reply.

this place is a joke. if i should ever need help again i will go to lutheran.  shame on you.

i got to spend two nights here recently. luckily i wasn't the patient -- but i kept my man company after his surgery. i actually slept on two chairs bedside while he was there. 

i've been here before myself, but they seem to have upped their game. in addition to taking all the extra precautions for covid, every person we came in contact with was very professional and enjoyable to deal with -- from the cleaners on up to the doctors and nurses. there really was a great team effort. and it shows. 

each shift change, they came in and introduced the new people. they went over the necessary info and posted it each time on a board by the bed. each patient has a phone with the number to call to reach the attending nurse, the assistant and floor personnel. it's a very efficient system. and they are very informative to prepare the patient for what's going to happen and how to manage your pain. 

the food here was surprisingly way better than average for hospital food. every morning starting at 6:30 am you can call in your breakfast order from their menu. it takes about an hour or less to get your hot breakfast. you use your phone to call the kitchen extension. (hint: they're busy. don't hang up. just hold til they answer.) choices included various omelets, eggs, turkey sausage, potatoes, breads/cakes, fresh and canned fruits, juices, cereals, etc. the only thing they didn't have was toast! you also call in for your other meals at least an hour or so in advance. lunches, too, were good as well as dinners. there's a lot of variety and they try to accommodate all requests if possible. two standouts were their fresh sliced hot turkey with mashed potatoes and gravy and their mac n cheese.

the hospital offers free valet parking which is helpful as the lot fills up. 

the only downside was the day we came their computers were acting up so it  took longer to register and to be processed during pre-op. and a longer time than expected waiting for a room to be available. 

no one really wants to be in a hospital, but if you do need to be, this is one of the better options in town.

took my infant to the er here after calling my pediatrician and describing her symptoms. she's had a fever for four days, lethargic, inconsolable crying, weak, distressed and in pain. she was having a hard time breathing normally and that's what i was most worried about. 

the receptionist was very friendly, took our information and we waited. the waiting room was nearly empty. due to covid 19 they only allowed one parent in w my daughter so my husband waited outside, even though there was a mom and a dad with their baby in the waiting room. 

they took us back to triage and left us waiting. finally a nurse practitioner came in, not friendly at all, almost annoyed that we were there, looked in my baby's ears and down her throat and said as she's walking out that they'll do a swab test her for flu, rsv and strep. she left and i hear her talking happily w another nurse right outside our door. would it kill her to be kind or friendly to us? oh well, i figured, not a big deal, i just want to take care of my baby. 

they take us to a room. 

shortly after that a nurse walks in and listens to my baby's heart. she said she needs to go see what tests need to be done and she leaves the room. 

we weren't waiting long when someone shows up to do a chest x ray. a chest x ray? the nurse practitioner had said nothing about that. i didn't even know they were going to get x rays. i wondered if they had heard something when they checked her a few minutes ago. of course my baby is freaking out the whole time. the guy is kind and we get it done. 

one hour goes by. two hours go by. my poor baby is restless and fussy. no one checked on us or told us what was going on. i walked out into the hall and asked the first person i saw what was taking so long. she said they were waiting for results from the swab test. i told her they hadn't done the swab test yet. she said oh they're probably waiting for the x ray results. 

another hour goes by and i called the nurse to the room and come to find out she thought another nurse had already swabbed my baby. after being there for three hours and hardly anyone else there we hadn't even taken the sample yet. 

another hour goes by and i walk out to the desk where the nurse is sitting there eating cookies. i told them we're leaving. my baby and i are both exhausted at this point and the whole thing has been a joke. another nurse snaps at me and tells me they have a skeleton staff and they don't even have a technician on staff.

i finally get the results of the swab test back and the nurse practitioner comes in and apologizes for everything taking so long and said there was a mix up with one nurse getting distracted and thinking someone else had already done the test. 

still heard nothing about the x rays, why they took them or what they showed. 

frustrating experience.
