i write this not only as a mother that has birthed three babies at mission bernal but also as a doula that has supported countless clients both at mission bernal and other bay area hospitals. the care provided by the mb team is simply unparalleled. every prenatal appoint i was treated like i was the only patient they had to see that day. i was warmly welcomed and my questions were always answered thoroughly, never rushed. i had an uncomplicated beautiful birth my first time around so going there for my second pregnancy with twins was a no-brainer.  during the delivery of my twins, after delivering my fist twin vaginally, there were complications with the second twin and it looked like it might go to a c-section. pemberton and norell were simply amazing. they managed to deliver the second twin vaginally as well. i think the most important take away from my experience is that i felt like an active-participant in both my births.  i felt safe, heard, supported, and empowered. i felt like the midwives genuinely cared about my physical and emotional well being- probably because they did! even at the end, when i felt like i couldn't go any longer, they made me believe that i could- and i did! they trust the birth process and a woman's ability to birth, and they help their patients believe it, too! surly this factors into their low intervention rates! i love the mb team and sing their praises at every opportunity. 
now, putting on my doula hat... i have seen so many beautiful births at mission bernal that would've been a c-section anywhere else. again- they trust the process. in the last 2 years i've had over a half dozen clients leave cpmc van ness to get care at mb. all i say is, "go meet the midwives, check it out" and the rest is history.  cpmc van ness is very high intervention and not big on informed consent. in the birth community they have a reputation for bullying patients into unnecessary interventions and early inductions. mb midwives on the contrary, give our clients a voice. they empower our clients and make them feel safe. i think the reason so many clients switch from cpmc vn to mb is not just bc of the appealing intervention statistics but bc mb staff makes you feel like family- warm, loving and invested.

doc_text: i had an amazing experience delivering my first baby at cpmc mission bernal campus in july of 2019. in particular, the midwives at the women's center who supported me in my prenatal months, through delivery, and with my postnatal visits, are what made my experience so wonderful. i attended the group prenatal program leading up to my due date. every midwife that i met through that program and through my additional prenatal office visits was amazing and i felt a true connection to all of them. i definitely was wary at first, of working with midwifes and not an ob, but i immediately found their level of professionalism and incredible knowledge, put my worries at ease. i was also a high-risk case. all the while, i found the midwives were confident and knowledgeable, and handled my treatment perfectly. i was admitted to mission bernal at 40+2 weeks, with a diagnosis of preeclampsia. two midwives handled my labor from beginning to end and worked perfectly with the doctor on the floor. their collaboration was impeccable and although i was delivered by the doctor, what stands out to me was the hours of amazing care i received from the midwives. they added a personal level of care that i know would have been missing, had i worked only with an ob. finally, i was excited to go back to to the women's center for my post-natal visits. it felt like a home to me and i was emotional to see my midwives again. there is no way that i can thank them enough for what they have given me. the postnatal time period is extremely difficult and i relied on their support as i recovered. they were only a quick phone call away to answer any question i had and provided medical support, when i needed it. in the future, i hope to have another hospital birth under the care of these outstanding midwives. i don't believe there is any other place in san francisco that would be able to offer this format and standard of care.

i'll try to make this as short as possible.  i had hip replacement surgery in november 2019.  i was so disgusted with the surgeon.  i used to have private insurance and now have medi-cal because of my disability.  i've worked as a unit clerk at oroville hospital, had front office and back office positions before becoming a case manager with butte county social services.  i am very well aware of being treated differently with private insurance and medi-cal.  maybe this is why that surgeon reserves a separate office for private insurance patients and may see his medi-cal patients for five minutes in the "clinic' office.  this is appalling.  i had to have labs done before surgery (probably a cbc and a chem panel).  my platelet count was 765.  i'm sure you know that the normal is between 140-400.  hmm.  after waking up on the surgery table, my lower back felt worse than labor pains. not the hip, yet.  i tried to tell him this and he kept walking out of the room and didn't even respond to me.  by the time i got to the floor to a room i was experiencing pain as i had never had before.  my blood pressure began to drop and i couldn't stop shaking.  one of the nurses said he knew where the dr. was and needed an order written for pain. i will commend the nursing staff and physical therapy.  they were all very pleasant.  i did not appreciate a male nurse telling me that pain medications were not the answer and i needed to try to do my part instead of being high on pain killers.  this was at the same time i couldn't couldn't quit shaking all over from no pain medication after a 12 inch cut into my hip and nerves.  what!?  get high?  if i wanted to do that i would stay at home with my drug of choice and company of choice.  it would not be any opioids. the last night i was there the dr writing orders for that floor told me that if my pain was seven or above what i was suppose to have.  even though the nurses were nice and probably over worked, i was not given anything for pain from six that evening until six in the morning. i heard my nurse at the station discussing my case with the charge nurse.  she admitted not giving me anything and was afraid she would lose her job.  the charge asked her if i was a trouble maker or if i could have been drinking.  what?  i told them to come into my room if they wanted to talk about me.  my nurse apologized and i understood.  i did tell the charge what i heard her saying about me, not knowing me at all. i, like many in this town knows what to expect when being at oroville hospital.  people make mistakes, but this whole experience from the pain level i endured, to the surgeon not noticing my platelet level, to the surgeon showing no concern or compassion for his patient, was nothing that anyone should experience.  i did not mention his name.  i have a wonderful general practice physician that did notice my labs.  i'm now with an oncologist.  she has been great also.  and again, the nurses were very pleasant, but should give you the medicine that the dr writing the orders believes you need.  i would tell them my pain level and they did not treat it accordingly.  if there is any dispute with what i am saying, i can provide proof.  i took my phone to record or document just this kind of thing.  if not, thanks for listening.  you do have some wonderful nurses and physical therapists.
sheila mastelotto

overall my experiences at scripps encinitas have been relatively positive for having to stay in the hospital. i've also stayed at scripps encinitas about 6 times over the last 3 years, so i know how the process works, and knowing what to expect is helpful. 

positives:
1. treated quickly (this has to do with the condition i have), unfortunately, if you have a broken arm, just like most hospitals, it will probably take longer to be treated.
2. er is a major improvement from 10 years ago, private rooms with doors.
3. good experience with every doctor i've had.
4. i've only had to share a room 2 out of 7 times, however this also had to do with my condition. 
5. they allowed my boyfriend/fiance/and now husband to stay overnight with me when i was in my own room.
6. 90%+ of nurses i've had here have been helpful and sweet.
7. the billing process has significantly improved through online portal.
8. access to medical records and tests as well as communication online is helpful.
9. pcu and the standard hospital rooms on that floor are very nice. 

possible negatives:
1. possibility of not having a private room. this is huge for me. if you are sick, in pain, and recovering, you want your own space and a space for someone to stay with you. all new hospitals in the san diego area are required to have their own rooms now, i'm sure they will get there and understand it's a big undertaking, but it makes a big difference for experience and patient care. 
2. nurse response time - this can be long (i never experienced longer than 20-30 minutes at any given time), and i understand that there are tons of other patients to care for, however, if you are not allowed to get up to go to the bathroom by yourself or your pain really spikes 20-30 minutes can seem like forever. overall, the response time was adequate. 
3. lack of communication between doctors & nurses. i felt like i had to advocate and/or repeat for myself on several occasions. maybe notes weren't written down, maybe doctors don't always read them, who knows. my surgeon also has privileges at this hospital but is not based out of scripps encinitas, so there may be some gaps due to that.
4. not all of the hospital is updated. some floors and areas are, but some feel pretty old.

after my friend fell in january of 2019 and was not found for over three days, she was in dire physical condition and required a tracheostomy to stop recurring pneumonia infections. once stabilized, she was moved to barlow respiratory hospital, one of the best facilities of its kind in the country. here she had the medical and physiotherapy attention she required as well as a staff willing to take the time to understand her.

this was a woman who had no family and no medical coverage (although i had applied for medicare on her behalf at this point). this made no difference to the quality of her treatment by the people at barlow.

although her body had betrayed her, her acute intelligence was still there, something other facilities ignored. as a result, even after she improved to the point where she was breathing on her own and able to talk with a pmv and was moved to a nursing home, she never ceased wanting to go back to barlow.

six month later following more episodes of pneumonia, she did get to go back.  and, again, received the same great medical attention, the same personalized care by the staff and, again, her condition improved to the point that she could communicate with people even without the pmv.

eventually, all her determination could not will her body back to health and it finally gave out but, to the end, she appreciated the doctors and staff at barlow who took care of her physical challenges and made her life worth more than just existing and, especially, those who enjoyed her twisted sense of humor.

if i could rate this place zero stars i would, the visit was a nightmare from start to finish. i came in to the er on a weekend with agonizing abdominal pain. i'd heard the horror stories about this place but i was very new to the area and was in such intense pain that i just wanted to get the closest care possible. i was triaged and put in a waiting room where i was left to sit in pain for an hour and a half. then finally, i was brought back to what i thought would finally be my room, but i was just placed in another waiting room where i sat for another 30 minutes. i appreciate that there is a lot going on behind the scenes that contributes to long wait times in the er, but this hospital was seemingly empty, with staff just standing around talking. 

finally i get brought back to a room and see the doctor (oluwaseye acabi). nobody asked me for a list of medications i was currently on or for any sort of medical history. i explain to him that i was having severe abdominal pain and that i had an iud and a history of bad ovarian cysts. i told him that i was afraid that either my iud had migrated or i had a cyst that was causing my ovary to twist (which would need to be treated immediately if that were the case). he proceeded to tell me that the iud migrating would be impossible after having it in for a year already. 

he then asked me if i wanted a pelvic exam and/or an ultrasound, which i thought was odd considering he was supposed to be the expert and should know what he needs to do to figure out and solve the problem. i said yes to both. he started the pelvic exam and it was by far the weirdest and most uncomfortable pelvic exam i have ever had. it was clear that he didn't know what he was doing, but i'll leave out the graphic details. 

he then tells me that i am welcome to wait for an ultrasound but that i "wasn't a priority" and would be waiting all night. at this point i was so fed up, tired, and in so much pain that i just wanted to go home and get in bed, there were no beds in the rooms for me to try and get comfortable in while i waited, so i told them to discharge me. 

they came in with the discharge papers and they'd given me bs diagnoses of pelvic inflammatory disease and dehydration. he also prescribed me antibiotics (which i didn't take because i had a feeling i didn't need them, and my obgyn confirmed), and muscle relaxers. mind you, they never took down my medications so they would have never known if i had any medicines that would interact. 

as i'm being discharged, he comes in and tells me "oh by the way, during your pelvic, i couldn't find the strings to your iud. i didn't look any further because i didn't want to inconvenience you." i am still confused as to how he would have "inconvenienced me" by doing his job and investigating the problem that brought me to him in the first place. 

so i went home and stayed in extreme pain until i could get in with my obgyn. within seconds, my ultrasound tech was able to tell me that my iud was embedded in the wall of my uterus and needed to be taken out (something the er doctor told me was impossible, if you remember). when my doctor came in she did a pelvic and was instantly able to see my iud strings clear as day... the ones the er doctor claimed he couldn't find. 

i've been to a lot of bad doctors and hospitals and had a lot of bad experiences but this one takes the cake. i paid $500 to wait around in pain and to be treated with extreme negligence and incompetence. stay far away.

during covid-19, right after the travel ban, i was on quarantine for 14 days since i arrived from europe on vacation.  during that time, i fell ill and after a few days under virtual care, my doctor advised me to go to the er.  i chose memorial hermann sugar land thinking i would get good care.  i was totally wrong.

once in the er, which was set up efficiently because of the virus, the er doctor immediately explained to me that they will not send my covid-19 test off to be tested unless i was admitted to the hospital.  his main concern was not diagnosing my problem but explaining that i would have to go somewhere else to get tested for covid-19.

i was advised to go the the er by my doctor because i was coughing excessively, barely able to breath, experiencing pain in my back when breathing and coughing, wheezing and extreme shortness of breath even with using an inhaler.  my temp stayed below 100.4 so it wasn't considered a fever.

the er began to run tests:  chest x-rays, ct scan, urine-analysis, blood-work, i.v., etc.

i waited about 45 minutes for all the test results to return and during that time, i suffered and tried to breath over and over in spite of the difficulties i was experiencing.  finally, the er doctor returned (dr. b. parker) and said that my lungs were clear and that the covid-19 swab would not be sent to the lab because i'm not being admitted to the hospital.  i stated that i understood about the swab but i didn't understand what was going on with my breathing so i asked him again about my lungs.  dr. parker repeated that my lungs were "all clear" and that there was no sign of the virus in my lungs. 

i asked the doctor what was he diagnosing me as having. since we know there's no sign of covid-19 in my lungs, what is it then and what was he going to give me to help me breath.   dr. parker turned the paper around and it read, "cough - adult".  i asked, "so you're diagnosing me as having a cough?"  he replied yes.  i was dumbfounded.  i came to the er with a cough and shortness of breath and now the dr. was telling me that i had a cough.  wow!  

i asked him what was he going to do about helping me?  he stated that he was calling in prescriptions to my pharmacy to take but to act like i had covid-10 and still isolate.  he stated that he believed it was just an allergy infection and that these meds would clear it up.  i informed him that i don't typically suffer with allergies and that i had been taking zyrtec because the virtual doctor i spoke to recommended it but i wasn't getting any better.  he reemphasized again that the test would not be sent and that if i wanted a covid-19 test, i needed to go to another site.  i asked about an antibiotic to clear up the infection and he said the meds he prescribed would clear up the infection.  i later learned that the meds were regular over-the-counter stuff that i had already been using that wasn't effective:  tylenol, mucinex and claritin-d.

i believe dr. parker's only concern was covid-19 and not finding the real source of my problems.  i asked my discharge nurse again about my lungs being "all clear" and she said well they are not all clear and that they had a haze over them.  i asked what does a haze mean.  she informed me that the doctor believes the haze is possibly from a bacteria infection from allergies so he's prescribed some meds to help.  i again said i don't suffer with allergies but ok the pollen is high so i guess.  

i was discharged and walked to my car still struggling to breath just the same way as i walked into the hospital.   

that was saturday, march 21st. fast forward to wednesday, march 25th and i was not feeling any better, in fact, i felt worse. i called my doctor both the 25th and 26th and left messages. her nurse called my back on the 27th and informed me to stop taking all allergy meds immediately and that she had reviewed the labs and x-rays and they believe that haze over my right lung is pneumonia.

pneumonia?!!  so i had pneumonia in the right lung for an additional 6 days without any treatment?!  why would dr. parker say i was "all clear" and ignore the haze?  i had to take additional time from work to heal whereas if dr. parker would have just taken the time to explore my results for something more than covid-19, he could have treated me correctly and i could have returned back to work without taking additional time.  

lastly, once i got the bill, i saw that i was billed $273.50 for a pregnancy test!!!  the admitting nurse asked if there was anyway i could be pregnant, i immediately answered no and explained why i couldn't be.  so why would you give me, a 49 yr old woman with a valid reason a pregnancy test?  especially for $273.50.  over billing???   yes!

i will never go back to memorial hermann sugar land emergency room.  the care of the treating physician was below sub-par and i could have saved way more time and money going to another facility.

the physicians here are stunningly incompetent and lazy.  running ventilators on a peep of 0?! that's truly malpractice. no wonder nobody ever got better.  one physician has signs posted all around the nurses station - "do not call me for anything overnight unless it's an emergency! i will put in orders in the morning."  yeah when that emergency finally happened, 5 hours of calling later never heard back from him and sadly the patient didn't make it to the morning.

call light system....was those bells that you ding ding ding like at the front of a hotel lobby. no joke you'd hear all these bells and you'd wander the hall trying to figure out who was calling.

and so much more.  none of this stuff is normal.  this is a criminal organization role playing as a hospital.  you would literally be better off dying at home than coming to this place.  i was asked to extend here but i told them i felt like a bad person working there.

i discovered that she was put on the covid-19 floor even though she did not have the virus. i was told that everyone goes to that unit until their test comes back negative twice. then they are moved to another floor.

the day after she was admitted i called her and there was an ear piercing alarm going off in her room. her door was shut and the call button was not within her reach. she was in tears because this noise was nonstop for who knows how long and it was ear deafening! she said it goes off in the middle of the night when she is sleeping and wakes her.  i immediately hung up and called the nurses station. when the nurse picked up her phone i told her the situation and she literally laughed! oh yes, she said, when you have an intravenous tube in your arm that alarm goes off if you bend your elbow. i was in disbelief! how could you subject an 85 year old to this who can't get out of bed and can't reach her call button and you have her door closed?

also, her phone was put in a place where she could not reach it when i called. this happened more than once! trying to get someone at the nurses desk/station to help with this situation was a horrendous experience!!! if they answer the phone they might transfer you to your loved ones nurse who might answer their phone, but might not.

 one day i called the nurses desk for the second time because i couldn't reach my sister, and the nurse that picked up could hear me fine until i asked to speak to my sisters nurse.  she then did the "hello? hello? hello? i can't hear you" act and then hung up on me.  her name is bethany on the third floor.  she could hear me fine! 

 two days later, after putting in 8 phone calls in over a half hour, i finally got my sisters nurse, who had to check first to see if she was his patient, although i was told later that he had seen her that morning. i told him what i had been through and how frustrated i was at that point so he than told me he would walk in there with his phone so i could talk to her, but once again the phone hung up before that happened. my 9th phone call, the operator told me she would connect me to the floor supervisor who assured me he would make sure that my sisters nurse would call me right back.

he called and told me he was with my sister but that he was having a hard time waking her. she would open her eyes but than close them immediately. he said "i don't know if this is her base line."
i couldn't believe my ears. no, i said this is not her baseline! he didn't know her baseline? he had not been informed when he came on shift of the condition of his patients? she is like you or i, very alert, talking and awake during the day. there's something wrong with her! i don't know how long she was in this state. 

turns out they thought she had a stroke! they hadn't even noticed! thank goodness i insisted the nurse go in and check on her! later the neurologist called who hadn't even examined my sister, this was on may 26th, and told me the report said she had fainted. when i questioned this, in a smart ass way her reply was "were you there? because the last time i checked relatives and visitors are not allowed in the hospital because of covid-19." (i wish i could remember her name.) yes, i was there, on the phone, and she did not faint! 

they claimed it was a sudden change, that she was awake and talking that morning. so i ask why did the nurse not know that comatose was not her baseline then.? it just doesn't add up.

my sister is still there and today she was not answering her phone again. when i called the nurses station for room 428 the nurse that picked up told me that "her board did not show that anyone was in that room". what????????? she has been in that room now for 2 days.  i hung up and called the hospital operator who assured me that my sister was in room 428 and asked if i would like to be connected with her nurses cell phone. thank goodness for the operators at fawcett memorial hospital. they were the only ones that were truly helpful. if it weren't for them i would have gone out of my mind!

doc_text:
my husband went to scripps memorial la jolla for help because he was having difficulty using his arms and legs for basic, everyday things.  it was a fast, steep decline for someone who until that point was in reasonable shape, and not long before that served in the military.  this was essentially a last resort, and we decided to go after he was almost totally unable to use his legs for about two weeks.  

enter dr. lisa m. morikado.  she immediately seemed more annoyed than concerned, which was honestly pretty baffling to us at the time.  she had no interest in running any tests or imaging - we had to specifically ask that she do so because what she apparently wanted to do, was nothing.

things got even worse when she told my husband she thought he was lying about his symptoms and condition.  she went on to rush us out of the er with absolutely nothing accomplished, other than her telling us to follow up with primary care.  lisa morikado doesn't think that the sudden inability to use one's legs warrants a spot in a hospital bay.  the same minute i left my husband's bed to go get a snack at the cafeteria, morikado went in to tell my husband that he didn't need to be there, and he was getting discharged.  it's almost like she has extensive experience avoiding liability for negligence.  we were exhausted, defeated, and realized we weren't going to get any meaningful help, so we left.

at the time we lived on a third floor with no elevator.  i was pregnant and did my best to painstakingly help my husband up the stairs one at a time.  it took about 20 minutes and was agonizing for him, even though he was mostly supporting himself with me and the handrails.

conclusive diagnostics would have been nice.  being treated with basic human dignity would have been better.  we received neither from dr. morikado.

sadly, i'm not the first person to wonder if race played a predominant role in what occurred here.  what's even sadder, is that if other reviews are accurate, the patient liaison might not help you either.

what a sad, sad way to treat someone.  doctors have an incredible power - that is the power to help people.  in my opinion, it's perfectly ok for a doctor to think that their patient is feigning or exaggerating injury.  the problem is when doctors refuse to treat a patient on account of that opinion.  think about that.  we all have inherent biases, and one way doctors can avoid them in medicine is to have standards and run the same tests on every patient based on the symptoms they describe, regardless of personal opinions.  that's not what happened here.

i had to re-write this review from scratch so that it would fit within yelp's character limits.  that should say something.

my husband is now permanently disabled.  he's a runner and can't run - he's a computer programmer and can't type.  i want to thank you for doing next to nothing and treating him like he's subhuman.  thank you.

doc_text: it has taken me awhile to decide if i was going to share my mother's story while hospitalized at peacehealth.  i've decided it's important to do so in order to let the community understand what happens within those four walls.  my mother was admitted april 27th, 2019 with severe sepsis.  she was admitted to the icu by dr. chen, at the time of admission it was asked kris keough (hospital ethicist) not be involved in her care.  after 24 hours in the icu she was transferred to the fourth floor.  my mother had been admittted to this floor before and it had always been a nightmare, we should have requested a different or better yet be transferred out of this hospital.  april 29th my mother was working very hard to breathe, mind you my sister and i are both nurses and we know our mom's medical history and we know her very well.  we told the evening nurse, she told the physician and no new orders.  this was dr. eric yang. shift change came and again we were persistent that she was working entirely too hard to breathe and told the nurse shelly a. multiple times and requested her to be evaluated by a physician.  the nurse kept telling us the physician was doing an admit and would see her after.  we went to the charge nurse several times.  finally when my sister went to the charge nurse and asked for hospice medications to make my mother comfortable because that's where we were heading a physician magically appeared, it only took three hours.  upon obtaining my mother's medical records shelly had time to document how upset we were but not time to advocate for my mom.  my mom continued to decline over the next few days and despite our continued verbal concern to physicians and nurses it seemed to fall on deaf ears.  on 5/2 i spoke with the evening jacqueline m. and i requested medication for her breathing, she did request the medication but also had time to turn up my mother's oxygen to 4 liters (my mother retained co2) turning up her oxygen only caused her to retain co2 as she was already retaining fluids and working to breathe.  the next morning she was transferred to the icu with chf and respiratory failure.  the physician following her was chi-chang yen who told us on her icu admission he felt he could pull her through this.  we were very present in the icu only leaving at bedtime and back in the am.  our only mistake was asking kris keough the ethicist not to be involved in my mother's care. we only saw dr. yen on her icu admission and never came back at all during her admission to speak with my sister or myself, we were both her poa's. on friday may 3rd physician rounding was taking place and visitors are asked to leave.  kris keoug went into my mother's room and told her she was dying.  she told this to my mother alone with no support person in the room.  not only doing this to my mom there was never a family conference to discuss my mom's care or she may not survive this hospitalization.  kris came to the waiting room, blindsided us and stood over us with arms crossed and stated, "you're mom has chosen to go to hospice and she will be there by one o'clock and everyone will be much more comfortable."  my mom was very upset and we were so blindsided and couldn't think to say no let's slow down, she had been in the icu less than 48 hours.  kris was not the doctor and dr. yen never once said my mother was dying to my sister or myself.  upon obtaining medical records dr. yen falsely documented there was a family conference held and it was a family decision for hospice.  it was a forced blindsided decision in my opinion.  i did dispute the documentation and dr. yen again said his documentation was accurate.  i was told by the qi coordinator molly b. "everybody has a different definition of a family conference."   there was not a family conference held the risk manager dan is well aware of this and he stated "kris felt she knew you and your sister and felt it wasn't needed."  she didn't know me and knew my sister on a professional level only. i met with senior leadership and there were changes that came out of my mother's hospitalization and death, two of the most important family is no longer asked to leave the icu during physician rounding and  there is a phone number in each room on the white board to call if family or patients feel they are not getting the care they need.  hopefully there  were  more and nursing staff and kris has learned from this situation and the outcome. our parents do not live forever and i completely understand this but how this was handled made everything traumatic for my mom and her family, something that is almost unforgivable.  i would not recommend this hospital and wish i would have taken my mom elsewhere unfortunately it wasn't an option as sick as she was.

i just gave your hospital how much revenue and you are telling me to not ask questions about my care? what is that? isn't that my rite as a patient? that is confusing and rather irritating. after he left my room, he then ordered a brace for my wrist although the incision is by my knuckles. i asked to speak to him as this didn't make sense and he was charging my insurance for it(you can see the money theme starting, can't you?). i was told that he wouldn't be coming in my room again. i asked for a patient advocate. i got the er manager. that is akin to asking for a democrat and getting mitch mcconnell; farthest thing from the request. the er manager told me that dr russell had already come in my room multiple times to talk to me about my care and that he would not be coming in again. i responded that he had only come in twice. the er manager pretty much told me i was lying without having the guts to just state her claim. own your sh*t, woman. i asked her to bring dr russell in so we could get to the bottom of this(remember: st johns is still getting paid for my visit: $$$). the er manager said no. i told her she could look at the security cameras to see i was telling the truth. i was ignored. why would you not look at the evidence that would point you to the truth? that is moronic. long story short: i was essentially escorted out of the er by the er manager who brought in security guards to help. i'm 5'7", 117 lbs and i have one working hand. i'm not a real threat and i'm getting escorted out for not paying a copay? i wish you good luck with your loved ones in combating this dreadful disease.

buyers beware! this hospital is known for unethical billing practices. you will be charged for services far higher than market average. 

we recently had an ultrasound completed on my pregnant wife at an outpatient doctor's office located near saint mary's hospital.  we received a bill from the doctor's office for the services.  we then received a second bill from st. mary's hospital charging us again for an ultrasound.  why would we receive a hospital bill when we were never in the hospital, we were in a doctors office? this bill was for over $5000 and was billed as if my wife was in the hospital as a patient. we went to an outpatient office. we have been to other physicians in this same building (which is not the hospital) and were never charged as if we were using inpatient services. after further research i found that this is over ten times the cost of this service looking at national and local averages.  we also were not admitted in saint mary's hospital.  

after calling to review these charges with bon secours customer service they informed us that we would have to take this issue up with the billing department of the doctor's office.  once we spoke with the doctor's office they said that it was a bill from saint mary's hospital and would have to be handled by them.  after calling bon secours back, they gave me the name of a contact that all billing complaints go through.  they refused to give me her email or phone number.  they said all issues must be through hand written letters.  we contacted her stating our issues and after some time received a letter back.  the contact only offered services which are openly provided through customer service (pay balance right now 15% discount or set up monthly payment plan).  wrote contact back trying to get explanation of charges and cited local health care cost averages for ultrasounds.  stated that these charges were billed unethically (as if we were admitted in the hospital) and that costs of services were not within market value and were not discussed with us ahead of time.  we waited a couple months and heard nothing back.  we called their customer service and they told us our letter was received and under review.  we waited a couple more months and a collection notice came in the mail from bon secours.  we called their customer service back and let them know about this issue and that it had been under review.  they stated the bill was unpaid and therefore sent to collections.  we were never able to speak with anyone with autonomy, were billed extremely unethically and nobody from their organization would directly communicate with us about their bill.  my wife and i have high credit scores and always pay our bills in accordance with our responsibilities.  this company refused to openly communicate with us or explain their absurd billing practices.  buyers beware!!! there are many other companies providing the same services in our area with far better customer service and for far cheaper.

so i'm a teen who's struggled with depression and anxiety in my life. my parents made me attend a program called aspire, which you may or may not heard of. it's a group therapy program meant for people like me who struggle with mental illnesses and uses a thing called dbt. the program is 10 weeks for middle schoolers and 8 for high schoolers, but there's a 2 week period before that, so technically it's even longer. 

during the program, i felt pressured to pretend everything was okay, just to avoid confrontation with the staff and an even longer period of stay. i have trauma, but i feel like it was ignored by staff, simply being told to "use coping skills" despite the fact i feel more comfortable doing them by myself. i have issues discussing things with my family in the room, specifically my parents, but i was forced to do so, despite the fact it's a trigger for both my trauma and anxiety. one of the staff there even triggered an episode for me, too, pressuring me into saying i had an addiction despite the fact that i didn't, and guilted me into saying i had one during our unit on negative addiction. i've had my stuff taken away from me multiple times, which has consistently been a small backpack with a sketchbook, personal sketchbook for coping, pen and pencil, and a book for reading. it was called a "schoolbag" by the staff, which they had to take away because they don't want me doing homework, despite the fact i was mostly in the program during the summer. additionally, the skills we were leaning for coping were things i already knew and was using, and the program taught us, how i like to describe it, how to be a human being. 

the environments there aren't great either. the room you're in for the first two weeks has gray walls and flooring, and is very cold. there's no table either, and you sit in chairs in a circle while the staff member explains things with a whiteboard. there's no windows in this room. after that, there's two other rooms you use. there's a meeting room, which has one wall with windows, and fluctuated between hot and cold. there's also a whiteboard here for the staff to write on. there's a table here and the colors of the room are bright compared to the first one. the next room is meant for creatives, like making art and projects in the program. this is the best room, since it has decorated walls and two walls with windows on them. there's also a whiteboard in here, and the walls are a similar color to the last room. this room is cold, but only a little. the break room is for in between lessons, and has one wall with windows and is colored like the last two rooms. it's small and doesn't fit the amount of people in it well. the temperature changes in here too. 

at the end of the program, they made me fill out a sheet on who i could contact when i needed help, and they had me show it to my parents. by now, i think you can assume i have trauma stemming from negative experiences with my family, so i didn't feel comfortable doing this. however, since they forced me to do so (with the threat of more of this program looming over my head), i did it regardless of how i felt. at the end of it all, they said i didn't qualify for medication for any of my illnesses and disorders, and all i can assume is that because they thought i got better in the program and by the end it wasn't bad enough to assign any, despite the fact it got worse afterwards a few months later i proceeded to engage in self harm. in fact, the program made me feel worse than i had felt going into it, since not only did staff take away my methods of coping and trigger episodes of anxiety, depression, and trauma, everyone else in the program actually had genuine problems, which resulted in me feeling like my problems were insignificant and didn't matter, furthering my problems. 

luckily, they referred me to a new therapist (i had been seeing one before aspire) who i actually felt comfortable with, and i was able to open up to. one of the positives that came out of this, other than possibly more trauma, is that i got officially diagnosed with autism. honestly, i'm happy i was able to get this diagnosis, since i've always had little quirks, but i didn't know why before they told me. 

but other than that, the program was horrible for my mental health, despite how they say they help people get better. i felt like staff didn't care for me, and that they disregarded my reactions to things and situations. with staff triggering episodes for me, and some actually seeing it happen in front of them, i got little to no comfort from them. they didn't care that having to talk about my problems in front of my family was a trigger for me, and that it was a huge issue for my mental state, despite the fact it happened multiple times. 

if you care about your kids wellbeing, send them somewhere else. even the patients i was with hated it there, and were there because family forced them to go, much like mine.

#1 son had swelling on his face and feeling lethargic and urgent care saw something suspicious on his chest x-ray so they sent us here to the ermmediately. 

this is my first experience with this hospital, it is closest to our new retirement town and it takes approximately 20-25 minutes by car to get here unless of course the seasonal traffic is heavy. that's a big change for me since,  in all the 12 states that i have lived in, i have always been pretty close to an er. but it is what it is. 

the covid protocols are very strictly enforced here, there's a person asking questions and taking temperatures outside and they give you a mask if you don't have one. they only allow adult patients to enter however i am my son's medical proxy so i accompanied him for the whole process. 

the wait didn't look bad at all however the urgent care called ahead and we were taken right away. i worked in er's for several years both in the navy and in a civilian trauma center so my critique will be from an insiders prospective.

the receptionists demeanor, efficient and professionalism was very good. we made it through the paperwork and were taken back very quickly. once inside there was a triage nurse who whisked us into an exam bay, two other nurses quickly hooked matt up to a monitor and got his vitals while putting in an iv line. they drew blood from the iv, which proved to later be a problem, and the portable x-ray was done within minutes. 

a phlebotomist arrived in approximately ten minutes to draw five new tubes of blood commenting that the nurses needed to get up to speed on their, apparently new, iv setups as the original draws had hemolized. that's an unfortunate error because blood sticks are sometimes difficult and of course more unnecessary blood draws are not a good practice for time and for the patient. 

moving on, dr. ronnie sims came in within a half hour of our arrival and assured us that the chest x-ray was just fine and after asking some good questions he just wanted to draw another set of enzymes to make sure that there were no cardiac issue. 

the blood draw was taken quickly however the turnaround was an hour, which could have been done in fifteen minutes, but once they got the results we were expeditiously discharged out and we're on our way. 

there's no way for me to know if our experience was typical for this er, since we have nothing to compare it to, but overall they staff did a very nice job. 

bottom line: #1 son is well and this hospital er does a very nice job!

doc_text: although my experience is not recent, i believe it's indicative of the care at mayo. while in the air force, i was diagnosed with mononeuritis multiplex and left partly because of my symptoms (difficulties walking, balance, pain, numbness).  a couple of years after separating, i was diagnosed with ms and went to the va to confirm the diagnosis. the va referred me to a neurologist who found i didn't have ms. he referred me to mayo clinic scottsdale. when i came to mayo, i spent less than 10 minutes with the neurologist who specializes in peripheral neuropathy and started two days of testing. after the testing, the neurologist spent another 5 minutes with me and said he we would let me know his diagnosis. after a couple of weeks, i received a letter which basically said i didn't have peripheral neuropathy. but he also sent me the letter intended for the referring doctor which said that whatever was wrong was in my head and if i continued to complain i should be referred to psychiatric care. i was stunned, disappointed, and felt betrayed. i had spent $2000 over what my insurance had payed to get nothing but disrespect. over the next several years, my symptoms became worse and worse until i was disabled after a surgery. i could not walk, had constant pain, and felt terrible. i was referred by barrow neurological to a neurologist who spent an hour with me, performed both an emg and an ecv, and diagnosed me with hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsy (hnpp). finally, a meaningful diagnosis. there's no treatment but at least i have an idea what's wrong. mayo is a brand. it doesn't have any greater ability to diagnosis disease but continues to pull people in with stories of success when there are probably far more stories like mine that are never heard.

i can't even begin to express my gratitude to the staff in the emergency department, and all of the other nurses, doctors, and technicians who treated me with extraordinary patience and kindness during my stay at mercy general.

doc_text: i wasn't happy with my emergency room experience here, but they more than made up for it with how they took care of one of my loved ones. when they went to the emergency room here we never could have guessed that they had a serious issue that would require them to stay several days. from the moment they arrived they received excellent, caring help from all of the staff. the nurses and the hospitalists were especially wonderful. we were so delighted to find there were private rooms, which made such a difference in the healing process. many hospitals have very restrictive visiting hours but that's certainly not the case here. do you want to have four people in the room at the same time? a social worker who's very familiar with all the nursing homes in this county says, "creekside is about one and a half stars out of five."

finally i get brought back to a room and see the doctor (oluwaseye acabi). nobody asked me for a list of medications i was currently on or for any sort of medical history. i explain to him that i was having severe abdominal pain and that i had an iud and a history of bad ovarian cysts. i told him that i was afraid that either my iud had migrated or i had a cyst that was causing my ovary to twist (which would need to be treated immediately if that were the case). he proceeded to tell me that the iud migrating would be impossible after having it in for a year already. 

he then asked me if i wanted a pelvic exam and/or an ultrasound, which i thought was odd considering he was supposed to be the expert and should know what he needs to do to figure out and solve the problem. i said yes to both. he started the pelvic exam and it was by far the weirdest and most uncomfortable pelvic exam i have ever had. it was clear that he didn't know what he was doing, but i'll leave out the graphic details. 

he then tells me that i am welcome to wait for an ultrasound but that i "wasn't a priority" and would be waiting all night. at this point i was so fed up, tired, and in so much pain that i just wanted to go home and get in bed, there were no beds in the rooms for me to try and get comfortable in while i waited, so i told them to discharge me. 

they came in with the discharge papers and they'd given me bs diagnoses of pelvic inflammatory disease and dehydration. he also prescribed me antibiotics (which i didn't take because i had a feeling i didn't need them, and my obgyn confirmed), and muscle relaxers. mind you, they never took down my medications so they would have never known if i had any medicines that would interact. 

as i'm being discharged, he comes in and tells me "oh by the way, during your pelvic, i couldn't find the strings to your iud. i didn't look any further because i didn't want to inconvenience you." i am still confused as to how he would have "inconvenienced me" by doing his job and investigating the problem that brought me to him in the first place.

i've been to a lot of bad doctors and hospitals and had a lot of bad experiences but this one takes the cake. i paid $500 to wait around in pain and to be treated with extreme negligence and incompetence. stay far away.

this review is for the er and hospital.

what i thought was a routine visit to my cardiologist suddenly turned south when, after some testing, he announced i had to get to the er immediately. that's how i found myself here in the emergency room being told i needed triple bypass heart surgery. 

spoiler alert: i'm still alive

the surgeon (dr. hargrove) was confident and calming. she proved to be exceptionally skilled and performed a successful surgery despite some minor complications along the way. i can't speak highly enough about her.

during several days of recovery, my nurses - there were many - and their support staff were competent, caring and all-around fantastic. actually there was one exception but i believe it was due to inexperience. i was impressed with all the controls they had in place to protect patients while this 2020 pandemic is going on.

as expected, the food was generally lousy although breakfasts were okay. the beds were not the most comfortable. and if you want a good night's sleep a hospital is not the place to be, between getting poked for blood tests all night and patients in other rooms making every type of noise imaginable echo down the hallways. most recovery rooms are double occupancy but i was lucky to have a private room so my stay was probably better than most. 

follow up by cardiac rehab and my surgeon was excellent. 

i certainly hope you won't ever need to come here but if you do, rest assured they will take good care of you. a 4.5 rating from me.

i have had both private and kaiser insurance, so i feel qualified to comment and compare the two systems.  been to private physicians in the bay area (including stanford and ucsf), have had lab and radiology services, and hospitalizations up and down the peninsula over the past 30 years.  i realize people have individual experiences that may not be like mine.

kaiser ssf is designed to handle large volumes of people more efficiently, so it is in some ways less personal medicine.  one can sometimes feel like cattle. however, i don't need a lot of hand holding, and i love kaiser ssf for its relative efficiency.  i've been going to kaiser now as my primary insurance for over 15 years, because i find my coordinated care to be far better than through private insurance.  i like the fact that i can see another doctor in the kaiser system in a timely fashion if my doctor is unavailable.  i like having my meds mailed to me. flu shots are super easy.  your preventive care schedules (immunizations, colonoscopy, mammograms etc) are tracked and you are informed in writing.  

at kaiser ssf, i have never had to wait more than 5-15 minutes for an x-ray or mri or ct or a blood draw.  er was reasonably quick the one time i was there -- i was able to check in and be seen and get a ct, then out the door in about 90 minutes.  the er doctor was kind but also very businesslike and to the point, which was appreciated. the er staff also scheduled an appointment for a specialist for the next morning, so that i wouldn't have to do it myself.  i really appreciated their thoughtfulness. in private practice facilities, i've had to wait over 2 hours for a pre-scheduled simple chest x-ray; over 30 minutes for a lab; and weeks for a doctor's appointment. 

quality of doctors --- i have had some really great doctors over the years at kaiser and outside of kaiser.  (exception: i liked my obgyn and dermatology doctors outside of kaiser better.) my internist, oncologist, and surgeon at kaiser are as knowledgeable and skillful as the ones i had outside of kaiser, but unlike the others, my kaiser doctors talk to each other so the care is coordinated each step of the way.  

my personal feeling is that private practice care is fractured -- the doctors can't talk to each other, and reimbursements with in-network/out-of-network facilities and providers are a real pain. it's sad, and all created because some mbas out there thought they had a better business model.  they broke it, and we will never have american medicine the way it used to be.

i returned to cedars sinai for extensive treatment:  surgery on both feet resulted in complications - an incurable nerve condition in both feet (that potentially can worsen and in some people becomes totally crippling) that has left me with permanent damage, ongoing significant pain, and difficulty walking.  i do not fault the surgeon; this condition can occur after surgery or body trauma.  to stop the spread and treat this, i ended up using the pain center, going for bilateral sympathetic nerve blocks under anesthesia twice a week for more than six months plus some other procedures and another "revision" surgery on both feet a year later that included a short inpatient stay for an intravenous treatment.  that intravenous treatment was to be performed by a doc other than my pain center doctor (who doesn't do in hospital procedures) but needed to be done same day as my surgery to avoid hypoglycemic problems (fasting overnight for surgery and no food for this next procedure).  when this procedure got held up overnight and then was to occur - with no food - hours later the next day, i called a halt to protect myself/my health.  a major "incident" occurred (this "prima donna" doctor tried to kick me out of the hospital without me getting the prescribed treatment, i objected and reached out to cedars' management, head of the department was called to intervene, and finally my inpatient stay to do the intravenous procedure was extended a couple of days and my regular pain center doc enlisted to do the procedure (although i was supposed to have the intravenous procedure twice and was shortchanged with only one).  when i was in the process of scheduling my next pain center outpatient block, i suddenly received a letter from the head of cedars' administration informing me cedars would no longer treat me effective immediately and i should seek medical care elsewhere!  the politics due to one doctor's ego prevailed.  technically that constitutes "patient abandonment" - and it violates state legal/regulatory/medical board rules, particularly given i was in the course of treatment for a serious medical condition.  add to that very few doctors - even in a city as big as los angeles with all its fine hospitals and medical schools specialize in/treat my condition (complex medical pain syndrome) - and it takes months to get an appointment with those specialists, and i got left high and dry.  while i could have initiated action against cedars, i did not:  i was also in the middle of a move, ended up contracting walking pneumonia and had only a month to move out of my residence, and barely had the resources to survive my other challenges at the time.

i checked into sutter er on march 9th, 2020, because i thought i could be miscarrying my pregnancy and urgent care suggested i go to the er to get an ultrasound. i walked in, the lobby was empty (due to the covid19 scare), sanitized my own seat, and everything went smoothly after checking in. i had no pain, i was offered wheel chairs, but i preferred to walk, the er was also empty, and i even saw nurses sitting and texting on their phones.  i had my blood drawn for standard blood testing and two ultrasounds that showed a baby's heartbeat (i skipped out on the urine test due to lack of cups in the ultrasound room).  on the way out, i asked how much the visit was going to cost me, "$250- do you want to pay now or would you like us to bill you?"- i asked them to send me the bill. i thought this was a pretty successful precautionary visit- until i got the bill.

they are trying to charge me for a level 4 (levels start at 1 and go up to 5- 5 is the most serious and most expensive) service charge. that alone is over $3,000- the charges add up to almost $6,000 not including my insurance coverage. now, i know i walked into an emergency room, and that it would cost more than my less-than-a-hundred-dollars copay, but really?? everything that was done that day could have been done by my doctor and the lab for under $100. i decided i wouldn't dispute the charges for the lab work, doctor's fee, and ultrasounds- but the level 4 charge needed to be reduced. the price is absolutely unjust and unreasonable for the standard service i received.

i called sutter, who directed me to my insurance company, called them and realized the issue was not my insurance...   i called sutter again, was given a number for something i didn't need- i can't tell you how many times i have called or how many people i have talked to, but i would say i talked to at least 5 of the regular billing department agents, and then i asked to escalate it, that was another person, and then i was told to take it up with the er doctor directly, called the er department who gave me to the department manager who needed to talk to the next person...  this has been going on since march. i have played endless phone tag, left messages, and i've gotten the run-around. it is now almost the end of may and i still haven't talked to anyone who can do anything about anything, and i'm damn tired of people trying to explain things to me, when they can't give me answers to questions i have been asking. it is almost time for my bill to get shoveled over to collections because they refuse to help me. 

i can say whole-heartedly that i feel i have been scammed by sutter. i am in the middle of my pregnancy and have canceled all my appointments. i delivered my first baby with sutter, but not this one, not after this wretched experience. how could i ever trust them again?

my body decided to go haywire on me this morning. i was concerned that it could possibly be a very high glucose level, so i headed to the er.

before entering, my temp was taken, and then i checked in. i was only in the waiting room for about 10 minutes.

after i was taken back, i got in my gown, settled onto the gurney, and then shortly after, dr martinez came in.

she has a great bedside manner, and she talked to me about my symptoms, and explained what she was going to do. she then said the nurse would be in shortly.

i was expecting a long wait, because that's how it goes in hospitals, but then about 10 minutes later, nurse jenny came in.

y'all, she is awesome. very nice and funny, and i did not even feel the needle when she drew blood and started an iv. a+ phlebotomy skills. she sent me off to the bathroom to get a urine sample. i told her i didn't know if i could give her anything because i had just gone before i went to the er. she told me that she actually doesn't need much, and that she laughs whenever people give her a full cup back, because it's just overkill. so after i returned with a fuller cup than i expected, i said "i got more than i expected" and she laughed and said "what did i tell you?! i only need a tiny bit!"

anyway, she took my various fluids to be tested, and i settled in with a podcast, anticipating a long wait.

but about 45 minutes later, dr martinez arrived, said my test results all looked great, and determined that the cause was the cough syrup i had been taking for an allergy-induced cough that i've had since march.

she said to follow up about the cough with my primary care, and said she was ready to "bust you outta here."

i got dressed, jenny came in with a note for work and my discharge notes, and off i went.

all in all, i only spent 2 hours in the er. i think that might be some kind of record.

so, if you have to go to this er, and you get dr martinez and/or nurse jenny, you'll definitely be well cared for. if you get both of them together, you've hit the freakin jackpot.

by now, many of my fellow yelpers have heard about my recent battle with brain cancer.  i had no idea that i had a fist sized tumor in my right temple until i had a massive seizure that caused me to throw myself to the flow, striking my side table next to my bed so hard with my jaw that i broke the legs off!  i don't remember any of that but remember waking in the hospital with a breathing tube in my mouth and feeling somewhat confused.

within a few days my surgery was scheduled and they successfully removed a small high grade tumor as well as the massive low grade tumor.  i spent nearly a week in the hospital and must say that everyone i came into contact with was friendly and caring and encouraging, so i felt the care i received throughout my stay (and my recent follow up visits) has been excellent.

even the food from the cafeteria was pretty good.  not high cuisine, but palatable and with enough diversity that i felt like i had decent choices for each meal.  in fact, my only complaint is that they could boost their wifi since over the course of the week, there wasn't much i could do other than take naps.  streaming on my phone was not very successful.  but honestly, i probably needed the naps to recover from the huge surgery (42 staples needed) more than i needed to watch some episode of a tv show.

i feel like the staff was so upbeat and supportive including helping my wife and i find our way around the hospital.  if anything, they may have given too much information upfront since i am not well versed in medical and medicinal terminology.  fortunately, my wife takes great notes and was able to coordinate all my follow-up appointments for me and to fill my pill box so that i took the right pills at the right frequency.

when i met with the surgeon and oncologist, i felt they explained things in terms i could understand and they prepared me for the upcoming challenge of the multi cycle treatment plan which starts next week.  i understand what each phase is supposed to provide and with so many ways of attacking my disease, i am confident that i will one day be back to my independent self.  it won't be easy, but i felt each doctor and nurse i dealt with cared about me and did their best to make sure i knew they were in this fight with me.

on my follow up visit where i was fitted with a radiation mask, i met a completely different set of staff and each of them was equally helpful whether it was on getting registered, or someone escorting us to the right department for our appointments.  just wonderful people who are doing their best to help the patients in their care.  what more can a patient ask for?  i am thankful for the good folks at methodist who literally saved my life.  and despite having an initial prognosis of only having 15 months if i don't continue with treatments, their support and plan gives me hope that i will one day be back to writing more reviews as i explore our state, one county at a time.

methodist is a great place and benefits with its connection to the greater iu health organization including the goodman hall neuroscience center across the street.

thank you to all the staff who took care of me.

i concur with other one star reviews.  this is the worst er i have witnessed.  i am a woman in my 70's.  i tripped and fell on a sidewalk, hitting the left side of my head and left side of my upper body.  there was an abrasion near my eye and a bump on the side of my head. medical people passing by assisted me and gave some basic neuro exams, urging me to go to the er.  that was more than i got at sutter er.

a p.a. interviewed me very briefly after i arrived.  he did not perform even the most cursory exam.  he remained behind a computer and never approached me to check my injuries.  he told me i would have a ct scan to check my brain and sent me back to the waiting room.

i was in the er for 4 hours.  i was never seen by a medical doctor and was never examined by anyone.  i had very sore ribs, sore head, sore jaw, sore upper arm and upper side of back.  there may be something illegal here because patients with medicare must be seen by an m.d. or the plan will not pay.  however, my issue is not the billing, but the situation of malpractice where an elderly patient is never checked for injuries nor given a brief neuro exam after a head and body injury on concrete.

my healing was impaired by my having to sit for hours, in pain, in an uncomfortable, hard plastic chair in the waiting room.  if i could have rested, my healing could have begun more effectively.  i only stayed to get the ct scan.  the waiting room was a very miserable place.  a woman in a wheelchair was brought in with abrasions as though she had been in some sort of accident.  she was moaning in pain and her support person was trying to comfort her.  i guess she was getting the same sort of care that i was getting which was none.  adding the misery of the other patients to my wait, it was the last place anyone would want to be while reacting to a physical trauma.

my experience was in sharp contrast to that of my husband at the sutter, roseville er.  a few years ago when we lived nearby, my husband had an injury similar to mine, but in the house and not on concrete.  he was immediately placed in a wheelchair and wheeled to the beds in the er.  he was seen by a doctor, was made comfortable, interacted with nurses frequently, and had all of the necessary tests from his gurney.  i guess that is what being in a solid middle class area gets you. drive a little further to a better er if you need one.

beware! i know covid-19 is changing life as we know it, but self quarantining and following cdc recommendations is subject to a lot of subjectivity. 

i had an elective retina surgery scheduled at this facility 3/24. i had notified surgeon, primary care physician and lab that i had traveled to italy during the initial phase of the pandemic. i returned and "voluntarily" put myself in 14 day quarantine, as no one in customs or tsa asked me one question about where i had traveled to. my wife and i both quarantined and received return to work authorization from our pcp. we were advised to remain diligent and that if any symptoms presented to contact immediately. 22 days later, and no symptoms, surgery is a go.

with all this noted, i arrived at facility for surgery. wife was asked to remain in car. okay, no problem. she is a health care professional and understood. staff was a little skittish and requested i wear a mask. no problem. surgeon comes to lobby to meet with me and he and anesthesiologist agree to go forward with surgery. nurse invites me back to pre op to prepare. i was asked to sign consent forms and pay my patient share. no problem as we had been advised how much our share would be. i know i am a clean person, but i was told to put on a hair net and surgical booties over my size 15 shoes and put the gown over my street clothes. i was wearing sweat pants that were fully exposed and the booties were stretched just to cling to the soles of my shoes. i questioned how sanitary this was and was told no problem. i asked the nurses if they knew what i should expect post op and they said the surgeon would advise after surgery and that they had no experience with my procedure. now i'm nervous. surprisingly vitals were very good as i was feeling stressed. they dilate my eye with six doses of drops. my eye looked like a possums! heart monitor probes are stuck to my body by reaching down my neck hole in my polo shirt, wires attached and the machine is going crazy. charge nurse comes over and literally asks "is he coding"? now my nerves are freaking out. the other nurse had misplaced the probes. after tearing out chest and belly hair they replaced in correct location. 

machine functioning accurately now. iv started in right hand and ready to move into surgical room. charge nurse appears next to me and says "your surgery is cancelled". i asked what? why. "because i don't feel comfortable" and "the ceo of the surgical center supports my decision". she includes "my husband is also a nurse and he has a covid-19 patient on a ventilator". this is without consulting with the surgeon nor anesthesiologist, who were finishing another procedure. 

they immediately took the iv out and pulled the wires on the probes and told me to leave. i was both pissed and in shock. 

i hadn't brought sunglasses because i assumed i would be leaving there with dressings on my eye. mask still on my face i left office and started toward elevator to go downstairs and out to my wife inhabited parked car. dilated eye didn't appreciate direct sunlight so i went back in and requested sun shield plastic wrap. everyone looked shocked that the "infected one" was back. i also demanded a full refund of my payment. at first they balked, but the office manager had enough sense to provide a refund credit receipt.

i left and not 60 seconds out of the lot the surgeon called and was obviously upset, embarrassed and apologetic. he asked that i keep my follow up appointment the following morning to evaluate my condition.

i told him i refused to go back to that surgical center and he agreed that we could use an alternative further from my home. he said charge nurse is equally abrupt to surgeons and that he would be filing a formal complaint. he said barranca surgical center would be shutting down on 3/26 due to this event and the current state of the pandemic and reopening is pending further review by bod. got hope and realized probes were still attached to my skin/hair. all of them!

surgeon advised me yesterday that my condition had deteriorated since last office visit and surgery is now considered necessary to save my vision. he is trying to schedule another surgical center immediately.

good luck!

thank you again for your team's exceptional attention to our mother's recovery. we want to express our sincere gratitude to the health care workers at kentfield for saving our mom's life and for working to help her regain her independence. our simple expression of gratitude we could repeat thousands of times but could never be enough.
 
we will never forget the nurses, specialists, doctors, and therapists who work day in and day out, tirelessly long hours with determination, big hearts, and compassion.
 
during this shelter in place, it is difficult to be as physically present as we wish we could be for our loved one and so the hospital staff have been our bridge to our mom and stand-in family or friend to comfort and care for our mom.
 
there were staff who especially stood out to us because they took the time and extra effort to give a little bit more to our mom; whether it was in their casual conversation or morning greeting and afternoon/evening check in or taking a little bit of time to do what was beyond their specified job duties. my mom definitely shared with us how she appreciated these.
 
these small but big gestures had a huge impact in my mom's experience and positive recovery. most especially
 
we want to especially thank the staff in particular:
 
eric (concierge): for his kindness and personable attention to our mom, always provided a bright face in the morning, ensuring she was ok and reached out to other staff if my mom needed something addressed.
maria (admission liaison): for her empathetic approach to helping us with my mom's transfer and admission to kentfield; her timely responses to our questions and helpful information she provided in such a kind manner.
becky (speech therapy): for her gentle and patient encouragement in our mom's swallow evaluations and progress in eating and speaking.
pooja (physical therapy): for her cheerful personality and motivating instructions in our mom's physical therapy. she pushed her just enough to keep our mom's spirits up.
beverly (occupational therapy): for her positive, sweet and gentle approach. she treated our mom with so much kindness.
massood, joey, kevin, brook, rubin (respiratory therapists): for their encouragement and patience. they were constant, provided clear information and attentive.
marivel, dan, jonalyn, elena, johnny, sam, kim, marilyn, serray (cnas): some of the key people that made an extra effort in their care for our mom. their attentiveness, quick responsiveness, and very thoughtful approach was greatly appreciated by our mom and all of us.
vana, jennifer, ansley, yana, hayden, sarala (rns): very responsive, attentive to our inquiry about medication questions and questions about care. they showed kindness and patience and did not hesitate when our mom had a request.

although there are some staff that we acknowledged for their great work, we can't say the same for all staff. there were some challenges in regards to discharge planning and preparation. the staff member managing this process could improve her communication style and approach, as well as empathy and support for families who are worried about the health and recovery of their loved one.  

another area which needs improvement is the overall housekeeping of equipment and facility.  
  
thank you from the bottom of our hearts, may god bless all of you for the selfless work you do for the care of others.
